commits.subject: fix(contracts): drop nested defaults from a root union sibling (#10254)
commits.body:
fix(contracts): drop nested defaults from a root union sibling (#10254)

* fix(contracts): drop nested defaults from a root union sibling

Flattening a union of strict object groups lifts each group's properties
into one object. A default the scenario group carried inside
normalization.rules survived that lift even though the passive group
declares no normalization, so a client that fills nested defaults sent
{normalization: {rules: []}} and the runtime parser refused the call
with "Unrecognized key: normalization".

Remove defaults below a property that any group omits, not just the one
on the property itself. A property every group owns keeps its own
nested guidance.

* fix(contracts): keep a nested default a reference still targets

Dropping the nested default of a property a sibling group omits also removed defaults that references point into. A resource whose validation $ref targets its own default was advertised with that reference intact but its target gone, so the advertised schema no longer compiled in AJV or client projection.

Collect the paths into a default that references inside the branch target and keep those entries while stripping the rest. Other nested defaults are still removed, so the strict sibling group keeps refusing the object.

* test(contracts): type the root union default regression fixture

The fixture spread the canonical branch through a widened cast, so the repository typecheck rejected the spread and indexed access. Narrow the branch shape and guard the optional schema before collecting its referenced defaults.

---------

commits.subject: fix(contracts): enforce well-formed Unicode paths without advertising surrogate patterns
commits.body:
fix(contracts): enforce well-formed Unicode paths without advertising surrogate patterns

rea-agents 6.9.0 advertised `^[^\uD800-\uDFFF]*$` on every local path
input. RE2 has no `\u` escape and Rust's `regex`/`jsonschema` crates refuse
non-scalar code points, so strict MCP clients and gateways (DeepSeek, RE2
gateways, Open Design) rejected the complete tools request and no REA tool
could run.

Move the rule into one runtime check, `rejectUnpairedSurrogates`, which
advertises nothing and still raises the `invalid_format` regex issue, so
CLI and MCP corrections keep reason, expected value, and message. The
objdump disassembly symbol already enforced the same rule with its own
refinement; it now shares the owner and the correction shape.

Dropping the pattern also brings inspect_android_jni_bindings within the
compact profile's per-schema budget, so compact delivery now keeps its
DEX dimension pattern. The descriptor admission test follows the actual
presentation instead of assuming compact always omits it.

Fixes #10238
Fixes #10348
Fixes #10198

Co-Authored-By: gensokyo-dev <gensokyo-dev@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: test(ci): double test deadlines on hosted runners (#10417)
commits.body:
test(ci): double test deadlines on hosted runners (#10417)

* test(javascript): give the wide fingerprint regression a capacity deadline

Each case runs about 22 s of CPU-bound projection on a typical hosted
runner. Its explicit 30 s deadline failed on slower runners at both two
and four Vitest workers, and it also overrode the suite's 60 s
coverage-mode allowance.

* test(ci): double test deadlines on hosted runners

Hosted CI jobs run four Vitest workers on a four-core runner. CPU-bound
capacity cases then share every core with other workers and their
subprocesses; three such cases exceeded the 30 s deadline at four
workers (16.8-22.7 s at two). The deadline only needs to bound a hang,
so hosted CI doubles it: 60 s, or 120 s with coverage. Local runs keep
30 s and 60 s.

* test(ci): check worker and deadline policy for local and hosted runners

The policy test loaded vitest.config.ts in a child that inherited the
parent's GITHUB_ACTIONS, so on CI it observed the hosted deadlines and
failed. Select the runner explicitly and check both: two workers and the
base deadline locally, four workers and twice the deadline on hosted CI.

commits.subject: fix(cli): advertise the decimal token grammar on integer arguments
commits.body:
fix(cli): advertise the decimal token grammar on integer arguments

`cliIntegerArgument` piped a regex-guarded string into a number but never
published Zod's input view, so `--schema` advertised a bare integer for 15
fields while the parser accepted only decimal argv text. `environment-serve
--port` had the same gap through the transforming MCP_PORT owner.

Remove `cliIntegerArgument` and route every call site through
`cliDecimalField`, binding each field to its domain or contract owner where
one exists so bounds, defaults and optionality come from that owner. Export
the input-view publisher as `publishArgvInput` and apply it to `--port`,
which keeps the MCP_PORT grammar shared with `rea mcp --http`.

The decimal catalog test now requires every numeric field's advertisement
to admit its decimal argv token, covers repeated options and
string-advertised token grammars, and checks `--schema` output directly.

The string branch's missing numeric range (#9348) is unchanged.

Fixes #9344

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(rizin): report shell refusals instead of complete empty results
commits.body:
fix(rizin): report shell refusals instead of complete empty results

Rizin exits 0 when its shell refuses a statement, so execute_rizin_command
reported completion_status complete with exit code 0 and an empty stdout
that read as a genuine empty result.

Rizin 0.6 through 0.9.1 log exactly four refusal lines from
librz/core/cmd/cmd.c: an unknown command, a wrong argument count, an
invalid statement (RZ_CMD_STATUS_INVALID, which also stops the remaining
statements) and a parse error. The Rizin command profile now classifies a
completed process's stderr against those lines; the shared one-shot
service reports completion_status "rejected" and a limitation that names
the refusal and says stdout holds only earlier statements' output. Other
ERROR lines come from commands that ran and stay diagnostics.

Fixes #10364

Co-Authored-By: gensokyo-dev <gensokyo-dev@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(debuggers): keep stopped Rizin and GDB sessions explainable
commits.body:
fix(debuggers): keep stopped Rizin and GDB sessions explainable

After REA stopped a Rizin debug session (frame or output limit, deadline,
cancellation, protocol failure) or the debugger exited, later commands
returned a generic invalid_request and status gave no reason. GDB
collapsed the same states the same way.

Both managers now keep a published session addressable until
close_*_session releases it, record the first reason it stopped, report
it as closed_reason in session status, and refuse later commands with
capability_unavailable naming that reason and the close-then-restart
recovery. An ID the server never returned, or that close released, still
fails as invalid_request with its own recovery. Retained stopped
sessions keep their slot, which the capacity recovery now says. A GDB
command deadline now records its reason like cancellation already did.

Fixes #8024

commits.subject: perf(mcp): build advertised tool schemas once per contract (#10421)
commits.body:
perf(mcp): build advertised tool schemas once per contract (#10421)

* perf(mcp): build advertised tool schemas once per contract

The MCP SDK reprojects every registered tool schema on each tools/list.
REA memoized that projection, but per wrapper, and each server built new
wrappers for every contract, so each new server reconverted the whole
catalog: about 280 ms per tools/list for 255 tools with the full input
profile. Each wrapper also registered a new schema in zod's global
registry, so heap grew with every server.

Contracts are immutable module values, so build each advertised input
and output wrapper once per contract. tools/list on later servers drops
to about 26 ms (full profile) or 48 ms (compact).

* test(mcp): load only the contract family under test

commits.body:
test(mcp): open stdio clients through the shared local-tools fixture (#10411)

* test(mcp): open stdio clients through the shared local-tools fixture

Twelve files built their own StdioClientTransport and Client for
`rea mcp`. Those clients never listed tools, so the SDK did not
validate structured results against advertised output schemas, and each
file repeated transport setup, stderr draining and close ordering.

Use connectLocalToolsMcp, which lists tools, validates replies,
silences logging, leaves deep providers unconfigured and owns cleanup.
Per-test clients register test-scoped cleanup; module-level clients
collect cleanup for afterAll.

* test(mcp): keep failed file-scoped MCP cleanup owned

The three module-level clients removed every cleanup callback before
running them, so a failed cleanup lost its only handle. Add
fileLocalToolsMcp, which connects before the file's tests and removes
each cleanup only after it succeeds, and use it in those files.

commits.subject: test(artifacts): fit the buffered member case to Windows stream buffers
commits.body:
test(artifacts): fit the buffered member case to Windows stream buffers

The shared reader lifecycle case waits for a member's writable side to
finish before it reads anything. That only happens while the member fits
below the readable high-water mark. Node's default is 16 KiB on Windows and
64 KiB elsewhere, and the ESP flash fixture's first member is a 32 KiB
bootloader region, so both cases hung until the 30 s timeout on Windows.

Pick the first nonempty member that fits the default buffer and assert
that it fits the opened stream before waiting.

commits.subject: test(filesystem): admit the snapshot fixture as written on Windows
commits.body:
test(filesystem): admit the snapshot fixture as written on Windows

The snapshot identity test writes its file and admits it at once with the
default ChangeTime mode. On Windows that ChangeTime is inside the 2 s drift
window, so admission keeps re-reading the descriptor until it settles. The
returned baseline is then a later observation, not the one the test
captured, and the descriptor stat runs more than once.

Admit the fixture as written. That is the documented mode for a file that
was just written, and it reads the descriptor once on every host. Settling
keeps its own coverage in ChangeTimeBaseline.test.ts.

fix(decompile): derive the body-coverage caveat from retained records

decompile_all set its top-level "procedure_info is unavailable" caveat
from a per-call flag that only a newly attempted function could raise.
A resume that skipped every verified file, or selected nothing, rewrote
the manifest and decompile-index.json with an empty limitations list
while every retained record still reported an unavailable body.

The export owner now answers from the records it retains: the summary
counts every non-external record whose body is unavailable, including
records an earlier run wrote, and repeats the reason when all share one.
The per-call flag is removed. A fresh export whose procedure_info works
but leaves some bodies unavailable now reports that caveat too; a later
attempt that records a known body clears it.

commits.subject: fix(ghidra): say when an inferred no-return call cuts a function
commits.body:
fix(ghidra): say when an inferred no-return call cuts a function

Ghidra's Non-Returning Functions - Discovered analyzer can mark a
returning callee, such as an imported operator new thunk, as
non-returning. Ghidra then clears the fallthrough at each call site and
refits the callers, so a constructor decompiles to a few plausible
lines. REA reported the terminal call with the FunctionManager flag but
did not say the result omits the code after it or how to compare.

That analyzer bookmarks each entry it marks with the Analysis comment
"Non-Returning Function Found" (Ghidra 11.0 through 12.1.4 source); the
name-list Known analyzer writes "Non-Returning Function Identified".
When a terminal call's callee, or the function a thunk forwards to,
carries the Discovered bookmark, the call's limitation now says the
flag was inferred, and the function adds one address-free limitation
that its body and pseudocode end at that call and omit the following
code if the callee returns, with the REA_GHIDRA_DISABLED_ANALYZERS
comparison. A flag without the bookmark keeps an unknown origin.

The function-boundary observation contract moves to v5 so snapshots
from earlier bridges are not replayed without the qualification.

Refs #10365

commits.subject: fix(process): exonerate kernel threads from ownership token checks
commits.body:
fix(process): exonerate kernel threads from ownership token checks

An unrelated kernel thread that appeared during a provider run has no
readable /proc/<pid>/environ, so the ownership sweep recorded it as a live
candidate with an unreadable token and failed cleanup with
cleanup_incomplete. Kernel threads exit quickly, so the read usually
reports ESRCH and is not attributable to environment withholding, which
meant a cleanly finished provider run discarded its result.

Kernel threads are forked by the kernel, never by a provider, so they can
never carry that run's token. Read PF_KTHREAD from the same /proc/<pid>/stat
identity observation and treat a kernel thread with no readable token as
unverified evidence, like an unrelated process whose environment the OS
withholds. The candidate still has to be otherwise unrelated and holds no
signal authority.

commits.subject: fix(mcp-doctor): stop the owned process family on every exit path
commits.body:
fix(mcp-doctor): stop the owned process family on every exit path

runProductionMcpDoctor wrapped the SDK StdioClientTransport and only joined its
close calls. That transport clears its direct-child reference, ends stdin and
signals only that child, so a server whose launcher exited after forking an
inherited-stdio descendant left the descendant running while the doctor
reported nothing but the transport deadline.

Run the doctor on OwnedMcpStdioTransport, which spawns the child in a dedicated
POSIX process group or Windows job and verifies group and token-owned
descendant cleanup before close returns. Feed stderr through a sink on
acquisition so diagnostics survive an early child exit and still honor the
64 KiB retained prefix and full byte count.

Covered by a fixture that forks a descendant, exits, and is timed out: the
regression asserts the descendant is gone after the doctor returns.

commits.subject: fix(mcp-doctor): keep the diagnostic child target-free and its stderr visible
commits.body:
fix(mcp-doctor): keep the diagnostic child target-free and its stderr visible

The owned launcher merges its host base back under the explicit overrides, so
filtering only the override object let an ambient HOPPER_TARGET_* variable
through and the diagnostic child could open the target the doctor promises to
skip. Pass the filtered environment as the host base too, and opt into the
token sweep so a detached descendant that outlives the launcher is still
reached by cleanup.

Also keep the stderr observer attached until bounded cleanup and draining have
settled, report the typed cleanup resources instead of a generic close_binary
message, and drop a first-attempt cleanup failure once the owned retry proves
release.

commits.subject: fix(mcp-doctor): close only through the owned transport
commits.body:
fix(mcp-doctor): close only through the owned transport

The owned transport is the doctor's only cleanup owner, and Client.close
only delegates to it. Close it once and report its typed failure instead
of aggregating a duplicate SDK close and clearing that failure after a
retry. Pass the filtered caller environment as the launcher's base only,
and name the doctor operation in transport cleanup errors.

Cover a descendant in its own session, which only the token sweep can
reach, and a late cleanup denial that keeps the startup diagnostic and
reports the retained run. Bound the fixture descendant's lifetime so a
failing run cannot leak it. Document the doctor's process-family
ownership and output bound.

commits.subject: fix(setup): say when an authentic Hopper package mismatches its feed hash
commits.body:
fix(setup): say when an authentic Hopper package mismatches its feed hash

Linux Hopper setup verifies the package signature, then compares the
launcher it contains with the release feed's main_exe_hash. When only
that comparison failed, as with the Fedora 6.6.1 RPM, setup reported the
generic integrity failure and advised retrying or updating REA, which
cannot change a stale vendor feed.

The publisher now reports that case as launcher_digest_mismatch. Setup
keeps the public integrity_mismatch code and the refusal, and its
recovery says the download is authentic, the feed describes another
launcher build, and the mismatch needs a corrected feed. The two digests
stay in the detail. Every other integrity failure keeps its recovery.

Fixes #8138

commits.subject: perf(tests): run plain CLI commands on the file's shared process (#10412)
commits.body:
perf(tests): run plain CLI commands on the file's shared process (#10412)

* refactor(cli): run one-shot commands through one shared owner

scripts/rea.mjs and the test CLI session worker each implemented the
one-shot command sequence: argument normalization, output admission,
configuration errors, version documents, the Amp scope refusal, and
result delivery. The worker copy had drifted: it never rendered
formatted version reports or the Amp refusal.

Move the sequence into src/cliOneShot.ts. Both callers supply a host
for their streams, exit and resource ownership. The launcher keeps
closed-pipe status, worker shutdown and process exit; the session
worker captures output per command.

The cliOutput bundle entry is superseded and removed. The dispatcher
test now replaces only the command runtime, so output admission runs
production code. A new parity test compares the file session with a
fresh process.

* test(cli): bundle the one-shot entry in the runtime bundle fixture

* perf(tests): run plain CLI commands on the file's shared process

`cli.run` in `cliTest` files started a fresh compiled CLI for every
command, about 0.45s and 260 MB each before any work. The file-scoped
session already existed, but callers had to opt in through
`runFileCli` or `sharedCliRun`, so 1,300 call sites still spawned.

Make the fixture choose: `cli.run` uses the shared process when it
reports the command exactly as a fresh process would, and starts one
otherwise (stdin, explicit deadlines, MCP and MCP doctor routing,
NODE_OPTIONS, or enabled logging). `freshProcess: true` keeps
explicit process-level checks. The session worker now presents the
launcher's entrypoint, so registration identity matches a fresh
process.

`runFileCli` and `sharedCliRun` are superseded and removed; their
call sites use `cli.run`, and paired fresh/shared checks use
`freshProcess`.

* style(tests): format the managed member summary call site

* test(cli): give each shared-session command an empty stdin

The shared CLI process reads session frames from its own stdin. A
command that reads stdin without supplied input, such as
`compare-wasm-interfaces - --json`, read that pipe and hung, where a
fresh process receives EOF. The worker now presents an ended, empty
stdin to each command and restores its own afterwards.

The parity test compared the routed path with itself after cli.run
began choosing the session. It now compares a fresh process with the
session directly, including the `mcp add` refusal and a command
reading absent stdin.

* test(cli): keep default command logging and launcher checks on fresh processes

environment-serve and environment-build log at info when REA_LOG_LEVEL is
unset, through a logger that writes to stderr directly. The shared CLI
process captures only process.stderr writes, so routed runs lost those
lines. Declare the default-logging commands beside the command names,
have infoLogger read that set, and start a fresh process for them.

The log-level precedence checks compared the shared process with itself
after routing; their fresh side now passes freshProcess: true.

commits.subject: fix(process)!: retain observed cleanup intervention (#10481)
commits.body:
fix(process)!: retain observed cleanup intervention (#10481)

* fix(process)!: retain observed cleanup intervention

Process capture derived `settlement.cleanup_outcome` from the settlement
state alone in three places, so a quiesced capture reported
`not_required` even after final owned-process cleanup SIGKILLed a live
token-owned descendant. `cleanupOwnedProcessGroup` already knew it had
signaled, but the capture lifecycle discarded that fact.

Carry the observed signal out of ownership cleanup (also on failure
paths), accumulate it across cleanup retries as true/false/unknown, and
derive settlement and the intervention residual unknown once in
`processCaptureCleanupFacts` for full, partial and harness results.

BREAKING CHANGE: a quiesced settlement may now report
`cleanup_outcome: "cleaned"`. Saved captures stay valid; readers that
accepted only `not_required` for quiesced settlements must accept
`cleaned`.

Fixes #8032

Squashed from #8043 and rebased onto main (adapted to the resource-scope
release API and the inspection-failure cleanup path).

Co-Authored-By: gensokyo-dev <gensokyo-dev@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(process): keep a sent signal when cleanup throws an inspection failure

Final ownership verification can rethrow a typed inspection failure (for
example cancellation) after SIGKILL succeeded. The capture owner then
recorded the attempt as unknown and dropped the intervention fact.

cleanupOwnedProcessGroup now marks a failure it throws after signaling,
without changing the failure's identity, and the capture owner keeps
the signal for such failures.

commits.subject: fix(ghidra): prevent loader relocations from constant folding (#10483)
commits.body:
fix(ghidra): prevent loader relocations from constant folding (#10483)

* fix(ghidra): prevent loader relocations from constant folding

Ghidra imports loader relocation destinations with their file bytes. A
destination in a non-writable loaded block can be populated by the
runtime loader instead, for example a copy-relocated musl `stderr` in
RELRO, so the decompiler folded the on-disk zero and showed
`fprintf(NULL, ...)`.

Before initializing the decompiler, mark each loaded, initialized,
non-writable block containing a relocation destination volatile in the
ephemeral database, and add a limitation to procedures that read such a
destination. ELF shared objects and PIEs are included; relocatable
objects and core files are not. Permissions and source FileBytes are
unchanged.

Sessions without database-mutation authority (Windows P0 and existing
caller projects) record the limitation but do not mark blocks volatile,
and the analysis profile versions the two behaviors separately.

A real Linux Ghidra ELF probe runs in the Ghidra bridge CI lane.

Fixes #4177

Squashed from #4198 and rebased onto main. Rebase adaptations: the
read-only gate, the verifier renamed to verify-ghidra-loader-relocation
so it stays out of the manual-verifier glob, docs moved to
docs/testing-lanes.md and docs/providers/ghidra-provider.md.

Co-Authored-By: gensokyo-dev <gensokyo-dev@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ghidra): await installation inspection in the relocation verifier

inspectGhidraInstallation became async on main after #4198's base, so the
verifier asserted on a pending Promise. Also wait for provider output to
close before reading it, like the sibling Ghidra verifiers, and keep the
workflow reference inside the docs site.

Co-Authored-By: gensokyo-dev <gensokyo-dev@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ghidra): address relocation review findings

- Version the existing-project analysis profile with the read-only
  relocation semantics, since those sessions now add the limitation.
- Inspect the installation through the verifier helper that owns the
  file-reader resources.
- Build the fixture with -fPIC: with -fPIE, GCC 12 emits a copy
  relocation of rea_external_value into writable .bss, so the probe's
  GOT check could not hold.
- Run probe cleanup through withVerifierCleanup so a cleanup failure
  does not hide the probe failure, and keep the workspace when owned
  Ghidra cleanup is incomplete.
- Link the workflow with a full GitHub URL, per the docs guide.

Co-Authored-By: gensokyo-dev <gensokyo-dev@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(ghidra): reach the external data through the GOT with a weak extern

Building the whole fixture with -fPIC also turned the reader's direct
load of rea_loader_pointer into a GOT-relaxed lea plus two loads, and
the real-Ghidra lane then reported that the baseline no longer folds
the file constant. Keep -fPIE and declare only rea_external_value weak:
GCC and clang must reach a possibly absent symbol through a GOT entry,
which lands as R_X86_64_GLOB_DAT inside GNU_RELRO (checked with readelf
for GCC 12.2 and clang/lld).

Co-Authored-By: gensokyo-dev <gensokyo-dev@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ghidra): protect only relocations Ghidra could not apply

Running the real-Ghidra lane locally (Ghidra 12.1.4, JDK 21, GCC 12)
showed that marking every non-writable block that holds a relocation
volatile also marks full-RELRO .got. External calls then decompile as
opaque pointer calls (`(*pcVar2)(param_1)` through
`PTR_rea_external_...` instead of `rea_external(param_1)`), which the
probe's GOT-stability check caught.

Ghidra applies GLOB_DAT and RELATIVE relocations, so those bytes already
hold the loader's value and folding them is correct. The #4177 case is
a copy relocation, which Ghidra imports as UNSUPPORTED with the file's
zero in place. Protect only destinations whose relocation status is not
APPLIED or APPLIED_OTHER.

The fixture now reads a provider `const` object that the linker copies
into .data.rel.ro, the #4177 shape. The probe requires that relocation
to be unapplied and requires applied GOT relocations to stay
non-volatile. Ghidra 12.1.4 already shows this x86-64 read by name
without protection, so the probe records whether the baseline folds and
compares before and after only when it does. The profile value becomes
volatile-unapplied-relocation-blocks-v1.

commits.subject: fix(verifiers): release fixture roots only after their owners finish (#10491)
commits.body:
fix(verifiers): release fixture roots only after their owners finish (#10491)

* fix(verifiers): release fixture roots only after their owners finish

Several real-tool verifiers released a fixture root even when a cleanup
that still used it had failed, so a surviving MCP server, session or
descendant kept running against a deleted directory and the failure
looked like ordinary cleanup.

- scripts/lib/verifier-cleanup.mjs: new releaseAfter(dependents,
  release, retained) task. It attempts every dependent cleanup and
  releases the resource only if all succeed; otherwise it keeps the
  resource and reports it with the dependent failures.
- verify-signal-recording: the root is released after the MCP client

commits.subject: refactor: prune internal seams and preserve configuration ownership (#10430)
commits.body:
refactor: prune internal seams and preserve configuration ownership (#10430)

* refactor: prune internal seams and preserve configuration ownership

* fix(setup): keep YAML aliases and inherited registration settings on refresh

- Reuse an unchanged YAML collection only while every alias in it still
  resolves after the edit; otherwise rebuild it so the alias becomes its
  value. A sibling anchor replaced or moved in the same refresh no longer
  leaves an unresolved alias in Hermes or Goose output.
- Keep a connection selector whose existing value already chooses stdio
  (for example an inherited Hermes transport: stdio) instead of superseding
  it; remote selectors are still replaced. Explicit stdio selectors are
  therefore no longer rewritten (Kimi expectation updated).
- When the whole Hermes registration is inherited through a merge,
  override it with that merge and write only the changed fields.

* fix(setup): edit registration fields whose YAML key is an alias

A key written as an alias to a string scalar (for example *field with
field: &field env) was treated as a source-only key, so any change to
its value was refused in Hermes and Goose. Resolve such keys to their
string, keep the aliased spelling while its anchor survives the edit,
and write the plain key when the same edit rebuilds the anchor.

* test(process): bound cleanup-boundary waits and always release gates

Both cancellation tests awaited a bare started promise and released
their gates only on success, so a missed boundary waited for the outer
deadline and could leave cleanup parked. Use awaitAcknowledgement and
release and join the cleanup in finally.

* fix(setup): repair only aliases an edit leaves unresolved

Replace the pre-edit alias survival guess, which expanded aliases to
sibling anchors that survive unchanged, with an exact repair: record
what each alias in the replaced value resolves to, write the edit, then
replace only aliases left without a preceding anchor by that value.

- Keep an aliased key's source position, so its anchor stays ahead of
  later aliases.
- Treat an aliased key as its string only when no other key in the map
  resolves to the same string; an ambiguous one stays guarded.
- Override an inherited Hermes registration only when the requested
  entry keeps every inherited field, so an explicit replacement can drop
  remote selectors.

* fix(setup): repair aliases whose binding an edit changes, keeping comments

An alias whose own anchor was removed could resolve to an earlier anchor
with the same name and silently change value. Record the node each alias
resolved to and repair any alias that no longer resolves to that node.
Carry the alias's comments and spacing onto the repaired value.

* test(setup): split the Hermes anchor and merge refresh cases

* fix(setup): refuse removing an overridden key its merge would restore

The merge-retention check skipped keys the mapping also overrides, so
dropping such a key (for example a remote url during an explicit stdio
replacement) let the retained merge restore it. Check removal before
skipping overridden keys, so the edit is refused with the existing
message instead of producing a registration that cannot be applied.

Comparing retained scenario captures flattened each side's unique step

the same id arriving uniquely on the other side then landed in
before_only/after_only and produced a missing_before_step or
missing_after_step failure for a step the duplicate side still retains.

the same id, a stronger claim than the ambiguity supports.

Alignment now keeps a duplicated id out of the absence lists on both
sides: the id stays unaligned with its duplicate failure, but no capture
is described as missing a step it retains. Genuinely missing ids keep
their missing_* classification and absence lists.

commits.subject: fix(cli): exit one-shot commands by draining the event loop
commits.body:
fix(cli): exit one-shot commands by draining the event loop

process.exit() shuts Node's platform down without tearing the V8
isolate down. When a concurrent Maglev or baseline compile job is
waiting for a collection at that moment, the main thread blocks forever
in NodePlatform::Shutdown joining it (captured with gdb on Node
24.22.1). A one-shot command that called Incur's exit then never
terminated: about 1 in 20 such exits after the lazy CLI loading change,
and rarely on main.

The exit callback now sets process.exitCode and lets the event loop
drain, so Node tears the isolate down in order. A handle that outlives a
one-second grace still gets the forced exit with the same status.

Co-Authored-By: gensokyo-dev <342580529+gensokyo-dev@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.subject: test: let the deadline policy own test waits
commits.body:
test: let the deadline policy own test waits

Vitest's expect.poll and vi.waitFor stop after one second by default, a
host-speed guess that the project's deadline policy does not see. Under
hosted-CI load, kunaProjectConcurrency failed that way twice on unrelated
PRs. Another 256 waits relied on the default, and 97 passed literals
picked to fit some host.

Waits now take as long as their test may run, less the reporting reserve
that children already keep. Each Vitest project sets expect.poll's
default, and the new waitFor in tests/support/testWait.ts replaces
vi.waitFor. Fixture readiness waits (awaitAcknowledgement and the provider
process waits) default to the same deadline, and their host-speed literal
arguments are removed. One remainingTestDeadline owns the arithmetic for
both children and waits.

Ten waits whose short timeout was the real check now assert it directly
(Kuna version probe, Cutter discovery, doctor and Inspector cancellation,
apktool fixture teardown, JADX disconnect): settlement before the
production deadline that would otherwise also satisfy the wait, or a
deadline pinned beyond every test deadline.

The rea/project-wait-deadline lint rule rejects vi.waitFor and explicit
expect.poll timeouts. The testing guide and the CI tests audit skill now
document the policy.

commits.subject: perf(cli): load only the registrar a one-shot command needs
commits.body:
perf(cli): load only the registrar a one-shot command needs

Every rea process imported and registered all 52 command registrars
(about 1,900 modules) before running any command. A one-shot command
now loads only the registrar that defines its top-level command.

- src/cli/cliCommandRegistrations.ts holds every registrar in one table,
  grouped by tool family, with its module loader and its call. The
  complete createCli registers the table with static imports, and the
  types check that each entry matches its module.
- src/cli/cliShell.ts owns what does not depend on which commands are
  registered: identity, globals, argument policy, completions and the
  registration builtins. The full and lazy paths share it.
- scripts/record-cli-commands.mjs records, after tsc, which registrar
  defines each top-level command, from the same compiled table. The
  bundle keeps the record as an external dist module.
- cli/cliLoader.ts selects the recorded registrar when a known top-level
  command runs. It loads the complete CLI for help, --schema, --llms,
  completions, builtins, unknown names ("did you mean"), or a missing
  record.
- Process-owned CLI resources register their closers when their module
  loads (cli/cliResources.ts), so the shell no longer imports
  JavaScript-analysis and guidance owners just to close them.

Measured on one pinned core (median of 5 warm runs, base main vs this
change):

commits.subject: fix(hopper): name the unconfirmed shutdown step in retained cleanup (#10594)
commits.body:
fix(hopper): name the unconfirmed shutdown step in retained cleanup (#10594)

* fix(hopper): name the unconfirmed shutdown step in retained cleanup

When close_binary retains a Hopper document, the cleanup error lists the
retained resources but not why shutdown went unconfirmed. On Linux CI,
hopperClient.handshakeRecovery "recovers an application exit after the
first valid handshake occurs during cleanup" fails intermittently. The
vitest blob reports show only hopper-document and the runtime root
retained with authenticated_application "readable". From those facts we
cannot tell whether the shutdown request was not sent, failed, or was
sent while the application was still observed as present.

provider state, or why it was not sent) and the final exit observation
of the authenticated application in the retained-document diagnostics.
Exit observation now reports a positively observed Linux exit in
progress (PF_EXITING before state Z) as "exiting", separate from
"present". Neither confirms exit. The flaky test asserts the projected
error, so a later failure prints these diagnostics in the CI log.

commits.body:
refactor(cli): derive contract-backed command options from the tool contract (#10571)

* refactor(cli): derive contract-backed command options from the tool contract

Each contract-backed CLI command restated its contract's input fields as
hand-written incur options and mapped them back to snake_case input with
conditional spreads. Nothing checked that the two schemas agreed.

Add registerContractCommand: a per-command projection names only what the
CLI spells differently (positionals, caller-relative path fields, option
renames, CLI help wording, omitted optional fields with a reason). Option
schemas, decimal argv tokens and the contract's cross-field rules are
derived from the contract input schema, and parsed options map back to the
contract input mechanically.

Migrate inspect-sqlite-database and the thirteen flat binary-diagnostics
inspectors. Their --schema output is unchanged apart from property order,
and help lists options in contract order. Delete the SQLite superRefine that
mirrored the contract and the per-command spreads.

Add a parity test: every projected command exposes each contract field or
declares its omission, and each field admits exactly what the contract
admits for empty, NUL, relative-path, bound and numeric-spelling probes.

* refactor(cli): refuse unprojected contract input forms at registration

Address review findings on the contract projection:

- Bind inspect-sqlite-database to its contract by name instead of catalog
  position.
- Accept only field forms argv can carry (string, number, boolean, enum,
  and arrays of strings or enums) instead of rejecting a short list, so
  arrays of objects, tuples and other forms fail at registration.
- Refuse root input keywords other than the projected object constraints
  and presentation annotations, so a contract rule such as `not` cannot
  disappear from --schema.

* refactor(cli): describe contract commands independently of the CLI framework

Split the contract projection into a framework-neutral description and a
thin Incur adapter, so a later REA-owned CLI layer (#10583) can render the
same description.

- contractCliDescription.ts derives each positional and option from the
  contract and projection: key and short flag, help, argv admission
  schema, boolean-flag/repeatable/decimal/caller-path facts, object
  constraints renamed to CLI keys, the optional argv-time cross-field
  check, and the mapping back to contract input.
- contractCommand.ts only renders that description as Incur args and
  options and runs the handler.

Cross-field rules now refuse at argv parsing only when a projection asks
(inspect-sqlite-database does, keeping its behavior); otherwise the
service's contract parse refuses them as before. Exact-optional fields are
projected as optional because argv cannot carry an explicit undefined and
Incur's help reads flag and choice types only through optional.

The parity guard reads the descriptions, and also checks that boolean
fields parse as bare flags and that no projected field stays
exact-optional.

commits.body:
fix(parsers): stop reading every RangeError as a format failure (#10602)

* refactor(parsers): report format failures through one ParseFailure algebra

Add ParseFailure (malformed, truncated, unsupported, limit, with format,
offset and field) and its one carrier, ParseFailureError, in the domain.
BinaryReader now names truncation and the field it read, and its native
format and resource failures are ParseFailureError subclasses.

Providers projected a format failure with their own instanceof ladder,
and some dropped the selected path from the invalid_format message.
parseFailureAnalysisError now owns that projection for the native,
Go, devicetree, V8, Windows Shortcut and Electron fuse providers.
The V8 code cache, Windows Shortcut and Electron fuse format classes
are removed in favour of the algebra.

The architecture guard counts raw Buffer and DataView reads, plain
Error throws in parser folders and plain JSON.parse of parser input
against baselines that can only shrink.

* fix(parsers): stop reading every RangeError as a format failure

Mach-O, Swift and Objective-C metadata parsers threw RangeError for a
truncated or malformed record, so their catch sites treated any
RangeError as a partial decode: a call stack overflow or a host string
limit became an "unresolved" metadata reason, and the IL2CPP Mach-O
path reported it as a malformed container.

Those parsers and the CIL method body reader now throw ParseFailureError.
hostRangeErrorKind is the one interpreter of a host RangeError (stack
overflow, host capacity, raw out-of-bounds read), and
parseFailureFromCause admits only a parse failure or a raw
out-of-bounds read as evidence about the input. Fixup stream catch-alls
rethrow host limits. The architecture guard counts the remaining direct
instanceof RangeError checks.

The capture path parsed TShark's selected-field JSON without the expansion
estimate the pcap reader charges. It now reads through readTsharkJsonPackets
under capture.packet_json_expansion_bytes (REA_CAPTURE_PACKET_JSON_EXPANSION_BYTES).

Node string, so no admissible output reaches 69,793,215,440 bytes; the default
and maximum are 128 GiB, so the budget refuses only when lowered. A refusal is
an adjustable_budget resource constraint naming the setting and keeps the
producer output; a malformed launch seed is refused before the capture is read.

packet_limit is passed to TShark's -c as a C int packet count, not a timer delay, so it keeps its own named bound and a documented exception in the signed 32-bit guard.

* feat(ida)!: require an explicit protocol for attached IDA registrations

An attached registration (the default mode) silently selected the legacy

with a configuration error naming the choice. Add `"protocol": "legacy"` to
an ida-pro-mcp 1.4 proxy registration (or `"protocol": "native"` for the
ida-free-mcp plugin). Headless registrations are unchanged.

The setup budget fixture still wrote an attached URL registration without a
protocol, and the IDA registration rejection fixtures relied on the missing
protocol as one of several failures. Each now names its protocol, so setup
reaches its timeout checks and every rejection case fails only for its own
constraint.

commits.subject: fix(test): run the Hopper launch-failure CLI case in fresh processes on macOS CI (#10825)
commits.body:
fix(test): run the Hopper launch-failure CLI case in fresh processes on macOS CI (#10825)

The case checks that a one-shot CLI exits after a retained-cleanup
failure and that the operating system then releases the Hopper target
lease to a retry. Since #10412, `cli.run` serves plain commands on the
file's shared CLI process. That process keeps the lease, as the
cleanup-ownership rules require while cleanup is incomplete, and never
exits between commands, so the retry was refused as "already open" and
the final lease check failed on macOS.

Run both attempts with `freshProcess: true`, which the fixture provides
for process-exit facts. The case is macOS-only because target leases
are taken only on the macOS launcher route, and no CI lane ran it, so
add it to the Apple lane and its change scope.

commits.subject: refactor(gdb): parse MI result records with one typed record parser (#10799)
commits.body:
refactor(gdb): parse MI result records with one typed record parser (#10799)

* refactor(gdb): parse MI result records with one typed record parser

GdbSessionManager recognized ^done with a prefix regex at seven sites, kept a hand-written span scanner and a second character scanner for -list-thread-groups, and decoded C-string fields with a dynamic RegExp. src/gdb/GdbMiRecord.ts now parses a result record into its token, class and typed results (C-string bytes, tuples, value lists and result lists), and returns a typed malformed-mi-record failure with a reason and offset. The done checks, the thread-group PID inventory and the C-string field reader use it; the stream dispatcher reads only the record header through the same module. An architecture guard keeps MI result-record regexes in the owner.

* perf(gdb): encode each unescaped C-string run once

The MI C-string decoder allocated a Buffer per unescaped character, pushed every byte into a number array, and copied the rest of the line for each hex or octal escape. It now validates unescaped runs in place, encodes each run once, reads escapes with sticky patterns, and joins the chunks once. On a 12.1 MiB groups reply: 887/832 ms elapsed and 818/775 ms CPU before, 76/76 ms elapsed and 131/128 ms CPU after; peak RSS 152-170 MiB both.

* test(gdb): refuse a malformed ^done for a startup setting through a real session

A fake GDB answers -gdb-set auto-load off with ^done,msg="unterminated. The session must not start: the typed MI record parser refuses the record, where main's ^done prefix match accepted it (the case fails against main's GdbSessionManager).

* feat(gdb): record the GDB version from -gdb-version in session Evidence (#10865)

* feat(gdb): record the GDB version from -gdb-version in session Evidence

Startup now asks -gdb-version before the auto-load setting and reads its first console stream record through a new MI stream-record parser (parseGdbMiStreamRecord). Each session's Evidence names that version; an unrecognised banner, malformed record or refused query leaves it null (unknown), as before.

Fake GDB fixtures answer -gdb-version from one owner in gdbTestHelpers: a stdin preamble for scripted fakes and answerFakeGdbStartup for in-process fakes, so scenarios model only their own commands.

* fix(gdb): leave a lossily decoded version unknown and frame fake startup replies by line

* test(gdb): reject unmodeled commands in the lossy version banner fixture

* test(gdb): refuse commands the scripted fake GDBs do not model (#10947)

* test(gdb): refuse commands the scripted fake GDBs do not model

* test(gdb): match the migrated fakes' special commands exactly

AnalysisError.cleanupIncomplete becomes a getter over the error's own unresolved state and its bound dependencies. The WeakRef dependents graph and resolveCleanup's push propagation are removed, and subclasses mark their initial state through markCleanupIncomplete instead of overriding a public mutable field.

A composite whose dependencies had released but whose status was never read

AnalysisCleanupLeaseGroup no longer calls resolveCleanup() on its error.
The error holds the group as a release claim and reads cleanupReleased when

OwnedWorkerRuntime's root epoch is now an AnalysisCleanupReleaseClaim. Errors bound to it read its release when asked instead of the epoch pushing resolveCleanup() through weak references, and a runtime without a retained root binds an already-released owner. Removes the OwnedWorkerCleanupFailure structural type and four resolveCleanup() pushes; the counted baseline shrinks accordingly.

Retained pcap commands, retained snapshot failures and snapshot completion descriptors now own their release and errors read it: commands and snapshot failures implement AnalysisCleanupReleaseClaim, and a failed completion-descriptor close is retried through an AnalysisCleanupLease bound to its error. Cline VS Code extension, Kiro, Mastra Code, Zed and Amp move from

runner launcher, then check that doctor reports it stale, update selects

current launcher.

* fix(setup): register Amp in settings.jsonc when that is its settings file (#10717)

Amp reads ~/.config/amp/settings.json or settings.jsonc. REA always
used settings.json, creating a second file beside an existing
settings.jsonc. Use settings.jsonc when it is the only file, and refuse
when both exist because Amp does not document which one it reads.

The Cline extension keeps its MCP settings in the global storage of

client-table row per editor, resolved through the shared Code-OSS user
data rule, and detected where that editor's Cline settings exist.

Address review: VSCODE_PORTABLE moves only VS Code's own storage, so the other editors keep their settings path; and the older-release note now says which hosts mcp add could register before.

commits.subject: feat(evidence)!: give Evidence bundles a format revision owned by one module (#10861)
commits.body:
feat(evidence)!: give Evidence bundles a format revision owned by one module (#10861)

* feat(evidence)!: give Evidence bundles a format revision owned by one module

`src/domain/evidenceFormat.ts` owns Evidence format evolution. Bundles now
carry `evidence_format: 1`; every bundle reader admits only the current
revision and refuses an unmarked or other-revision bundle once, with the
single recreate-observations guidance, instead of admitting earlier shapes
one optional field at a time.

The 6.7-era artifact inventory summary identities are no longer rebuilt:
compare_artifacts checks the current projection only and reports a mismatch
with the owner's guidance. The pre-6.6 identity diagnosis uses the same
guidance. SQLite `worker_timeout_ms` and Dart AOT `string_pool.policy`,
optional only for historical Evidence, are now required.

BREAKING CHANGE: Evidence bundles written by REA 6.x (no `evidence_format`)
are refused by import, comparison, reconstruction and analysis-snapshot
readers as an integrity mismatch telling the caller to recreate the
observations; re-exporting an earlier bundle does not update its format or
identities. Bundles constructed by hand must include `"evidence_format": 1`.
6.7-era artifact summaries are refused by compare_artifacts, and SQLite and
Dart AOT Evidence without the newly required fields fails validation.

* fix(evidence): let the ledger application admit its bundle's format

build_reconstruction_obligation_ledger registered the full bundle schema with the SDK, so an unmarked or other-revision bundle was refused as invalid_request before the format owner ran. Register it like coverage: the application parses the request envelope and admits the bundle.

* feat(pcap)!: read capture Evidence through the current result schema only (#10879)

Delete the pcap read-compatibility schema that defaulted executable identity for historical capture Evidence, and require query_labels_hex (null when unknown) now that every producer writes it. Evidence from an earlier format is refused at the bundle format owner; a record that omits these fields is reported as malformed instead of defaulted.

BREAKING CHANGE: inspect_pcap_capture results always carry query_labels_hex, and analysis views no longer default missing tshark/capinfos identity fields.

* feat(desktop)!: require the effective view policy in desktop state Evidence (#10886)

inspect_desktop_application_state always records the complete policy it used, including sqlite_view_bytes. Drop the optional historical shape and the task draft's absent-policy branch.

BREAKING CHANGE: desktop application state results without effective_view_policy, or with a policy missing sqlite_view_bytes, are refused as malformed.

* feat(android)!: require component declaration facets and reference aggregates in Android Evidence (#10904)

* feat(android)!: require component declaration facets and reference aggregates in Android Evidence

The JADX producers always write the manifest component projection with every declaration facet, target_definition and direct_invokes_coverage. Require them, delete the duplicate observed component schema, drop the unknown declaration coverage that only described historical omission, and give manifest view results their explicit facet.

BREAKING CHANGE: Android package, component and reference results missing these fields are refused as malformed; component declaration_coverage and its summary counts no longer include unknown; manifest view results always carry facet manifest.

* refactor(android): parse package results with the domain schema directly

* feat(browser)!: require the DOM length unit and redirect-scoped prior-hop facts (#10897)

* feat(browser)!: require the DOM length unit and redirect-scoped prior-hop facts

Both CDP producers always declare node_value_length_unit, and the observation session writes redirect_response on every redirect event and no other. Require the unit, drop the diff's absent-unit branch, and admit redirect_response exactly on redirect rows.

BREAKING CHANGE: DOM snapshots without node_value_length_unit and redirect timeline rows without redirect_response are refused as malformed, including inline inspections passed to compare_web_captures.

* docs(browser): drop the historical redirect_response omission note

* feat(native)!: require native Evidence fields that were optional only for historical Evidence (#10946)

Mach-O encryption, slice malformed cause, symbol runtime names and import
facts; ELF export encoding facts and visibility; value-flow limits; load-image
permissions and relocation symbols; Swift type-reference kind and GPU AMD
target metadata are required. Legacy enum values (unrecorded, unknown
visibility, undecodable, modinfo_field_exceeds_limit) and the retained
schemas, view defaults and reinterpretations that served historical Evidence
are deleted.

BREAKING CHANGE: native records missing these fields are refused as
malformed; recreate the observation.

refactor(wasm): leave WABT cancellation to the shared owners (#10796)

* fix(pcap): report a refused tool launch as an unavailable tool

When a capture read's tool launch was refused with EPERM, pcap reported it
as unreadable tool output (AnalysisProtocolError) instead of an unavailable
tool. Pcap also never told "not executable" apart from "missing".

Add classifyLaunchFailure in src/process as the one owner of which spawn
errnos mean missing (ENOENT, ENOTDIR) and which mean present but not
executable (EACCES, EPERM, ENOEXEC, EISDIR). Pcap, apktool and gdb used three
different errno lists; all three now use it.

* refactor(process): classify owned command outcomes through one owner

Add ProviderOutcome, read once from the supervisor's facts, and classifyProviderOutcome, the one mapping from an outcome to a typed error. Migrate pcap and the shared artifact producer command failure (TShark, sigrok). Add the rea/provider-failure-classifier lint rule with a shrink-only baseline of per-site (cause: unknown) => AnalysisError functions.

* refactor(process): classify Java and adb launch refusals with the shared owner (#10598)

The Ghidra and JADX Java probes and adb's version probe now take
missing-versus-not-executable from classifyLaunchFailure instead of their
own errno checks. ELOOP and ENAMETOOLONG join the owner's missing set, so
adb keeps its existing classification and both Java probes now treat a
non-directory path component as a missing runtime.

* fix(pcap): preserve command launch attribution

* test(pcap): expect an unknown failing stage when a limited capture tool exits unsuccessfully

* refactor(process): classify owned command outcomes through one owner

Add ProviderOutcome, read once from the supervisor's facts, and classifyProviderOutcome, the one mapping from an outcome to a typed error. Migrate pcap and the shared artifact producer command failure (TShark, sigrok). Add the rea/provider-failure-classifier lint rule with a shrink-only baseline of per-site (cause: unknown) => AnalysisError functions.

* test(lint): cover baselined files in the provider-failure classifier rule

* fix(apktool): report the decoder JVM's heap exhaustion as memory, not a target refusal

The supervisor now watches for a managed runtime's out-of-memory report while output streams (JVM java.lang.OutOfMemoryError, V8 'JavaScript heap out of memory'), so a retention budget cannot hide it. ProviderOutcome gains a runtime-exhausted kind and classifyProviderOutcome maps it once. Apktool decode opts in and moves to the shared classifier; Ghidra's single-purpose output token becomes the JVM runtime option and its area matching reuses the shared table.

* fix(process): keep the runtime's out-of-memory report on the memory error it supports

* fix(pcap): attribute a limited capture's exit through the prlimit wrapper

* fix(process): keep a shortened out-of-memory line marked as shortened

* fix(process): identify the refused executable for every launcher shape

Name the executable on errnos Node throws synchronously from spawn
(ENOEXEC, ENOTDIR, ...) and read the Windows native launcher's
executable-launch constraint, so pcap attributes those refusals to the
selected tool or limiter instead of an unknown stage.

* test(pcap): prove synchronous launch naming with ENOTDIR on every POSIX host

* fix(apktool): advise the JVM limit that governs the reported memory area

* fix(ghidra): read the supervisor's parsed OOM area instead of reparsing lines

* fix(sqlite,capture): read V8 heap exhaustion from streamed output, not retained stderr (#10724)

The SQLite worker and the Node capture decoders now declare runtime: "v8", so the supervisor observes V8's heap report as output streams. Both classifiers read the runtime-exhausted outcome instead of matching retained stderr, so a report beyond the retention budget, or one whose process then overflowed its output budget, is still reported as memory exhaustion.

* refactor(evm): classify EVMole worker outcomes through the shared provider classifier (#10716)

* refactor(evm): classify EVMole worker outcomes through the shared provider classifier

The EVMole worker's cancellation, deadline, output budget and CPU/file-size signals now go through classifyProviderOutcome; only the prlimit launch refusal and the reserved EFBIG exit remain in its dialect. The worker is opted into V8 exhaustion scanning so a heap report names its fixed 256 MiB heap. providerOutcomeOf now reads a launch refusal only from a spawn errno, so a private-storage or carrier read errno is no longer reported as a limiter launch failure.

* fix(evm): keep a stream failure's exit status and update Linux worker expectations

* refactor(process): read launch refusals through the launcher identity owner

* refactor(wasm): classify WABT command outcomes through the shared provider classifier (#10727)

* refactor(wasm): classify WABT command outcomes through the shared provider classifier

WABT's cancellation, command deadline, output budget, and inherited-limit signals now go through classifyProviderOutcome; its dialect keeps only the configuration-probe and launch-refusal unavailability and the unclassified-exit output error. A tool ended by SIGXCPU/SIGXFSZ or the memory limit is now a resource constraint instead of an output error, and a refused launch in the producer phase is reported as unavailable. The shared timeout context gains the analysis setting that selected the deadline, and the output-limit context may name its exceeded budget.

* fix(wasm): keep setup guidance when a WABT version probe's output cannot be collected

* refactor(providers): classify raw provider failures through one owner

* refactor(process): build classified cancellations with cancelledBy and the carried caller reason

* chore(lint): count runOwned's close-failure mapper from main in the classifier baseline

* fix(process): carry the runtime's exhaustion report on every memory error that claims it

SQLite and historical-capture memory errors recognised a streamed V8 heap report but dropped it, so a report outside retained output reached callers without its source line or omission flags. One projection, runtimeExhaustionReport, now owns that shape for the shared classifier and both consumers. Also lowers the EVMole and WABT cancellation-constructor baselines.

* fix(process): keep the provider's recovery for a native-thread exhaustion report

The shared classifier replaced the provider-supplied recovery with generic capacity advice whenever the JVM reported it could not create a native thread, dropping Apktool's launcher guidance and flipping retryable to true. The provider's recovery now wins; the capacity advice remains the fallback for providers that supply none.

* refactor(pwntools): classify pwntools failures through the shared provider classifier (#10782)

* refactor(pwntools): classify pwntools failures through the shared provider classifier

pwntools' per-site classifier is replaced by pwntoolsFailureDialect for classifyProviderFailure. Command outcomes go through classifyProviderOutcome, launch refusals through launcherRefusalOf instead of a 'spawn ' syscall prefix check, the input limit through the file dialect's fileSize, and the cleanup report through commandCleanup. The shared read cancellation now carries the reader's partial observation, and resource-signal reports accept provider detail.

* fix(pwntools): report a failed command's output once and expect resource_constraint for overflow

The shared outcome owner already attaches the command's output as capturedOutput, so the pwntools adapter fallback no longer copies the same text into diagnostics.stdout, diagnostics.stderr and diagnostics.captured_output; diagnostics keep the exit facts. Update the overflow expectations the dialect migration missed (layout provider cleanup and over-budget rows, pwntools cleanup) to resource_constraint.

* refactor(wasm): leave WABT cancellation to the shared owners

WabtFailures matched any Error named AbortError as a cancellation. No WABT path produces one: reads, path checks and owned commands report cancellation as ArtifactReaderFailure or OwnedCommandFailure, which classifyProviderFailure and classifyProviderOutcome already classify with the caller's reason. The provider's two signal checks now build the cancellation with cancelledBy. Lowers the AnalysisCancelledError constructor baseline for both WABT files to zero.

* fix(wasm): report a cancelled snapshot write as the caller's cancellation

The private snapshot write passed the caller's signal to Node's writeFile, whose abort envelope reached the dialect's unclassified output failure once the name-based AbortError guess was removed. The write now turns the envelope carrying its own signal's reason into cancelledBy at the producer.

* refactor(firmware): classify firmware failures through the shared provider classifier (#10810)

Firmware producers now report their own deadline expiry: the start check, the output inventory and launcher admission throw the phase timeout where they observe the abort, and a read the phase signal cancelled reports it through the dialect's interruption. The classifier no longer rereads a cancellation's reason as a timeout. A new readCleanup hook keeps firmware's cleanup report shape.

commits.body:
fix(filesystem): close file handles only through the owned-handle owners (#10578)

* fix(filesystem): close file handles only through the owned-handle owners

Three sites still closed a fs/promises FileHandle in a finally block, where a
failed close replaced the operation's own failure or result: the agentenv
runner head read, the Linux cgroup kernel-file read and the JavaScript
analysis transfer writer. They now use withOwnedFileHandle, which retains the
operation outcome alongside a failed close.

A lint rule, rea/no-raw-file-handle-close, refuses close() on a handle opened
from fs/promises or declared as FileHandle, and fs close/closeSync on a
descriptor, in src outside src/filesystem/Owned*.

* fix(lint): distinguish owned handle class fields

* fix(filesystem): retain diagnostic file cleanup owners

* test(hopper): retry after confirmed application exit

* fix(filesystem): settle doctor peers, sample cgroup outside admission, and bind lint this

Desktop doctor waits for every client inspection before reporting a retained close failure. Ghidra memory cgroup sampling no longer passes the resource scope's admission gate, so a pending owner cannot mask the provider failure; failed closes are still retained for session cleanup. The raw FileHandle close rule resolves this through arrow functions only, treats static blocks as static, and keeps #name distinct from constructor parameter properties.

* fix(ghidra): join in-flight cgroup samples before session cleanup

ArtifactResourceScope.track runs optional work outside the admission gate while cleanup drains still join it, so a cancelled request's final retry cannot finish before a sample retains a failed close.

* fix(filesystem): join work tracked during a cleanup drain and report doctor file cleanup as typed errors

A cleanup retry now repeats until no tracked work is active and every retained owner has had one attempt, so diagnostic work admitted while an earlier owner is releasing is joined. Doctor reports a retained runner or configuration file close as a ProviderCleanupError bound to its lease instead of rethrowing a raw file failure, so the error document keeps the retained file.

* fix(desktop): read the agentenv runner head through the artifact file owner

The runner read retained a failed close under one lease while the reported failure carried another, so a successful cleanup retry left the doctor error reporting an already-closed file. withArtifactFileHandle binds one lease to both.

* fix(mcp): register fx and MCPorter where they read their configuration

fx reads $FX_HOME/mcp.json when FX_HOME is set, and MCPorter reads
MCPORTER_CONFIG exclusively or prefers an absolute XDG_CONFIG_HOME file.
rea mcp add always wrote ~/.fx/mcp.json and ~/.mcporter/mcporter.json,
which those clients then ignored. Resolve both from the clients' own
rules, and refuse an FX_HOME fx itself refuses.

Address review findings: MCPORTER_CONFIG now also names the detection
marker, so default registration includes MCPorter when only that file
exists, and is resolved with path.resolve as MCPorter does. FX_HOME with
. or .. segments is refused, so the private profile mode cannot reach
the home folder through an alias. Override tests use the host's path
rules for real temporary paths.

* fix(mcp): never apply fx's private folder mode to the home folder

A linked parent in FX_HOME can name the caller's home folder after the textual root and home checks pass. The private profile writer now compares the opened folder's identity with the caller's home folder and refuses before changing modes or publishing.

* feat(setup): let doctor, update and uninstall see MCPorter registrations (#10702)

* feat(setup): let doctor, update and uninstall see MCPorter registrations

MCPorter becomes a client-table row, so a registration rea mcp add or
rea setup --client mcporter wrote is inspected, refreshed and removed like
other clients. MCPorter already imports setup-managed clients'
registrations, so the row is applicable only through REA's own
registration: setup never selects it from detection and doctor reports
it only when its file holds a rea row or the caller selects it. A
relative MCPORTER_CONFIG is refused because MCPorter resolves it per
command directory.

* fix(setup): detect MCPorter by the folder of the file it loads

With an absolute XDG_CONFIG_HOME and only a legacy ~/.mcporter file, the row returned the legacy file but the absent XDG folder as its detection evidence, so default registration and setup skipped MCPorter.

A client whose configuration location cannot be resolved (for example a relative MCPORTER_CONFIG) is reported as unknown, never missing or absent.
