commits.body:
refactor(captures): classify TShark, sigrok and pcap failures through the shared provider classifier (#10820)

* fix(pcap): report a refused tool launch as an unavailable tool

When a capture read's tool launch was refused with EPERM, pcap reported it
as unreadable tool output (AnalysisProtocolError) instead of an unavailable
tool. Pcap also never told "not executable" apart from "missing".

Add classifyLaunchFailure in src/process as the one owner of which spawn
errnos mean missing (ENOENT, ENOTDIR) and which mean present but not
executable (EACCES, EPERM, ENOEXEC, EISDIR). Pcap, apktool and gdb used three
different errno lists; all three now use it.

* refactor(process): classify owned command outcomes through one owner

Add ProviderOutcome, read once from the supervisor's facts, and classifyProviderOutcome, the one mapping from an outcome to a typed error. Migrate pcap and the shared artifact producer command failure (TShark, sigrok). Add the rea/provider-failure-classifier lint rule with a shrink-only baseline of per-site (cause: unknown) => AnalysisError functions.

* refactor(process): classify Java and adb launch refusals with the shared owner (#10598)

The Ghidra and JADX Java probes and adb's version probe now take
missing-versus-not-executable from classifyLaunchFailure instead of their
own errno checks. ELOOP and ENAMETOOLONG join the owner's missing set, so
adb keeps its existing classification and both Java probes now treat a
non-directory path component as a missing runtime.

* fix(pcap): preserve command launch attribution

* test(pcap): expect an unknown failing stage when a limited capture tool exits unsuccessfully

* refactor(process): classify owned command outcomes through one owner

Add ProviderOutcome, read once from the supervisor's facts, and classifyProviderOutcome, the one mapping from an outcome to a typed error. Migrate pcap and the shared artifact producer command failure (TShark, sigrok). Add the rea/provider-failure-classifier lint rule with a shrink-only baseline of per-site (cause: unknown) => AnalysisError functions.

* test(lint): cover baselined files in the provider-failure classifier rule

* fix(apktool): report the decoder JVM's heap exhaustion as memory, not a target refusal

The supervisor now watches for a managed runtime's out-of-memory report while output streams (JVM java.lang.OutOfMemoryError, V8 'JavaScript heap out of memory'), so a retention budget cannot hide it. ProviderOutcome gains a runtime-exhausted kind and classifyProviderOutcome maps it once. Apktool decode opts in and moves to the shared classifier; Ghidra's single-purpose output token becomes the JVM runtime option and its area matching reuses the shared table.

* fix(process): keep the runtime's out-of-memory report on the memory error it supports

* fix(pcap): attribute a limited capture's exit through the prlimit wrapper

* fix(process): keep a shortened out-of-memory line marked as shortened

* fix(process): identify the refused executable for every launcher shape

Name the executable on errnos Node throws synchronously from spawn
(ENOEXEC, ENOTDIR, ...) and read the Windows native launcher's
executable-launch constraint, so pcap attributes those refusals to the
selected tool or limiter instead of an unknown stage.

* test(pcap): prove synchronous launch naming with ENOTDIR on every POSIX host

* fix(apktool): advise the JVM limit that governs the reported memory area

* fix(ghidra): read the supervisor's parsed OOM area instead of reparsing lines

* fix(sqlite,capture): read V8 heap exhaustion from streamed output, not retained stderr (#10724)

The SQLite worker and the Node capture decoders now declare runtime: "v8", so the supervisor observes V8's heap report as output streams. Both classifiers read the runtime-exhausted outcome instead of matching retained stderr, so a report beyond the retention budget, or one whose process then overflowed its output budget, is still reported as memory exhaustion.

* refactor(evm): classify EVMole worker outcomes through the shared provider classifier (#10716)

* refactor(evm): classify EVMole worker outcomes through the shared provider classifier

The EVMole worker's cancellation, deadline, output budget and CPU/file-size signals now go through classifyProviderOutcome; only the prlimit launch refusal and the reserved EFBIG exit remain in its dialect. The worker is opted into V8 exhaustion scanning so a heap report names its fixed 256 MiB heap. providerOutcomeOf now reads a launch refusal only from a spawn errno, so a private-storage or carrier read errno is no longer reported as a limiter launch failure.

* fix(evm): keep a stream failure's exit status and update Linux worker expectations

* refactor(process): read launch refusals through the launcher identity owner

* refactor(wasm): classify WABT command outcomes through the shared provider classifier (#10727)

* refactor(wasm): classify WABT command outcomes through the shared provider classifier

WABT's cancellation, command deadline, output budget, and inherited-limit signals now go through classifyProviderOutcome; its dialect keeps only the configuration-probe and launch-refusal unavailability and the unclassified-exit output error. A tool ended by SIGXCPU/SIGXFSZ or the memory limit is now a resource constraint instead of an output error, and a refused launch in the producer phase is reported as unavailable. The shared timeout context gains the analysis setting that selected the deadline, and the output-limit context may name its exceeded budget.

* fix(wasm): keep setup guidance when a WABT version probe's output cannot be collected

* refactor(providers): classify raw provider failures through one owner

* refactor(process): build classified cancellations with cancelledBy and the carried caller reason

* chore(lint): count runOwned's close-failure mapper from main in the classifier baseline

* fix(process): carry the runtime's exhaustion report on every memory error that claims it

SQLite and historical-capture memory errors recognised a streamed V8 heap report but dropped it, so a report outside retained output reached callers without its source line or omission flags. One projection, runtimeExhaustionReport, now owns that shape for the shared classifier and both consumers. Also lowers the EVMole and WABT cancellation-constructor baselines.

* fix(process): keep the provider's recovery for a native-thread exhaustion report

The shared classifier replaced the provider-supplied recovery with generic capacity advice whenever the JVM reported it could not create a native thread, dropping Apktool's launcher guidance and flipping retryable to true. The provider's recovery now wins; the capacity advice remains the fallback for providers that supply none.

* refactor(pwntools): classify pwntools failures through the shared provider classifier (#10782)

* refactor(pwntools): classify pwntools failures through the shared provider classifier

pwntools' per-site classifier is replaced by pwntoolsFailureDialect for classifyProviderFailure. Command outcomes go through classifyProviderOutcome, launch refusals through launcherRefusalOf instead of a 'spawn ' syscall prefix check, the input limit through the file dialect's fileSize, and the cleanup report through commandCleanup. The shared read cancellation now carries the reader's partial observation, and resource-signal reports accept provider detail.

* fix(pwntools): report a failed command's output once and expect resource_constraint for overflow

The shared outcome owner already attaches the command's output as capturedOutput, so the pwntools adapter fallback no longer copies the same text into diagnostics.stdout, diagnostics.stderr and diagnostics.captured_output; diagnostics keep the exit facts. Update the overflow expectations the dialect migration missed (layout provider cleanup and over-budget rows, pwntools cleanup) to resource_constraint.

* refactor(wasm): leave WABT cancellation to the shared owners

WabtFailures matched any Error named AbortError as a cancellation. No WABT path produces one: reads, path checks and owned commands report cancellation as ArtifactReaderFailure or OwnedCommandFailure, which classifyProviderFailure and classifyProviderOutcome already classify with the caller's reason. The provider's two signal checks now build the cancellation with cancelledBy. Lowers the AnalysisCancelledError constructor baseline for both WABT files to zero.

* fix(wasm): report a cancelled snapshot write as the caller's cancellation

The private snapshot write passed the caller's signal to Node's writeFile, whose abort envelope reached the dialect's unclassified output failure once the name-based AbortError guess was removed. The write now turns the envelope carrying its own signal's reason into cancelledBy at the producer.

* refactor(firmware): classify firmware failures through the shared provider classifier (#10810)

Firmware producers now report their own deadline expiry: the start check, the output inventory and launcher admission throw the phase timeout where they observe the abort, and a read the phase signal cancelled reports it through the dialect's interruption. The classifier no longer rereads a cancellation's reason as a timeout. A new readCleanup hook keeps firmware's cleanup report shape.

* refactor(captures): classify TShark, sigrok and pcap failures through the shared provider classifier

TsharkCaptureProvider and SigrokRecordingProvider replace #failure with a dialect, and PcapProvider replaces analysisFailure and the tool-identity classifier. ArtifactAnalysisResources exposes its command context and a readCleanupFailure composer so the readCleanup hook keeps each provider's cleanup report shape.

* chore(guards): shrink the cancellation construction baseline after merging the base

commits.subject: refactor(desktop): release retained screen-judge cleanup through its lease (#10809)
commits.body:
refactor(desktop): release retained screen-judge cleanup through its lease (#10809)

* refactor(errors): read cleanup completion from dependencies instead of pushing it to dependents

AnalysisError.cleanupIncomplete becomes a getter over the error's own unresolved state and its bound dependencies. The WeakRef dependents graph and resolveCleanup's push propagation are removed, and subclasses mark their initial state through markCleanupIncomplete instead of overriding a public mutable field.

* fix(errors): settle bound dependencies before binding more

A composite whose dependencies had released but whose status was never read
stayed incomplete when a later dependency was bound.

* refactor(errors): let errors read a lease group's release instead of resolving them (#10759)

AnalysisCleanupLeaseGroup no longer calls resolveCleanup() on its error.
The error holds the group as a release claim and reads cleanupReleased when
asked, so completion follows the lease owner without a push.

* chore(verify): count resolveCleanup and bindCleanupDependencies calls so they only shrink (#10763)

* refactor(errors): let errors read a lease group's release instead of resolving them

AnalysisCleanupLeaseGroup no longer calls resolveCleanup() on its error.
The error holds the group as a release claim and reads cleanupReleased when
asked, so completion follows the lease owner without a push.

* chore(verify): count resolveCleanup and bindCleanupDependencies calls so they only shrink

* refactor(process): let worker cleanup errors read their root epoch's release

OwnedWorkerRuntime's root epoch is now an AnalysisCleanupReleaseClaim. Errors bound to it read its release when asked instead of the epoch pushing resolveCleanup() through weak references, and a runtime without a retained root binds an already-released owner. Removes the OwnedWorkerCleanupFailure structural type and four resolveCleanup() pushes; the counted baseline shrinks accordingly.

* refactor(pcap): let pcap cleanup errors read command and snapshot release (#10792)

Retained pcap commands, retained snapshot failures and snapshot completion descriptors now own their release and errors read it: commands and snapshot failures implement AnalysisCleanupReleaseClaim, and a failed completion-descriptor close is retried through an AnalysisCleanupLease bound to its error. Removes four resolveCleanup() pushes; the counted baseline shrinks accordingly.

* refactor(process): let Darwin helper cleanup errors read their owner's release

Darwin helper cache and run-token reader root cleanup now record an AnalysisCleanupRelease that every failure reports; a successful retry confirms it. Replaces the first-failure anchor that later failures depended on and the resolveCleanup() push. Removes two resolveCleanup() and two bindCleanupDependencies() calls; both counted baselines shrink.

* refactor(ghidra): let Ghidra cleanup errors read the client's and checkpoint's release

GhidraClient and GhidraCheckpoint bind each cleanup failure to an AnalysisCleanupRelease and confirm it when a later close or retry releases everything, instead of keeping a set of failures and pushing resolveCleanup() to each. Removes two resolveCleanup() calls; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(process): let debugger session cleanup errors read a confirmed stop

OwnedDebuggerSessionRegistry binds each retained gdb or rizin cleanup failure to the session's AnalysisCleanupRelease and confirms it when a stop is confirmed, keeping the latest failure for retry reporting, instead of pushing resolveCleanup() to a set of failures. Removes one resolveCleanup() call; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(process): drop the debugger registry's unused closeOperation option

Returning the latest retained failure removed the last reader of closeOperation; remove the option and the values gdb and rizin supplied.

* refactor(server): let environment shutdown errors read a successful close

serveEnvironment binds each shutdown failure to an AnalysisCleanupRelease that a later successful close confirms, instead of pushing resolveCleanup() to a set of failures. The state-file retry test now also requires the earlier report to read the release. Removes one resolveCleanup() call; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(desktop): release retained screen-judge cleanup through its lease

Each retained judge or screenshot cleanup owner is wrapped in an AnalysisCleanupLease bound to its failure; close() releases the lease, which records the release the failure reads, instead of closing the owner and pushing resolveCleanup(). Removes one resolveCleanup() call; the counted baseline shrinks.

commits.subject: docs: describe omitted output schemas as the default in README translations (#10658)
commits.body:
docs: describe omitted output schemas as the default in README translations (#10658)

* test(mcp): check advertised schemas against a portable dialect in every profile

* fix(mcp): re-emit advertised patterns in a portable regex grammar

* fix(mcp): present discover_tools input through the selected profile

The hot-cold catalog registered discover_tools directly with the SDK, so
the default compact input profile still advertised its canonical schema,
including page-size defaults clients apply on their own (#5322). Route
every listed input schema, transport discovery included, through one
server-owned presentation, and pass the selected presentation to the
deferred server, which serves recorded tool schemas but not discovery.

* fix(mcp): keep the Evidence union on described borrowed inputs

borrowEvidenceInput installed its advertised projection on one schema
instance. A call site's .describe() rebuilds the schema from its
definition, so match_native_functions advertised left and right as
unconstrained values in every input profile. Install the projection in
the borrowed parser's constructor so derived schemas keep it, for both
borrowed inputs and borrowed arrays.

* fix(mcp): validate advertised dialect by selected profile

* fix(mcp): preserve schema widening through references

* feat(mcp): project compact input schemas into the portable advertised dialect

One projection (advertisedDialectProjection.ts) owns the compact input
advertisement: one type per node, items on every array, string literals
as enums, oneOf widened to anyOf, allOf merged, tuples as element unions,
exclusive bounds made inclusive, and every keyword outside the dialect
dropped. Each rewrite is exact or widening; server validation is
unchanged. The root description and sentences for dropped cross-field
constraints move to the tool description, which Codex and Zed keep.

The compact baseline falls to nullable values only (29), which the
dialect cannot express without narrowing an input. The gateway shape
repairs (typeArrayItemUnions, hasGatewayIncompatibleShape), the second
dependentRequired-to-prose copy and the strict-gateway test denylist are
removed; the dialect checker gates the inline presentation instead.

* feat(mcp): omit output schemas from tools/list by default

No surveyed model API reads an output schema, MCP client validators
repeat REA's own result validation, and complete output schemas were
about 92% of the default tools/list. REA_MCP_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE now
resolves to off through one owner (resolveMcpOutputSchemaProfile);
compact and full remain selectable. structuredContent is still
delivered, and the deferred server serves both off and full from the
recorded catalog with the matching recorded identity.

Tests and artifact verifiers that validate results against complete
advertised output contracts select full explicitly.

* fix(mcp): keep the Evidence union on described borrowed inputs

borrowEvidenceInput installed its advertised projection on one schema
instance. A call site's .describe() rebuilds the schema from its
definition, so match_native_functions advertised left and right as
unconstrained values in every input profile. Install the projection in
the borrowed parser's constructor so derived schemas keep it, for both
borrowed inputs and borrowed arrays.

* test(mcp): select the borrowed Evidence contract from its family

* docs(mcp): admit baseline growth only for restored contract declarations

* fix(mcp): state reduced multi-type properties as typed branches, not type lists

The reduced fallback derived a property's types and emitted them as a type
list, which Gemini, Moonshot and Ark reject. A property whose canonical
schema is anyOf string and number therefore traded a typed union for a
rejected construct when the inline projection fell back. Emit one type, or
anyOf typed branches, so [T, null] becomes the dialect's nullable union.

commits.subject: refactor(application): build application cancellations with a required reason (#10574)
commits.body:
refactor(application): build application cancellations with a required reason (#10574)

* refactor(application): build application cancellations with a required reason

Migrate every AnalysisCancelledError construction under src/application
to cancelledBy and lower the guard baseline from 671 to 442.

Shutdown refusals in BinarySession report OwnerCancellation.ownerClosed
when the caller did not abort, instead of an undefined reason.
ReverseEngineeringService and DesktopBuildOwnedWork close their work
with the typed owner reason. SharedStartupAttempt returns the departing
caller's reason with a cancelled wait. One shared isAborted predicate
replaces eleven local copies and narrows a checked signal for
cancelledBy.

* refactor(desktop): drop an unused cancellation import from desktop capture state

commits.subject: perf(mcp): advertise large output union alternatives as shared definitions (#11005)
commits.body:
perf(mcp): advertise large output union alternatives as shared definitions (#11005)

* perf(mcp): advertise large output union alternatives as shared definitions

inspect_analysis_view's advertised output schema held every view result inline in one union definition, which the MCP SDK's default validator compiled into one function: about 1.7 s CPU and 500 MiB peak. Large union alternatives now become definitions of their own and identical definitions are merged, at the owning output projection. Tests that check results against the advertised output contract now compile that schema instead of a separate inline projection, which overflowed the main-thread stack under forked workers.

* perf(tests): run source test projects in forked workers (#11016)

Thread workers of the source lane share one process, which grew to 3.8-5.0 GiB; forked workers keep each heap separate so the largest process stays near 1.2-1.8 GiB.

* test(mcp): select the analysis view contract from its family

commits.body:
refactor(verify): give seven verifier directories' fixture roots to VerifierFixture (#11055)

* refactor(verify): give the android, electron, firmware, ghidra-seed, harmony, inspector and managed verifiers' roots to VerifierFixture

Each root is removed only after the MCP clients, transports, owned processes
and file handles that may still use it confirm cleanup; a failed cleanup
retains and names the root. The verifier-fixture-root baseline shrinks from
90 files / 95 sites to 80 / 85.

* fix(verify): keep nested Electron and inspector children owned by the fixture, and plain roots where Windows creates directories

The Electron cancellation CLI and application, and each inspector target,
now register their stop with the fixture (onceConfirmed keeps the early stop),
so the root is removed only after they confirm. The android and inspector
verifiers keep a plain directory as before: tools create directories beneath
the root, which a private root blocks on Windows.

feat(evidence): name the side and issue path of comparison source integrity failures (#11049)

* feat(process): name the side and issue path of process-capture integrity failures

compare_process_captures reported which side failed validation, and where,
only in the message. EvidenceIntegrityError now carries an optional side
and issue path, projected as details.side and details.issue_path, and the
CLI's malformed-capture issue carries observed.issue_path. The first issue
path comes from the same selection describeValidationFailure names.

* feat(evidence): report source authentication issue paths from the Evidence owner

readEvidence and readImmutableEvidence now set the record-relative issue
path on their integrity failure, and readEvidencePayload sets it when the

compare_process_captures. Process capture result issue paths are now
relative to the Evidence record (normalized_result.*) on both adapters.

commits.subject: fix(rizin): refuse a start after shutdown began as an owner-closed cancellation (#11041)
commits.body:
fix(rizin): refuse a start after shutdown began as an owner-closed cancellation (#11041)

OwnedDebuggerSessionRegistry owns the rule: closeStarts refuses later starts
as owner-closed (a caller that already aborted keeps its own reason) and
aborts in-flight ones. Rizin no longer reports an inferior_tty input error
for a start made after closeAll began; GDB's local copy of the rule is gone.

User-visible: start_rizin_debug_session called while REA is shutting down
now fails as a cancellation (owner closed) instead of an input error naming
inferior_tty, matching start_gdb_session.

commits.body:
feat(evidence): name a standalone Evidence record with detected_kind on every bundle refusal (#11039)

The file reader, inline bundle reader and investigation ledger refused a
single Evidence record with only a message saying so. The file reader's

commits.subject: fix(errors): rethrow internal invariant violations from plist consumers and the native output projection (#11029)
commits.body:
fix(errors): rethrow internal invariant violations from plist consumers and the native output projection (#11029)

* fix(plist): rethrow internal invariant violations from plist consumers

KeyedArchiveReader reported any non-limit decode failure as a format
failure, InterfaceBuilderAnalysis listed it as an invalid archive,
ReleaseExposureReader fell back to scanning raw bytes, and the native
plist parser reported it as provider output. An InternalInvariantError
is a REA defect, not evidence about the input, so each consumer now
rethrows it. The native parser's binary path now shares its one cause
projection instead of a duplicate.

* fix(native): rethrow internal invariant violations from the native output projection

nativeOutputFailure wrapped any producer failure as AnalysisOutputError,
so a REA defect thrown while reading a plist or dispatching a command was
reported as native output parsing. It now rethrows InternalInvariantError,
which reaches the provider's adapter-failure path with the invariant as
its cause.

* fix(artifacts): rethrow internal invariant violations from the shared artifact failure mapper

translateArtifactFailure turned every unrecognised cause into an
ArtifactOperationError with reason io, so the keyed-archive and
Interface Builder rethrows still reached users as artifact read
failures. The shared mapper now rethrows InternalInvariantError, and the
deferred client reports it as a ProviderAdapterError. Provider-level
tests drive both operations through that client.

* refactor(dotnet): report managed reader defects through invariantViolation (#11030)

* refactor(dotnet): report managed reader defects through invariantViolation

The managed readers threw plain TypeError and RangeError for states their
callers rule out: an allowance or method page outside the input schema, a
missing snapshot after identity admission, and a missing CLI header after
the caller already returned for it. These are REA defects, not malformed
targets, so they throw invariantViolation. The two CLI re-checks are gone:
the callers pass the CLI header they already narrowed. The dotnet
parser-plain-throw baseline drops from 6 to 0.

* refactor(providers): refuse unusable tool paths and record marker mismatches without throwing to their own catch (#11031)

* refactor(firmware): refuse unusable tool paths without throwing to its own catch

resolveFirmwareCommand threw a plain TypeError for a configured engine or
limiter path that is not a regular file, only to catch it in the next line
and wrap it as an unavailable capability. A helper now returns why a path
cannot run, and each caller builds the one refusal directly. Refusal
reasons are unchanged; the directory tests now pin them exactly. The
firmware parser-plain-throw baseline drops from 2 to 0.

* refactor(pwndbg): refuse unusable debugger paths without throwing to its own catch

inspectPwndbgCore threw plain Errors for a relative or wrong-kind
configured path only to catch them and wrap them as an unavailable
capability. A helper now returns why a path cannot be used, with any host
error as its cause, and the loop builds the one refusal. Cancellation
between host checks still propagates. Refusal reasons are unchanged. The
PwndbgCoreContext parser-plain-throw baseline entry is removed.

* refactor(pwntools): record a mismatched failure marker without throwing to its own catch

readPwntoolsFailureEvidence threw a plain Error when the private bridge
marker disagreed with the exit status, only to catch it and record its
message as the marker failure. The mismatch is now recorded directly. The
recorded evidence is unchanged; a unit test pins both the matching and
the mismatched marker. The PwntoolsResourceLimits parser-plain-throw
baseline entry is removed.

* fix(android): report an unobserved Java probe as a REA defect, not a Java refusal (#11032)

* fix(android): report an unobserved Java probe as a REA defect, not a Java refusal

When runOwnedCommand resolved without observing the completed run, the
probe threw a plain Error that its catch then classified as a Java
runtime refusal, telling the caller to review their launcher. The state
is a broken internal assumption, so the probe throws invariantViolation
and projects it as a jadx adapter failure. The JadxJavaProbe
parser-plain-throw baseline entry is removed.

* refactor(native): report native provider defects through invariantViolation (#11033)

* refactor(native): report native provider defects through invariantViolation

Native providers threw plain Error and TypeError for states their own
earlier steps rule out: a client with no target, a measured slice with no
selection, a read longer than requested, a decoder command without its
runtime, an LLDB root released before its children, and an IPS integer
fact from another reader. These are REA defects, so they throw
invariantViolation. NativeUiInterruptionControl no longer needs a throw:
recording the deadline interruption returns the interruption its error is
built from. Six native parser-plain-throw baseline entries drop.

* refactor(native): report malformed lipo, swift-demangle and UI helper output through ParseFailure (#11034)

* refactor(native): report malformed lipo and swift-demangle output through ParseFailure

The lipo and swift-demangle output parsers threw plain TypeError for
output that breaks their framing, and the lipo result classifier caught
every TypeError as malformed output, so a host TypeError from a REA defect
was reported as lipo output. Both parsers now throw malformedInput with
their own format, and the lipo classifier accepts ParseFailureError
instead of TypeError. Messages and the consumers' output and format
failure categories are unchanged. Four native parser-plain-throw
baseline entries drop.

* refactor(native): report the UI helper's non-JSON output through ParseFailure

The native UI helper runtime threw a plain Error when the helper's
stdout was not JSON. It now throws malformedInput with its own format and
the JSON failure as cause. The observation boundary still reports it as a
native-macos adapter failure with the same reason. The
NativeUiHelperRuntime parser-plain-throw baseline entry is removed.

* refactor(verify): keep process-lifecycle owners out of the parser plain-throw guard (#11035)

* refactor(verify): keep process-lifecycle owners out of the parser plain-throw guard

JadxWorkspaceRoot and PwntoolsDecoder sit in parser folders but own a
private helper process; their remaining plain throws report the helper's
startup, handshake and cleanup outcomes, not parse faults. The guard now
names them as process-lifecycle owners and leaves them out, so their
five baseline entries drop without inventing parse errors for process
failures.

* refactor(parsers): report the remaining artifact, il2cpp, model and domain defects through invariantViolation (#11036)

* refactor(parsers): report the remaining artifact, il2cpp, model and domain defects through invariantViolation

Nine plain Error, TypeError and RangeError throws in parser folders
reported broken internal assumptions or caller contracts (an
uninitialized ZIP or DMG reader, a missing scan result, a non-byte
stream chunk, an invalid traversal or marshal limit, a header count or
linking fact the reader itself should have produced, a misordered
Safetensors budget, an append after fingerprinting). None is an input
fault, and no catch site depends on their class. They now throw
invariantViolation with the same messages, and their parser-plain-throw
baseline entries drop.

* refactor(evidence): refuse an earlier Evidence format through ParseFailure (#11037)

* refactor(evidence): refuse an earlier Evidence format through ParseFailure

UnsupportedEvidenceFormatError restated the ParseFailure algebra as its
own TypeError subclass. The format owner now throws unsupportedInput for
the evidence-bundle format at the evidence_format field and exports the
predicate its consumers use. The bundle reader's unsupported-format kind
and message are unchanged. The snapshot reader surfaced only TypeError
messages, so it now also surfaces the format refusal and keeps its
recreate guidance; a boundary test pins that.

* refactor(native): report Mach-O reader and inspection defects through invariantViolation (#11042)

The Mach-O inspection plan reads the lipo, nm and dyld_info captures it
just ran, the dispatch metadata reader is called only for Mach-O
executables, and the command-name reader takes limits its callers
derive. A missing capture, a non-Mach-O target or a malformed limit is a
REA defect, not an input fault, so these six sites throw
invariantViolation with their existing messages instead of TypeError.
No catch site depends on their class. Their parser-plain-throw baseline
entries drop.

* fix(artifacts): join the Interface Builder cleanup failure to a catalog defect

When catalog work failed while the concurrent Interface Builder reader
failed to close, analyzeAppleAssetCatalogs built the primary through
translateArtifactFailure before joining cleanup. That mapper now rethrows
an InternalInvariantError, so a defect skipped the join and the reader's
retained resources were lost. The defect now becomes the artifact graph
provider's adapter failure at that site and joins the cleanup failure as
before.

commits.subject: feat(artifacts): name which ASAR integrity check failed on the reader failure (#11021)
commits.body:
feat(artifacts): name which ASAR integrity check failed on the reader failure (#11021)

* feat(artifacts): name which ASAR integrity check failed on the reader failure

* test(artifacts): assert the ASAR stream's declared-size and read-coverage checks

* fix(artifacts): report a close queued behind ASAR preparation as unavailable

The missing-snapshot check was reachable when close() ran between a
prepareContainer() and the following entries() or openContainer()
operation, and reported a caller close as an integrity failure. Classify
it like the sibling closed-inventory check and cover foreign-entry with a
stale entry opened after close.

commits.subject: feat(providers): bound runOwned work and close by one deadline (#10996)
commits.body:
feat(providers): bound runOwned work and close by one deadline (#10996)

* feat(providers): bound runOwned work and close by one deadline

* fix(providers): read an expired budget at settle time and keep a caller abort during cleanup

* fix(providers): follow a late close rejection's owner and keep captured output through budget replacements

* fix(providers): track budget expiry apart from the caller, keep replaced work's cleanup, treat empty leases as none

* fix(providers): classify thrown abort reasons, keep recorded failures and follow a late close owner's resources

Work that throws its signal's abort reason (throwIfAborted) is now a
cancellation, so an elapsed budget becomes a timeout and a caller abort stays a
cancellation. A budget cancellation replaced by a timeout or a caller
cancellation keeps the secondary failures it recorded. A late close rejection
that names its own owner now also supplies the retained failure's resources.

* fix(providers): classify only the budget's own abort reason, and follow only a late rejection that reports its own cleanup

A caller's abort reason is opaque, so a thrown value equal to it stays the
work's failure with the caller's cancellation retained; only the budget's typed
OwnerCancellation.deadlineElapsed marks a thrown abort as the budget's. A late
close rejection without unreleased cleanup of its own (such as a cancellation)
no longer confirms release or replaces the fallback resource.

* fix(providers): follow a late close owner that already released, by cleanup ownership not completion

AnalysisError.carriesCleanup owns whether an error ever owned cleanup, apart
from whether it finished. runOwned's late close rejection uses it, so a
producer error released by a concurrent retry still confirms release, while a
cancellation without cleanup keeps the close's lease pending. Uninstall and
SetupCleanupOwner used the same four-clause predicate locally; they now read
the owner.

commits.subject: feat(evidence)!: require JavaScript, browser, managed and reference-source facts their producers always write (#10990)
commits.body:
feat(evidence)!: require JavaScript, browser, managed and reference-source facts their producers always write (#10990)

* feat(javascript)!: require the runtime parse-failure count and active Electron execution paths

The V8 Inspector projection always writes scripts.parse_failed_total and the
active Electron service always commits parameters.resolved_paths, so both are
now required. Runtime reconciliation reads the admitted execution paths only
and no longer falls back to request-spelled paths in parameters, and checks
the observed executable path against them on every capture.

JavaScriptStaticAnalysis.routes and module_runtime keep their omission, which
current producers still make (a checkpoint that cannot retain route facts; no
recovered factory runtime); their comments now say so instead of naming
historical analyses.

BREAKING CHANGE: JavaScript runtime observations without
scripts.parse_failed_total, and active Electron Evidence without
parameters.resolved_paths, are refused as malformed; recreate the observation.

* test(javascript): give the shared Node reconciliation fixture the required parse-failure count

* feat(browser)!: require browser observation facts their producers always write (#10991)

* feat(browser)!: require browser observation facts their producers always write

The source-map fetcher always writes effective_url (string or null), the web
bundle analyzer always writes schema_property_names_coverage, and the CDP
storage fingerprinter always marks IndexedDB schema fingerprints with
projection_version 2. Each is now required. The IndexedDB marker is tied to
its scope by a discriminated union and derived from the scope in the
producer, so compare_web_captures no longer carries the store-only
projection branch.

response_identity and the WebMCP consequential hint keep their omission,
which current producers still make (a body not fully read; an invalid
annotation); the guide no longer attributes it to historical captures.

BREAKING CHANGE: source-map items without effective_url, WebMCP declarations
without schema_property_names_coverage, and IndexedDB schema fingerprints
without projection_version are refused as malformed; recreate the capture.

* feat(managed)!: refuse members beside a null signature resolution (#10992)

* feat(managed)!: refuse members beside a null signature resolution

signature_resolution is null only when member decoding exceeded capacity,
and the capacity-recovery producer then examines no members. The managed
member inspection schema now enforces that: a null resolution with any
field, method, member reference, call edge or field access is malformed.

With that rule, every admitted inspection with members attests type-name
resolution, so the raw-digest fallback is unreachable and is deleted:
comparableSides, hasSignatureResolution, the comparison's
signatureResolutionExamined flag and the "does not attest" limitation. The
shared workflow example that carried resolved digests beside a null
attestation now attests resolution.

BREAKING CHANGE: managed member Evidence with a null signature_resolution
and any examined member is refused as malformed; recreate the observation.

* docs: describe historical Evidence by what the format revision now refuses (#10993)

SQLite worker_timeout_ms is required, so the SQLite guide no longer reads a
missing value as unknown settings. The IL2CPP, ESP image and process capture
guides now say that bundles exported without evidence_format are refused,
while a standalone record from an earlier release is still read with the
stated omission semantics (records carry no format marker yet). The route
inventory guide describes a parent without route_inventory by its meaning
rather than by its age.

* refactor(javascript): require static analysis coverage from the JavaScript worker (#11001)

* refactor(javascript): require static analysis coverage from the JavaScript worker

Both JavaScript static producers always write analysis_coverage: the
analyzer measures it on every parsed source and the failed-parse result
carries an unexamined coverage. The worker schema and the static analysis
type therefore require it, the preload-discovery checkpoint copies it
unconditionally, and ElectronBoundaryAnalysis reads Electron applicability
and examination limits from it alone. The fallback that re-derived Electron
use from semantic module links and retained references for analyses
without coverage is deleted, as are the graph and builder branches for a
missing coverage.

Retained Evidence graph observations are unchanged: the analysis view still
counts a stored JavaScript observation without analysis_coverage as
unmeasured, since standalone records carry no format marker yet.

The worker runs from the same build as its parent, so no external caller
sees the stricter reply schema.

* feat(browser)!: require storage fingerprint, Link context, mapping index and invalid-map identity facts (#11002)

* feat(browser)!: require storage fingerprint, Link context, mapping index and invalid-map identity facts

Each field is written by its only producer on every capture:

- The CDP storage capture always writes content_fingerprints,
  fingerprint_algorithm and fingerprints_complete, so their schema defaults
  are removed.
- The CDP Link header projection always writes context_url and
  context_scope, so they are required.
- The source-map fetcher writes source_index and declaration_index on every
  mapping row, so they are required.
- The fetcher judges a map invalid only after reading its complete body. A
  separate invalidSourceMapItem builder now takes the response identity as a
  required argument, and the schema's invalid member requires
  response_identity; fetch_failed keeps it optional because those rows can
  come from a body that was not fully read.

The browser and source-location guides no longer describe these fields as
optional for older saved captures.

BREAKING CHANGE: page inspections without the storage fingerprint fields or
Link context fields, source-map mapping rows without their indexes, and
invalid source-map items without response_identity are refused as malformed;
recreate the capture.

* test(browser): keep source-omission coverage on a still-defaulted field and refuse a missing fingerprint algorithm

* feat(browser)!: require web-bundle target origin, inspection producer facts, scenario redirect state and exclusion kind (#11014)

feat(browser)!: require web-bundle target origin, page inspection producer facts, scenario redirect state and exclusion kind

Each field is written by its only producer on every record:

- buildCaptureObservation always writes capture.target_origin (the validated
  origin or null), so analyze_web_bundle Evidence and both web-bundle view
  results require it; the view's conditional spread is gone.
- The CDP page capture always writes accessibility node states, script
  frame_id (null when unattributed) and worker opener_target_id and
  parent_frame_id, so their schema defaults are removed.
- PlaywrightScenarioNetwork writes redirected_from_transaction_state exactly
  when the predecessor ID is null, so request events now require it there and
  still refuse it on linked events.
- The reference-source importer writes entry_kind on every exclusion
  (unknown when the kind was not observed), so it is required.

The browser scenario contract and CLI guide no longer describe older
captures or exclusions without these fields.

BREAKING CHANGE: web-bundle analyses without capture.target_origin, page
inspections without these script, accessibility or worker fields, scenario
network events with a null predecessor and no redirect state, and reference
source graphs whose exclusions lack entry_kind are refused as malformed;
recreate the capture or re-import the source.

commits.subject: refactor(jeb): classify JEB failures through the shared provider classifier (#10831)
commits.body:
refactor(jeb): classify JEB failures through the shared provider classifier (#10831)

* fix(pcap): report a refused tool launch as an unavailable tool

When a capture read's tool launch was refused with EPERM, pcap reported it
as unreadable tool output (AnalysisProtocolError) instead of an unavailable
tool. Pcap also never told "not executable" apart from "missing".

Add classifyLaunchFailure in src/process as the one owner of which spawn
errnos mean missing (ENOENT, ENOTDIR) and which mean present but not
executable (EACCES, EPERM, ENOEXEC, EISDIR). Pcap, apktool and gdb used three
different errno lists; all three now use it.

* refactor(process): classify owned command outcomes through one owner

Add ProviderOutcome, read once from the supervisor's facts, and classifyProviderOutcome, the one mapping from an outcome to a typed error. Migrate pcap and the shared artifact producer command failure (TShark, sigrok). Add the rea/provider-failure-classifier lint rule with a shrink-only baseline of per-site (cause: unknown) => AnalysisError functions.

* refactor(process): classify Java and adb launch refusals with the shared owner (#10598)

The Ghidra and JADX Java probes and adb's version probe now take
missing-versus-not-executable from classifyLaunchFailure instead of their
own errno checks. ELOOP and ENAMETOOLONG join the owner's missing set, so
adb keeps its existing classification and both Java probes now treat a
non-directory path component as a missing runtime.

* fix(pcap): preserve command launch attribution

* test(pcap): expect an unknown failing stage when a limited capture tool exits unsuccessfully

* refactor(process): classify owned command outcomes through one owner

Add ProviderOutcome, read once from the supervisor's facts, and classifyProviderOutcome, the one mapping from an outcome to a typed error. Migrate pcap and the shared artifact producer command failure (TShark, sigrok). Add the rea/provider-failure-classifier lint rule with a shrink-only baseline of per-site (cause: unknown) => AnalysisError functions.

* test(lint): cover baselined files in the provider-failure classifier rule

* fix(apktool): report the decoder JVM's heap exhaustion as memory, not a target refusal

The supervisor now watches for a managed runtime's out-of-memory report while output streams (JVM java.lang.OutOfMemoryError, V8 'JavaScript heap out of memory'), so a retention budget cannot hide it. ProviderOutcome gains a runtime-exhausted kind and classifyProviderOutcome maps it once. Apktool decode opts in and moves to the shared classifier; Ghidra's single-purpose output token becomes the JVM runtime option and its area matching reuses the shared table.

* fix(process): keep the runtime's out-of-memory report on the memory error it supports

* fix(pcap): attribute a limited capture's exit through the prlimit wrapper

* fix(process): keep a shortened out-of-memory line marked as shortened

* fix(process): identify the refused executable for every launcher shape

Name the executable on errnos Node throws synchronously from spawn
(ENOEXEC, ENOTDIR, ...) and read the Windows native launcher's
executable-launch constraint, so pcap attributes those refusals to the
selected tool or limiter instead of an unknown stage.

* test(pcap): prove synchronous launch naming with ENOTDIR on every POSIX host

* fix(apktool): advise the JVM limit that governs the reported memory area

* fix(ghidra): read the supervisor's parsed OOM area instead of reparsing lines

* fix(sqlite,capture): read V8 heap exhaustion from streamed output, not retained stderr (#10724)

The SQLite worker and the Node capture decoders now declare runtime: "v8", so the supervisor observes V8's heap report as output streams. Both classifiers read the runtime-exhausted outcome instead of matching retained stderr, so a report beyond the retention budget, or one whose process then overflowed its output budget, is still reported as memory exhaustion.

* refactor(evm): classify EVMole worker outcomes through the shared provider classifier (#10716)

* refactor(evm): classify EVMole worker outcomes through the shared provider classifier

The EVMole worker's cancellation, deadline, output budget and CPU/file-size signals now go through classifyProviderOutcome; only the prlimit launch refusal and the reserved EFBIG exit remain in its dialect. The worker is opted into V8 exhaustion scanning so a heap report names its fixed 256 MiB heap. providerOutcomeOf now reads a launch refusal only from a spawn errno, so a private-storage or carrier read errno is no longer reported as a limiter launch failure.

* fix(evm): keep a stream failure's exit status and update Linux worker expectations

* refactor(process): read launch refusals through the launcher identity owner

* refactor(wasm): classify WABT command outcomes through the shared provider classifier (#10727)

* refactor(wasm): classify WABT command outcomes through the shared provider classifier

WABT's cancellation, command deadline, output budget, and inherited-limit signals now go through classifyProviderOutcome; its dialect keeps only the configuration-probe and launch-refusal unavailability and the unclassified-exit output error. A tool ended by SIGXCPU/SIGXFSZ or the memory limit is now a resource constraint instead of an output error, and a refused launch in the producer phase is reported as unavailable. The shared timeout context gains the analysis setting that selected the deadline, and the output-limit context may name its exceeded budget.

* fix(wasm): keep setup guidance when a WABT version probe's output cannot be collected

* refactor(providers): classify raw provider failures through one owner

* refactor(process): build classified cancellations with cancelledBy and the carried caller reason

* chore(lint): count runOwned's close-failure mapper from main in the classifier baseline

* fix(process): carry the runtime's exhaustion report on every memory error that claims it

SQLite and historical-capture memory errors recognised a streamed V8 heap report but dropped it, so a report outside retained output reached callers without its source line or omission flags. One projection, runtimeExhaustionReport, now owns that shape for the shared classifier and both consumers. Also lowers the EVMole and WABT cancellation-constructor baselines.

* fix(process): keep the provider's recovery for a native-thread exhaustion report

The shared classifier replaced the provider-supplied recovery with generic capacity advice whenever the JVM reported it could not create a native thread, dropping Apktool's launcher guidance and flipping retryable to true. The provider's recovery now wins; the capacity advice remains the fallback for providers that supply none.

* refactor(pwntools): classify pwntools failures through the shared provider classifier (#10782)

* refactor(pwntools): classify pwntools failures through the shared provider classifier

pwntools' per-site classifier is replaced by pwntoolsFailureDialect for classifyProviderFailure. Command outcomes go through classifyProviderOutcome, launch refusals through launcherRefusalOf instead of a 'spawn ' syscall prefix check, the input limit through the file dialect's fileSize, and the cleanup report through commandCleanup. The shared read cancellation now carries the reader's partial observation, and resource-signal reports accept provider detail.

* fix(pwntools): report a failed command's output once and expect resource_constraint for overflow

The shared outcome owner already attaches the command's output as capturedOutput, so the pwntools adapter fallback no longer copies the same text into diagnostics.stdout, diagnostics.stderr and diagnostics.captured_output; diagnostics keep the exit facts. Update the overflow expectations the dialect migration missed (layout provider cleanup and over-budget rows, pwntools cleanup) to resource_constraint.

* refactor(wasm): leave WABT cancellation to the shared owners

WabtFailures matched any Error named AbortError as a cancellation. No WABT path produces one: reads, path checks and owned commands report cancellation as ArtifactReaderFailure or OwnedCommandFailure, which classifyProviderFailure and classifyProviderOutcome already classify with the caller's reason. The provider's two signal checks now build the cancellation with cancelledBy. Lowers the AnalysisCancelledError constructor baseline for both WABT files to zero.

* fix(wasm): report a cancelled snapshot write as the caller's cancellation

The private snapshot write passed the caller's signal to Node's writeFile, whose abort envelope reached the dialect's unclassified output failure once the name-based AbortError guess was removed. The write now turns the envelope carrying its own signal's reason into cancelledBy at the producer.

* refactor(firmware): classify firmware failures through the shared provider classifier (#10810)

Firmware producers now report their own deadline expiry: the start check, the output inventory and launcher admission throw the phase timeout where they observe the abort, and a read the phase signal cancelled reports it through the dialect's interruption. The classifier no longer rereads a cancellation's reason as a timeout. A new readCleanup hook keeps firmware's cleanup report shape.

* refactor(captures): classify TShark, sigrok and pcap failures through the shared provider classifier

TsharkCaptureProvider and SigrokRecordingProvider replace #failure with a dialect, and PcapProvider replaces analysisFailure and the tool-identity classifier. ArtifactAnalysisResources exposes its command context and a readCleanupFailure composer so the readCleanup hook keeps each provider's cleanup report shape.

* refactor(jeb): classify JEB failures through the shared provider classifier

JEB's raw MCP failures go through classifyProviderFailure with a JEB dialect;
a typed attribution step reports a shared phase's failure under the REA
operation. Each MCP phase deadline now reports its own interruption when it
aborts, deciding a cancellation's owner from the caller's own signal instead
of comparing abort reasons. A refusal carrying the JVM's OutOfMemoryError
report becomes a resource constraint naming JEB's Java heap.

* fix(jeb): advise the JVM limit that governs the reported memory area

* refactor(ghidra): classify Ghidra failures through the shared provider classifier (#10836)

* refactor(ghidra): classify Ghidra failures through the shared provider classifier

PSP extension inspection reports through classifyProviderFailure with a
Ghidra dialect. The startup deadline decides at abort time whether the shared
startup owner closed it, so Ghidra and Hopper no longer compare the abort
reason with the owner's sentinel, and Ghidra's startup no longer compares a
producer cancellation's reason with the deadline's. Three helpers that only
construct one error kind now name that kind instead of AnalysisError.

* refactor(hopper): classify original-source read failures through the shared provider classifier (#10838)

* test(ghidra): pin the aborted startup deadline over a producer cancellation

* refactor(kuna): classify Kuna failures through the shared provider classifier (#10843)

Session operations, the workspace copy and the project export report raw
failures through classifyProviderFailure with Kuna dialects; the copy and
export keep their cleanup report shapes through the readCleanup hook.

* chore(guards): shrink the cancellation construction baseline after merging the base

commits.subject: refactor(ida): launch stdio registrations through the owned MCP transport (#10739)
commits.body:
refactor(ida): launch stdio registrations through the owned MCP transport (#10739)

* refactor(ida): launch stdio registrations through the owned MCP transport

IDA stdio servers now run as an owned process group (POSIX) or job (Windows) through OwnedMcpStdioTransport instead of the SDK's unowned child. Windows bare commands resolve against the registration PATH/PATHEXT and .cmd/.bat launchers run through the shared WindowsBatchCommand cmd.exe invocation. The frame limit is classified from the transport's typed OwnedMcpOutputLimitError instead of parsing SDK error text, detach no longer reaches into the SDK's private _process, and the per-operation byte budget is optional.

* fix(ida): keep owned stdio cleanup observable and resolve Windows interpreter paths

- StructuredContentMcpClient observes SDK-initiated closes like OwnedMcpClient,
  so a failed handshake with incomplete owned cleanup cannot reject unhandled.
- OwnedMcpStdioTransport attaches an owner-redacted captured output to cleanup
  failures; IDA passes its retained stderr tail.
- findWindowsExecutable resolves path-qualified commands at their own location
  with PATHEXT; IDA routes every Windows registration through it and refuses
  non-drive paths with an actionable remedy before the owned launcher.

* fix(process): end a stalled stdio launch when the owned MCP transport closes

OwnedMcpStdioTransport passes the launcher a signal it aborts with OwnerCancellation.ownerClosed when it stops, so IDA's Windows PATH/PATHEXT lookup stalled on an unreachable directory no longer holds close() open; IDA reports the interrupted lookup by its abort reason. The IDA environment tests use createTestTempDirectory for owned temporary roots.

* fix(ida): bound the Windows command lookup by the registration timeout

The PATH/PATHEXT search for a stdio registration now runs under a ProviderStartupDeadline of the registration's timeoutMs that also follows the transport's close signal. A lookup stalled on an unreachable PATH directory ends as an AnalysisTimeoutError (phase windows_path_lookup) instead of leaving connect() pending, matching Apktool's Windows lookup.

* test(ida): stub REA's PATH again now that process inspection runs ps from fixed locations

* test(ida): pass the required registration protocol in owned-stdio fixtures

* fix(ida): report an uninspectable Windows command candidate with its path and code

* refactor(ida): take the host platform from composition, not an ambient read

* fix(verify): pass the host platform to the real IDA upstream check

* fix(process): keep a failed launch's preparation cleanup owned by the stdio transport's close

OwnedMcpStdioTransport discarded the launch rejection before a supervisor
existed, so an ownership-helper preparation that transferred a cleanup owner
(or reported a cleanup failure without one) was dropped and close() reported
success. The transport's close now closes each transferred owner from
processInspectionCleanupFailures, and reports a ProviderCleanupError naming the
preparation resource until it does; a later close retries it.

commits.subject: refactor(browser): parse frame lifecycle events once by a registered event schema (#10730)
commits.body:
refactor(browser): parse frame lifecycle events once by a registered event schema (#10730)

* refactor(browser): parse frame lifecycle events once by a registered event schema

CdpConnection admits each event through protocol/CdpEvents.ts, which parses
the five Page frame lifecycle events once into identity facts plus a frame
URL observation, like a frame-tree node. Screenshot, page capture, the
observation timeline, WebMCP, Electron inspection and the execution window
read those facts instead of re-parsing the raw payload; CdpFrameFacts no
longer carries the raw source record. Playwright CDP session subscriptions
name an event from Playwright's protocol table, and an architecture guard
counts the remaining raw event payload reads so they can only shrink.

* refactor(browser): admit transport events through the registered-event owner

Remove the unused cdpFrameUrl wrapper; its fragment cases now exercise
observeCdpFrameUrl. Add a connection-level test that two subscribers share
one parsed payload and the raw params.

commits.subject: feat(setup): manage fx, Junie, Goose and Kilo registrations through the client table (#10709)
commits.body:
feat(setup): manage fx, Junie, Goose and Kilo registrations through the client table (#10709)

* feat(setup): manage fx registrations with its private profile modes

fx becomes a client-table row, so doctor, update and uninstall see the
registration rea mcp add wrote, and setup offers fx when ~/.fx or
FX_HOME exists. Setup now publishes a private profile through the same
owner as mcp add (folder 0700, file 0600) and repairs those modes when
the row is otherwise current. Doctor parses fx's array launcher instead
of reporting it invalid.

* fix(setup): judge fx's private profile by its targets and keep its cleanup owner

Address review: privateProfileModesCurrent reads the modes of the canonical file and folder, so a linked profile becomes current; clientConfigurationAligned applies the same modes rule as plan and apply; a private-folder close failure reaches the caller with its cleanup owner instead of becoming a write failure; and the setup plan names the folder and file modes it sets.

* fix(setup): keep fx's recovery backups owner-only beside a linked profile

Setup and uninstall copied a private profile's original bytes with copyFile, so a backup beside a linked ~/.fx/mcp.json kept the target's readable mode outside the folder setup secures. Both now use the owner-only backup owner that mcp add already used.

* feat(setup): manage Junie registrations and apply its location policy (#10712)

* feat(setup): manage Junie registrations and apply its location policy

Junie becomes a client-table row, so doctor, update and uninstall see
the registration rea mcp add wrote, and setup offers Junie when its home
exists. Whether Junie loads its default user MCP file now has one owner,
read through the client policy block that setup, doctor and mcp add
already consult: setup and mcp add refuse, and doctor reports, a
registration Junie would not load.

* fix(setup): read Junie's user configuration as strict JSON

Address review: Junie loads config.json as strict JSON, so comments, trailing commas or an empty file leave its MCP location choice unknown, as before the move into the row. Filesystem tests also clear JUNIE_*, FX_HOME and MCPORTER_CONFIG so a developer's own client locations cannot be inspected or removed.

* test(setup): keep the detected client order out of the lifecycle suite body

The expected detection order grew with each folded client until the suite callback exceeded the max-lines-per-function lint limit.

* fix(update): report a client whose policy setup refuses instead of failing maintenance

Junie's disabled default locations (and Gemini's settings policy) make
doctor report the registration stale, but setup refuses that client, so
selecting it failed every other client's maintenance. The registration
inspection now carries the setup blocker, and maintenance lists that
client with its reason instead of selecting it.

* refactor(setup): read fx's private-profile host through HOST_PLATFORM

The fx private-profile mode checks and permissions describe the host REA runs
on, so they take it from the host-platform owner instead of reading
process.platform (refused by the ratchet from #10911).

* feat(setup): manage Goose registrations across its configuration layers (#10715)

* feat(setup): manage Goose registrations across its configuration layers

Goose becomes a client-table row, so doctor, update and uninstall see
the registration rea mcp add wrote, and setup offers Goose when its user
file or system file exists. Goose loads its system file and
GOOSE_ADDITIONAL_CONFIG_FILES beneath the user file and overlays each
extension one field deep; doctor now reports that effective
registration, while setup, update and uninstall change only the user
file. Doctor also parses Goose's cmd launcher instead of reporting it
invalid.

* fix(setup): keep Goose's layered environment and load order through setup and uninstall

Address review: read Goose's env alias and apply requested settings over envs; keep an inherited lower envs map instead of masking it with an empty default; keep each layer's last load so a repeated user file keeps its precedence; split GOOSE_ADDITIONAL_CONFIG_FILES with Windows quoting; validate only the effective environment across read-only layers; refuse uninstall while a read-only layer keeps REA enabled; and clear Goose's location variables in tests.

* fix(setup): apply requested Goose settings over the inherited environment

* fix(setup): leave lower-layer Goose settings in force and read admin layers read-only

Setup no longer writes its default timeout, enabled, name or description into Goose's user entry when only a lower layer declares that setting, so the inherited value keeps applying and a repeat setup stays current. Uninstall reads Goose's read-only lower layers where Goose reads them, without the write target's ownership check, so an administrator-owned system file no longer blocks removal. The client table accepts an injected Goose system-config path so tests no longer read or skip on the host's /etc/goose/config.yaml; adds a shadowed-invalid-lower-layer regression.

* fix(setup): keep an inherited Goose env alias's spelling when writing the user entry

Goose overlays each extension field separately, so writing envs into the user file beside a lower layer's env alias left both in force, which readers reject as ambiguous. Setup now writes the user map under the alias a lower layer declares, and mcp add neither adds a default envs map beside an inherited alias nor renames a user alias the lower layer shares.

* test(setup): inject Goose's system layer into mcp add selection

resolveMcpRegistrationClients accepts the caller's system configuration paths, so the Goose layers test no longer reads the host's /etc/goose/config.yaml.

* fix(setup): report REA's Goose registration that only a read-only layer defines

* test(setup): pass an isolated Goose system path through update maintenance and the mcp add table

* fix(setup): judge Goose uninstall by the merged entry and stop on an unreadable lower layer

* fix(setup): select Goose's env alias by presence so a null alias stays malformed

* fix(setup): use the shared record predicate for Goose's layered merge after #10588

* feat(setup): give Kilo a client-table row with an async layered location (#10823)

* feat(setup): give Kilo a client-table row with an async layered location

The client table gains a layeredLocation hook and resolveSupportedClients, which awaits it. Kilo's row resolves its user-scope layers through the same owner rea mcp add uses (KiloClientLocation), so both pick the same write target; the synchronous row keeps kilo.json in Kilo's config root with every candidate layer. The table refuses a relative KILO_CONFIG, KILO_CONFIG_DIR or XDG_CONFIG_HOME because Kilo's working directory is unknown.

Refs #7181

* fix(setup): treat every folder Kilo reads as evidence that it is installed

* fix(setup): normalize Kilo's absolute table paths and parse its command array

* feat(setup): resolve the client table's layered locations in setup, doctor, update and uninstall (#10832)

SetupHost (detection and the selectable table), ClientRegistrationStatus, uninstall, doctor's selected-registration environment and the mcp add catalog now read resolveSupportedClients, so each sees the Kilo layer Kilo writes rather than the synchronous default.

Refs #7181

* docs(adr): record the one-client-table decision for setup and mcp add

* fix(setup): refuse to read a client row whose location is unresolved

Doctor's selected-client settings read a Kilo row whose relative
KILO_CONFIG left only path evidence, so it inspected a file relative to
REA's folder. The shared configuration reader now refuses such a row,
so every reader reports the registration as unreadable.

* docs(adr): name the row's layeredLocation hook

* feat(setup): read KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT as Kilo's top read-only layer (#10851)

* feat(setup): read KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT as Kilo's top read-only layer

* fix(setup): refuse a Kilo uninstall that would expose or keep another layer's rea entry (#10852)

* fix(setup): recheck KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT at write time and name it in doctor's recovery

* refactor(mcp): register Kilo through its table row and remove the registration-only catalog kind (#10862)

* refactor(mcp): register Kilo through its table row and remove the registration-only catalog kind

* refactor(mcp): resolve user-scope targets in the catalog so location modules never import the client table

* test(setup): cover Kilo's KILO_CONFIG, home-folder and inline-only layers

* fix(setup): report REA's Kilo entry that only KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT sets during uninstall

Doctor reports a registration that KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT alone defines, but
uninstall found no file entry and reported Kilo as skipped. Uninstall now
reports it once as failed and names the variable to edit.

* docs(adr): record Kilo's inline layer in the client-table decision

* fix(setup): compare Windows environment names without case when a higher layer overrides REA's entry

Kilo's inline-layer check and Gemini's system-override check compared
environment maps by exact key, so an equal Path beside PATH on Windows was
reported as an override and setup refused the client. Both compare the
entry as the client launches it.

* fix(update): leave a stale Kilo registration KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT sets out of maintenance

Setup refuses a refresh the inline layer would override, and one refused
client failed every other client's maintenance. The registration inspection
now names the inline layer as the setup blocker of a stale entry, and
maintenance reports Kilo with that recovery instead of selecting it.

* fix(setup): refuse relative JUNIE_HOME and Cline CLI overrides like the other client roots (#10909)

* fix(setup): refuse relative JUNIE_HOME and Cline CLI overrides like the other client roots

* fix(setup): refuse Windows client paths without a drive that follow the client's current drive

* fix(update): select maintenance clients through setup's own refresh refusal check

Maintenance predicted setup's refusal with its own rule: any inline rea entry
blocked a stale registration, while an aligned one was never checked. A
harmless KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT entry (enabled: true) kept a stale Kilo launcher
pinned, and an inline value setup would not write (an extra environment
variable) let an aligned Kilo registration block every client's maintenance.

Setup's refusal checks (client policy, then the inline override comparison of
the entry it would write) now live in one reader that setup's alignment check
and maintenance share. Maintenance asks it for every owned enabled candidate
and reports a refused client with setup's remediation and its real state.

* fix(update): keep failed refresh-check reads owned by the supplied maintenance scope

clientRefreshRefusal read the client's layers, target file and policy without
the caller's resource scope, so a close that failed during those reads threw a
cleanup failure no scope retained; maintenance then reported it as text and
the scope's close could not retry the descriptor. The refresh reader now takes
the scope and passes it to every read.

* fix(setup): take the Kilo layer readers' default host from HOST_PLATFORM and the shared record predicate

After rebasing on main (#10911, #10588): the new inlineRegistrationOverride and
resolveSupportedClients defaults read the running host through the
host-platform owner, and the layered launcher merge uses isRecord.

* fix(update): keep an unreadable layer's reason in the refresh refusal check

readClientRefresh returned undefined for an unreadable or malformed layer, so
clientRefreshRefusal reported no refusal and maintenance selected a client
whose setup preflight then failed. The reader returns the typed file failure,
and the refusal check reports its detail like setup's preflight does.

* fix(setup): count REA's entry in KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT as Kilo lifecycle evidence

Doctor, update and uninstall inspected a client only when one of its folders
existed, so a registration set only by KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT was skipped. A
read-only inline layer that sets REA's entry is now evidence on its own.

* fix(update): report a client whose only conflict is a discovered provider path as needing setup

* fix(update): match discovered settings by the platform's environment identity

* fix(update): preflight maintenance with setup's write-target checks and treat discovered inline paths as unknown
