commits.body:
refactor(adb): report a pulled file's digest failure from its own type (#10848)

* fix(pcap): report a refused tool launch as an unavailable tool

When a capture read's tool launch was refused with EPERM, pcap reported it
as unreadable tool output (AnalysisProtocolError) instead of an unavailable
tool. Pcap also never told "not executable" apart from "missing".

Add classifyLaunchFailure in src/process as the one owner of which spawn
errnos mean missing (ENOENT, ENOTDIR) and which mean present but not
executable (EACCES, EPERM, ENOEXEC, EISDIR). Pcap, apktool and gdb used three
different errno lists; all three now use it.

* refactor(process): classify owned command outcomes through one owner

Add ProviderOutcome, read once from the supervisor's facts, and classifyProviderOutcome, the one mapping from an outcome to a typed error. Migrate pcap and the shared artifact producer command failure (TShark, sigrok). Add the rea/provider-failure-classifier lint rule with a shrink-only baseline of per-site (cause: unknown) => AnalysisError functions.

* refactor(process): classify Java and adb launch refusals with the shared owner (#10598)

The Ghidra and JADX Java probes and adb's version probe now take
missing-versus-not-executable from classifyLaunchFailure instead of their
own errno checks. ELOOP and ENAMETOOLONG join the owner's missing set, so
adb keeps its existing classification and both Java probes now treat a
non-directory path component as a missing runtime.

* fix(pcap): preserve command launch attribution

* test(pcap): expect an unknown failing stage when a limited capture tool exits unsuccessfully

* refactor(process): classify owned command outcomes through one owner

Add ProviderOutcome, read once from the supervisor's facts, and classifyProviderOutcome, the one mapping from an outcome to a typed error. Migrate pcap and the shared artifact producer command failure (TShark, sigrok). Add the rea/provider-failure-classifier lint rule with a shrink-only baseline of per-site (cause: unknown) => AnalysisError functions.

* test(lint): cover baselined files in the provider-failure classifier rule

* fix(apktool): report the decoder JVM's heap exhaustion as memory, not a target refusal

The supervisor now watches for a managed runtime's out-of-memory report while output streams (JVM java.lang.OutOfMemoryError, V8 'JavaScript heap out of memory'), so a retention budget cannot hide it. ProviderOutcome gains a runtime-exhausted kind and classifyProviderOutcome maps it once. Apktool decode opts in and moves to the shared classifier; Ghidra's single-purpose output token becomes the JVM runtime option and its area matching reuses the shared table.

* fix(process): keep the runtime's out-of-memory report on the memory error it supports

* fix(pcap): attribute a limited capture's exit through the prlimit wrapper

* fix(process): keep a shortened out-of-memory line marked as shortened

* fix(process): identify the refused executable for every launcher shape

Name the executable on errnos Node throws synchronously from spawn
(ENOEXEC, ENOTDIR, ...) and read the Windows native launcher's
executable-launch constraint, so pcap attributes those refusals to the
selected tool or limiter instead of an unknown stage.

* test(pcap): prove synchronous launch naming with ENOTDIR on every POSIX host

* fix(apktool): advise the JVM limit that governs the reported memory area

* fix(ghidra): read the supervisor's parsed OOM area instead of reparsing lines

* fix(sqlite,capture): read V8 heap exhaustion from streamed output, not retained stderr (#10724)

The SQLite worker and the Node capture decoders now declare runtime: "v8", so the supervisor observes V8's heap report as output streams. Both classifiers read the runtime-exhausted outcome instead of matching retained stderr, so a report beyond the retention budget, or one whose process then overflowed its output budget, is still reported as memory exhaustion.

* refactor(evm): classify EVMole worker outcomes through the shared provider classifier (#10716)

* refactor(evm): classify EVMole worker outcomes through the shared provider classifier

The EVMole worker's cancellation, deadline, output budget and CPU/file-size signals now go through classifyProviderOutcome; only the prlimit launch refusal and the reserved EFBIG exit remain in its dialect. The worker is opted into V8 exhaustion scanning so a heap report names its fixed 256 MiB heap. providerOutcomeOf now reads a launch refusal only from a spawn errno, so a private-storage or carrier read errno is no longer reported as a limiter launch failure.

* fix(evm): keep a stream failure's exit status and update Linux worker expectations

* refactor(process): read launch refusals through the launcher identity owner

* refactor(wasm): classify WABT command outcomes through the shared provider classifier (#10727)

* refactor(wasm): classify WABT command outcomes through the shared provider classifier

WABT's cancellation, command deadline, output budget, and inherited-limit signals now go through classifyProviderOutcome; its dialect keeps only the configuration-probe and launch-refusal unavailability and the unclassified-exit output error. A tool ended by SIGXCPU/SIGXFSZ or the memory limit is now a resource constraint instead of an output error, and a refused launch in the producer phase is reported as unavailable. The shared timeout context gains the analysis setting that selected the deadline, and the output-limit context may name its exceeded budget.

* fix(wasm): keep setup guidance when a WABT version probe's output cannot be collected

* refactor(providers): classify raw provider failures through one owner

* refactor(process): build classified cancellations with cancelledBy and the carried caller reason

* chore(lint): count runOwned's close-failure mapper from main in the classifier baseline

* fix(process): carry the runtime's exhaustion report on every memory error that claims it

SQLite and historical-capture memory errors recognised a streamed V8 heap report but dropped it, so a report outside retained output reached callers without its source line or omission flags. One projection, runtimeExhaustionReport, now owns that shape for the shared classifier and both consumers. Also lowers the EVMole and WABT cancellation-constructor baselines.

* fix(process): keep the provider's recovery for a native-thread exhaustion report

The shared classifier replaced the provider-supplied recovery with generic capacity advice whenever the JVM reported it could not create a native thread, dropping Apktool's launcher guidance and flipping retryable to true. The provider's recovery now wins; the capacity advice remains the fallback for providers that supply none.

* refactor(pwntools): classify pwntools failures through the shared provider classifier (#10782)

* refactor(pwntools): classify pwntools failures through the shared provider classifier

pwntools' per-site classifier is replaced by pwntoolsFailureDialect for classifyProviderFailure. Command outcomes go through classifyProviderOutcome, launch refusals through launcherRefusalOf instead of a 'spawn ' syscall prefix check, the input limit through the file dialect's fileSize, and the cleanup report through commandCleanup. The shared read cancellation now carries the reader's partial observation, and resource-signal reports accept provider detail.

* fix(pwntools): report a failed command's output once and expect resource_constraint for overflow

The shared outcome owner already attaches the command's output as capturedOutput, so the pwntools adapter fallback no longer copies the same text into diagnostics.stdout, diagnostics.stderr and diagnostics.captured_output; diagnostics keep the exit facts. Update the overflow expectations the dialect migration missed (layout provider cleanup and over-budget rows, pwntools cleanup) to resource_constraint.

* refactor(wasm): leave WABT cancellation to the shared owners

WabtFailures matched any Error named AbortError as a cancellation. No WABT path produces one: reads, path checks and owned commands report cancellation as ArtifactReaderFailure or OwnedCommandFailure, which classifyProviderFailure and classifyProviderOutcome already classify with the caller's reason. The provider's two signal checks now build the cancellation with cancelledBy. Lowers the AnalysisCancelledError constructor baseline for both WABT files to zero.

* fix(wasm): report a cancelled snapshot write as the caller's cancellation

The private snapshot write passed the caller's signal to Node's writeFile, whose abort envelope reached the dialect's unclassified output failure once the name-based AbortError guess was removed. The write now turns the envelope carrying its own signal's reason into cancelledBy at the producer.

* refactor(firmware): classify firmware failures through the shared provider classifier (#10810)

Firmware producers now report their own deadline expiry: the start check, the output inventory and launcher admission throw the phase timeout where they observe the abort, and a read the phase signal cancelled reports it through the dialect's interruption. The classifier no longer rereads a cancellation's reason as a timeout. A new readCleanup hook keeps firmware's cleanup report shape.

* refactor(captures): classify TShark, sigrok and pcap failures through the shared provider classifier

TsharkCaptureProvider and SigrokRecordingProvider replace #failure with a dialect, and PcapProvider replaces analysisFailure and the tool-identity classifier. ArtifactAnalysisResources exposes its command context and a readCleanupFailure composer so the readCleanup hook keeps each provider's cleanup report shape.

* refactor(jeb): classify JEB failures through the shared provider classifier

JEB's raw MCP failures go through classifyProviderFailure with a JEB dialect;
a typed attribution step reports a shared phase's failure under the REA
operation. Each MCP phase deadline now reports its own interruption when it
aborts, deciding a cancellation's owner from the caller's own signal instead
of comparing abort reasons. A refusal carrying the JVM's OutOfMemoryError
report becomes a resource constraint naming JEB's Java heap.

* fix(jeb): advise the JVM limit that governs the reported memory area

* refactor(ghidra): classify Ghidra failures through the shared provider classifier

PSP extension inspection reports through classifyProviderFailure with a
Ghidra dialect. The startup deadline decides at abort time whether the shared
startup owner closed it, so Ghidra and Hopper no longer compare the abort
reason with the owner's sentinel, and Ghidra's startup no longer compares a
producer cancellation's reason with the deadline's. Three helpers that only
construct one error kind now name that kind instead of AnalysisError.

* test(ghidra): pin the aborted startup deadline over a producer cancellation

* refactor(kuna): classify Kuna failures through the shared provider classifier

Session operations, the workspace copy and the project export report raw
failures through classifyProviderFailure with Kuna dialects; the copy and
export keep their cleanup report shapes through the readCleanup hook.

producer cancellation's reason with the deadline's. Three helpers that only

commits.body:
refactor(ida): let IDA close failures read the session's later close (#10811)

* refactor(errors): read cleanup completion from dependencies instead of pushing it to dependents

AnalysisError.cleanupIncomplete becomes a getter over the error's own unresolved state and its bound dependencies. The WeakRef dependents graph and resolveCleanup's push propagation are removed, and subclasses mark their initial state through markCleanupIncomplete instead of overriding a public mutable field.

* fix(errors): settle bound dependencies before binding more

A composite whose dependencies had released but whose status was never read
stayed incomplete when a later dependency was bound.

* refactor(errors): let errors read a lease group's release instead of resolving them (#10759)

AnalysisCleanupLeaseGroup no longer calls resolveCleanup() on its error.
The error holds the group as a release claim and reads cleanupReleased when
asked, so completion follows the lease owner without a push.

* chore(verify): count resolveCleanup and bindCleanupDependencies calls so they only shrink (#10763)

* refactor(errors): let errors read a lease group's release instead of resolving them

AnalysisCleanupLeaseGroup no longer calls resolveCleanup() on its error.
The error holds the group as a release claim and reads cleanupReleased when
asked, so completion follows the lease owner without a push.

* chore(verify): count resolveCleanup and bindCleanupDependencies calls so they only shrink

* refactor(process): let worker cleanup errors read their root epoch's release

OwnedWorkerRuntime's root epoch is now an AnalysisCleanupReleaseClaim. Errors bound to it read its release when asked instead of the epoch pushing resolveCleanup() through weak references, and a runtime without a retained root binds an already-released owner. Removes the OwnedWorkerCleanupFailure structural type and four resolveCleanup() pushes; the counted baseline shrinks accordingly.

* refactor(pcap): let pcap cleanup errors read command and snapshot release (#10792)

Retained pcap commands, retained snapshot failures and snapshot completion descriptors now own their release and errors read it: commands and snapshot failures implement AnalysisCleanupReleaseClaim, and a failed completion-descriptor close is retried through an AnalysisCleanupLease bound to its error. Removes four resolveCleanup() pushes; the counted baseline shrinks accordingly.

* refactor(process): let Darwin helper cleanup errors read their owner's release

Darwin helper cache and run-token reader root cleanup now record an AnalysisCleanupRelease that every failure reports; a successful retry confirms it. Replaces the first-failure anchor that later failures depended on and the resolveCleanup() push. Removes two resolveCleanup() and two bindCleanupDependencies() calls; both counted baselines shrink.

* refactor(ghidra): let Ghidra cleanup errors read the client's and checkpoint's release

GhidraClient and GhidraCheckpoint bind each cleanup failure to an AnalysisCleanupRelease and confirm it when a later close or retry releases everything, instead of keeping a set of failures and pushing resolveCleanup() to each. Removes two resolveCleanup() calls; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(process): let debugger session cleanup errors read a confirmed stop

OwnedDebuggerSessionRegistry binds each retained gdb or rizin cleanup failure to the session's AnalysisCleanupRelease and confirms it when a stop is confirmed, keeping the latest failure for retry reporting, instead of pushing resolveCleanup() to a set of failures. Removes one resolveCleanup() call; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(process): drop the debugger registry's unused closeOperation option

Returning the latest retained failure removed the last reader of closeOperation; remove the option and the values gdb and rizin supplied.

* refactor(server): let environment shutdown errors read a successful close

serveEnvironment binds each shutdown failure to an AnalysisCleanupRelease that a later successful close confirms, instead of pushing resolveCleanup() to a set of failures. The state-file retry test now also requires the earlier report to read the release. Removes one resolveCleanup() call; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(desktop): release retained screen-judge cleanup through its lease

Each retained judge or screenshot cleanup owner is wrapped in an AnalysisCleanupLease bound to its failure; close() releases the lease, which records the release the failure reads, instead of closing the owner and pushing resolveCleanup(). Removes one resolveCleanup() call; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(ida): let IDA close failures read the session's later close

IdaSessionClient's close failure binds an owner that is both its resource owner and its release claim, read from the client's closed state, instead of keeping weak references and pushing resolveCleanup() after a successful retry. Removes one resolveCleanup() call; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(javascript): let source-map codec cleanup errors read a later close (#10814)

* refactor(javascript): let source-map codec cleanup errors read a later close

OwnedCodec binds each close failure to an AnalysisCleanupRelease that a later successful close confirms, replacing the first-failure anchor that later failures depended on and the resolveCleanup() push. Removes one resolveCleanup() and one bindCleanupDependencies() call; both counted baselines shrink.

* refactor(cutter): let pending Cutter command errors read the completion receipt (#10815)

* refactor(cutter): let pending Cutter command errors read the completion receipt

Each pending Cutter command keeps an AnalysisCleanupRelease bound to its timeout failure; the producer's terminal completion receipt confirms it instead of pushing resolveCleanup(). Removes one resolveCleanup() call; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(application): let provider candidate cleanup errors read the candidate's close (#10817)

* refactor(application): let provider candidate cleanup errors read the candidate's close

AnalysisProviderRegistry keeps one AnalysisCleanupRelease per candidate whose resource close is unconfirmed; failures bind to it and a later confirmed close confirms it, instead of pushing resolveCleanup() to a set of failures. Removes one resolveCleanup() call; the counted baseline shrinks.

* fix(errors): bind a cleanup release claim to an error at most once

AnalysisError kept release claims in an array, so a provider whose retried close returned the same error bound the same claim again on every retry and each cleanupIncomplete read scanned the duplicates. Keep the claims in a set.

* refactor(application): let reverse-tool cleanup errors read a verified stop (#10819)

* refactor(application): let reverse-tool cleanup errors read a verified stop

Each retained provider process group in ReverseEngineeringService keeps an AnalysisCleanupRelease; its command and retry failures bind to it and a later verified stop confirms it, instead of collecting failures and pushing resolveCleanup(). Removes one resolveCleanup() call; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(sqlite): let SQLite worker and root cleanup errors read their release (#10821)

Each retained SQLite snapshot cleanup records an AnalysisCleanupRelease for its worker and for its runtime root; the resource failures bind to them and a verified stop or root removal confirms them, instead of pushing resolveCleanup(). Composite failures keep reading those resource failures. Removes two resolveCleanup() calls; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(application): let JADX and session close failures read their owner's release (#10854)

* refactor(android): let JADX cleanup errors read their retained cleanup's release

Each retained JADX cleanup records an AnalysisCleanupRelease for the admission failure's descriptor owners and one for the whole retained cleanup. The admission failure and every error the cleanup reports bind to them, and a confirmed close confirms them, instead of pushing resolveCleanup() through WeakRefs to reported errors. Removes two resolveCleanup() calls; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(application): let session close failures read the client's later close

A retained session cleanup records an AnalysisCleanupRelease; unowned cleanup failures the client's close reported bind to it and the successful close confirms it, instead of the session collecting them and pushing resolveCleanup(). Failures that already follow their own owner keep reading it. Adds a regression for an unowned close failure. Removes one resolveCleanup() call; the counted baseline shrinks.

commits.subject: refactor(browser): parse Runtime and Debugger events once by registered schemas (#10742)
commits.body:
refactor(browser): parse Runtime and Debugger events once by registered schemas (#10742)

* refactor(browser): parse frame lifecycle events once by a registered event schema

CdpConnection admits each event through protocol/CdpEvents.ts, which parses
the five Page frame lifecycle events once into identity facts plus a frame
URL observation, like a frame-tree node. Screenshot, page capture, the
observation timeline, WebMCP, Electron inspection and the execution window
read those facts instead of re-parsing the raw payload; CdpFrameFacts no
longer carries the raw source record. Playwright CDP session subscriptions
name an event from Playwright's protocol table, and an architecture guard
counts the remaining raw event payload reads so they can only shrink.

* refactor(browser): parse Runtime and Debugger events once by registered schemas

Register Debugger.scriptParsed, Debugger.scriptFailedToParse,
Runtime.executionContextCreated, Runtime.executionContextDestroyed and
Runtime.consoleAPICalled. Script and context payloads carry both the
tolerant facts passive capture uses and the active runtime's strict
declaration, derived from one parse, plus the declaration's byte size for
the runtime retention budget. Page capture, Electron script capture, the
V8 Inspector provider and the runtime source inventory now read the
registered payload. The cdp-raw-event-params baseline drops from 20 to 7.

* refactor(browser): admit transport events through the registered-event owner

Remove the unused cdpFrameUrl wrapper; its fragment cases now exercise
observeCdpFrameUrl. Add a connection-level test that two subscribers share
one parsed payload and the raw params.

* fix(browser): report an unserializable event declaration's size instead of throwing

JSON.stringify can throw on a declaration JSON.parse accepted (nesting
deeper than the serializer's stack). The registry sized script and context
declarations inside the connection's WebSocket callback, so such an event
escaped as an uncaught exception. The size is now a Result; the runtime
source inventory raises the failure inside its own catch, as before.

* refactor(browser): parse Network events once by registered schemas (#10743)

* refactor(browser): parse Network events once by registered schemas

Register Network.requestWillBeSent, responseReceived, loadingFinished,
loadingFailed, webSocketCreated and webSocketFrameSent/Received. The
request payload carries the tolerant facts page capture and the timeline
read plus the active runtime's strict declaration. Page capture's network
and WebSocket handlers, the timeline's request tracking and the runtime
request inventory now read the registered payload. The
cdp-raw-event-params baseline drops from 7 to 5.

* refactor(browser): drop payload helpers the capture handlers no longer use

* refactor(browser): read every CDP event payload through the registry (#10745)

* refactor(browser): read every CDP event payload through the registry

Register Target.attachedToTarget, Target.detachedFromTarget,
Page.lifecycleEvent and WebMCP.toolsAdded/toolsRemoved, and carry a
requested navigation's reason and a commit's transition type in the
frame-event payload. The timeline no longer threads raw params into its
entries: each entry receives its timestamp, frame and loader identity
explicitly. WebMCP discovery, the service-worker policy blocker and the
target-event matcher read the registered payload. With no raw reads left,
the cdp-raw-event-params guard is enforced at zero instead of counted.

* refactor(browser): drop raw payload helpers the timeline and worker blocker no longer use

* refactor(browser): type Playwright CDP session events by the registry (#10751)

PlaywrightCdpSession.on subscribes only to registered events and hands
the listener the payload parsed by its registered schema, returning the
unsubscribe function. Private storage seeding reads registered payloads,
including the events of non-flat child sessions, and applies its strict
seeding policy to the parsed facts. Its local attach, detach, nested
message and pause schemas and the storage-only script/context schemas are
removed; Debugger.paused, Runtime.executionContextsCleared and
Target.receivedMessageFromTarget join the registry.

* test(browser): admit fake policy events through the event registry

The service-worker policy now reads event.registered, but the PlaywrightScenarioSession fake connection delivered raw events, so three detached-target tests never reached the policy. The fake now admits each event with receiveCdpEvent as CdpConnection does.

* fix(browser): fail the CDP session closed when an event listener throws (#10758)

* fix(browser): fail the CDP session closed when an event listener throws

An exception from a CDP event subscriber escaped CdpTransportCore's socket message callback uncaught (for example the service-worker blocker's protocol_error on a Target event without a sessionId). The transport now stops delivery, fails the connection as a protocol error whose cause is the listener's exception, rejects pending and later commands with it, and notifies protocol-failure subscribers. The Playwright CDP session relay applies the same rule to its event listeners.

* fix(browser): report a failed service-worker policy connection at the next policy check

The policy's event listener rejects a malformed Target event, which now fails its connection. With no policy command pending, nothing reported it and later iframe targets went unprotected. The policy records its connection's protocol failure and assertBlocked, run before each scenario step, rethrows it.

* fix(browser): keep cleanup commands available after a listener failure

A listener failure no longer marks the wire as broken. The transport still rejects pending commands, notifies protocol-failure subscribers, stops delivering events and refuses reuse, but it keeps reading replies and admits commands sent in cleanup grace. The service-worker policy can then remove its init scripts, restore the main realm, detach and release its socket. Wire-level protocol errors still refuse every later command. The PlaywrightScenarioSession policy fake gains onProtocolFailure, which the policy now subscribes to.

* refactor(browser): keep raw CDP event payloads out of the received event (#10764)

* refactor(browser): keep raw CDP event payloads out of the received event

CdpReceivedEvent and CdpTransportEvent no longer carry params: receiveCdpEvent hands the raw payload only to the registered schema, so a subscriber cannot read it by property access, destructuring or computed keys. This supersedes the event.params text guard in architecture-guards, which is removed.

* refactor(browser): read registered event payloads in the JavaScript verifiers

The runtime, storage and URL-userinfo verifiers subscribe to CdpConnection, which no longer hands subscribers raw params. They now read event.registered. A test scans every scripts/ onEvent callback for raw payload reads, since the TypeScript check does not cover them. The storage verifier's pause trace records a malformed pause instead of the unregistered reason member.

* refactor(browser): track the timeline's main frame with the document tracker (#10779)

TimelineCapture kept its own mutable main frame id and replaced it on a root replacement. It now holds the CdpDocumentTracker that CdpTargetSession owns and observes the replacement document through it; every main-frame check (lifecycle, navigation, document request, redirect) reads the tracker's current frame. A characterization test pins that the replaced root's lifecycle events are no longer recorded.

* refactor(browser): select CDP events only by their registered name (#10829)

CdpReceivedEvent carried the wire method as a plain string, so a subscriber
could compare it with a misspelt or unregistered name and the check compiled
but never matched. Three owners selected Inspector.targetCrashed, an
unregistered event, that way.

Register Inspector.targetCrashed and drop the wire method from the received
event. Subscribers select events by registered.method, whose type is the
registered event names. The capture coverage start keeps reading the
wire domain, now the event's domain field.

* fix(browser): retire a policy child session that CDP reports gone

After a listener failure the connection stops delivering events, so an
iframe's Target.detachedFromTarget never retires its policy target. Cleanup
then sent Page.removeScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument to the dead session,
kept the stale child, and every retry failed before detaching the root.

The service-worker policy owner now treats CDP's session-not-found
rejection as proof that the child is gone and retires it. The classifier
moves from CdpTargetSession to CdpCommandRejection, its owner, and the
target-session detach path uses the same one.

* refactor(browser): route target events through one session owner (#10835)

* refactor(browser): route target events through one session owner

Page capture, WebMCP discovery, screenshot capture and the runtime sources
each compared the envelope session ID themselves, while the observation
window and execution collection used cdpTargetEventMatches, which also
routes the root Target.detachedFromTarget that names the target's session.

onCdpTargetEvent in CdpTargetEvents.ts now subscribes every target consumer
with that one rule; the matcher is private and the per-subscriber
comparisons are removed. Electron inspection keeps its own filter while
its capture isolation awaits a maintainer decision.

* fix(browser): report WebMCP subframe tools whose document is unverified (#10839)

* fix(browser): report WebMCP subframe tools whose document is unverified

A committed subframe navigation kept the frame's tools silently when CDP
reported no loader at the same URL, and removed them on any URL change even
when the loader proved the same document.

Each frame now carries a CdpDocumentTracker, the session's document
identity owner. Only a proven change removes the frame's tools. An unknown
comparison keeps them visible, marks webmcp_tools attach-limited and names
the frames whose document identity could not be established.

* test(browser): prove an unverified live subframe limits WebMCP coverage

* fix(browser): key a WebMCP registration by its frame and tool name

A subframe tool kept across a committed navigation that changed the URL
but not the loader was stored under a key built from the old URL, so a
later toolsAdded for the same frame and name added a second entry.
Registrations are now keyed by frame and name; tool_key still records the
registering frame URL.

* test(browser): deliver fake CDP events through the transport's admission (#10840)

Event fakes each rebuilt the received event: CdpAgentHints typed its
listeners as raw wire events behind an unknown cast, and the Electron,
scenario-session and routing tests each wrapped receiveCdpEvent by hand.

fakeCdpEvents (tests/fixtures) is a CdpConnection.onEvent fake whose emit
admits each raw event with receiveCdpEvent and the wire byte count, so a
change to the received event shape fails at the fake instead of silently
not exercising subscribers.

* refactor(browser): own the selected page generation in one target document tracker (#10860)

* refactor(browser): own the selected page generation in one target document tracker

Page capture, screenshot, the observation window, the runtime session and
the execution window each built a document tracker or rule of their own
from root-frame navigation events. CdpTargetDocument now follows the target
session's root-frame events and the frame-tree replies its consumers read,
classifies root identity once, and reports each navigation to consumers
that decide only what it means for their evidence.

* fix(browser): report a lost scenario policy connection before the next step (#10864)

* fix(browser): report a lost scenario policy connection before the next step

The service-worker policy recorded only protocol failures. When its CDP
socket closed or its page session detached, later documents lost the
blocking script, but the scenario learned of it only when a frame check
found an unprotected realm. The owner now records the disconnect or
detach when CDP reports it; the next policy check and the next step's
action report it first.

* fix(browser): refuse an unregistered CDP command before it reaches the browser (#10868)

JavaScript verifiers can name any command, and the send owners refused an
unregistered one only when its reply arrived, after the browser had acted
on it. CdpConnection and the Playwright session now refuse the name before
sending, and the Playwright session refuses an unregistered event name
instead of subscribing to events no listener receives. The verifier text
scan stays as an early warning and documents what it cannot see.

* fix(browser): keep a proven root change and the loaderless selection's uncertainty

Two review findings on the target document owner. A root event naming
another frame with a malformed loader set `changed` but was announced as
unidentified, so the execution window failed with protocol_error and
dropped what it had collected; the owner now announces it as the proven
change it is. The runtime session compared each frame-tree reply with the
tracker's current document, which can learn a loader from an event, so a
loaderless selection followed by an event and a reply with that loader
compared as same; it now compares the reply with the selected document
through the owner, and reports target_changed as before.

* test(browser): refuse the next scenario step after the policy session detaches

* refactor(browser): read WebMCP document identity from the target document owner (#10884)

* refactor(browser): read WebMCP document identity from the target document owner

WebMCP discovery compared the first and last frame-tree roots itself and
kept a document tracker per subframe. CdpTargetDocument now follows the
selected root and each committed subframe for it: the final frame tree
feeds the owner, a root change proven by a navigation event during
discovery is target_changed as in page capture, and a subframe whose
committed document changed loses its tools. A subframe navigation without
a loader still keeps the tools and reports them as unverified.

* fix(browser): start a subframe first seen within its document with an unknown loader

A subframe absent from the initial frame tree and first seen through Page.navigatedWithinDocument had no document tracker, so a later commit started a fresh one and the tools it registered meanwhile lost the unverified-document limitation. The owner now starts such a subframe with an unknown loader.

* fix(browser): refuse a verifier's unregistered CDP event name at subscription (#10885)

JavaScript verifiers subscribed to every event with CdpConnection.onEvent
and compared registered.method with a string literal. A misspelt or
unregistered name never matched and the verifier waited until its timeout.
CdpConnection.onRegisteredEvent now takes one event name, refuses an
unregistered one before subscribing (the same registry check the Playwright
session applies), and hands the listener only that event's registered
parse. The verifiers subscribe only through it, and the evaluation test
rejects a raw onEvent subscription in scripts.

* fix(browser): keep subframe documents by frame and loader without their URLs

refactor(desktop): let build-computer and agentenv cleanup errors read their owner's release (#10855)

* refactor(errors): read cleanup completion from dependencies instead of pushing it to dependents

AnalysisError.cleanupIncomplete becomes a getter over the error's own unresolved state and its bound dependencies. The WeakRef dependents graph and resolveCleanup's push propagation are removed, and subclasses mark their initial state through markCleanupIncomplete instead of overriding a public mutable field.

* fix(errors): settle bound dependencies before binding more

A composite whose dependencies had released but whose status was never read
stayed incomplete when a later dependency was bound.

* refactor(errors): let errors read a lease group's release instead of resolving them (#10759)

AnalysisCleanupLeaseGroup no longer calls resolveCleanup() on its error.
The error holds the group as a release claim and reads cleanupReleased when
asked, so completion follows the lease owner without a push.

* chore(verify): count resolveCleanup and bindCleanupDependencies calls so they only shrink (#10763)

* refactor(errors): let errors read a lease group's release instead of resolving them

AnalysisCleanupLeaseGroup no longer calls resolveCleanup() on its error.
The error holds the group as a release claim and reads cleanupReleased when
asked, so completion follows the lease owner without a push.

* chore(verify): count resolveCleanup and bindCleanupDependencies calls so they only shrink

* refactor(process): let worker cleanup errors read their root epoch's release

OwnedWorkerRuntime's root epoch is now an AnalysisCleanupReleaseClaim. Errors bound to it read its release when asked instead of the epoch pushing resolveCleanup() through weak references, and a runtime without a retained root binds an already-released owner. Removes the OwnedWorkerCleanupFailure structural type and four resolveCleanup() pushes; the counted baseline shrinks accordingly.

* refactor(pcap): let pcap cleanup errors read command and snapshot release (#10792)

Retained pcap commands, retained snapshot failures and snapshot completion descriptors now own their release and errors read it: commands and snapshot failures implement AnalysisCleanupReleaseClaim, and a failed completion-descriptor close is retried through an AnalysisCleanupLease bound to its error. Removes four resolveCleanup() pushes; the counted baseline shrinks accordingly.

* refactor(process): let Darwin helper cleanup errors read their owner's release

Darwin helper cache and run-token reader root cleanup now record an AnalysisCleanupRelease that every failure reports; a successful retry confirms it. Replaces the first-failure anchor that later failures depended on and the resolveCleanup() push. Removes two resolveCleanup() and two bindCleanupDependencies() calls; both counted baselines shrink.

* refactor(ghidra): let Ghidra cleanup errors read the client's and checkpoint's release

GhidraClient and GhidraCheckpoint bind each cleanup failure to an AnalysisCleanupRelease and confirm it when a later close or retry releases everything, instead of keeping a set of failures and pushing resolveCleanup() to each. Removes two resolveCleanup() calls; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(process): let debugger session cleanup errors read a confirmed stop

OwnedDebuggerSessionRegistry binds each retained gdb or rizin cleanup failure to the session's AnalysisCleanupRelease and confirms it when a stop is confirmed, keeping the latest failure for retry reporting, instead of pushing resolveCleanup() to a set of failures. Removes one resolveCleanup() call; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(process): drop the debugger registry's unused closeOperation option

Returning the latest retained failure removed the last reader of closeOperation; remove the option and the values gdb and rizin supplied.

* refactor(server): let environment shutdown errors read a successful close

serveEnvironment binds each shutdown failure to an AnalysisCleanupRelease that a later successful close confirms, instead of pushing resolveCleanup() to a set of failures. The state-file retry test now also requires the earlier report to read the release. Removes one resolveCleanup() call; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(desktop): release retained screen-judge cleanup through its lease

Each retained judge or screenshot cleanup owner is wrapped in an AnalysisCleanupLease bound to its failure; close() releases the lease, which records the release the failure reads, instead of closing the owner and pushing resolveCleanup(). Removes one resolveCleanup() call; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(ida): let IDA close failures read the session's later close

IdaSessionClient's close failure binds an owner that is both its resource owner and its release claim, read from the client's closed state, instead of keeping weak references and pushing resolveCleanup() after a successful retry. Removes one resolveCleanup() call; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(javascript): let source-map codec cleanup errors read a later close (#10814)

* refactor(javascript): let source-map codec cleanup errors read a later close

OwnedCodec binds each close failure to an AnalysisCleanupRelease that a later successful close confirms, replacing the first-failure anchor that later failures depended on and the resolveCleanup() push. Removes one resolveCleanup() and one bindCleanupDependencies() call; both counted baselines shrink.

* refactor(cutter): let pending Cutter command errors read the completion receipt (#10815)

* refactor(application): let provider candidate cleanup errors read the candidate's close (#10817)

* refactor(application): let provider candidate cleanup errors read the candidate's close

AnalysisProviderRegistry keeps one AnalysisCleanupRelease per candidate whose resource close is unconfirmed; failures bind to it and a later confirmed close confirms it, instead of pushing resolveCleanup() to a set of failures. Removes one resolveCleanup() call; the counted baseline shrinks.

* fix(errors): bind a cleanup release claim to an error at most once

AnalysisError kept release claims in an array, so a provider whose retried close returned the same error bound the same claim again on every retry and each cleanupIncomplete read scanned the duplicates. Keep the claims in a set.

* refactor(application): let reverse-tool cleanup errors read a verified stop (#10819)

* refactor(application): let reverse-tool cleanup errors read a verified stop

Each retained provider process group in ReverseEngineeringService keeps an AnalysisCleanupRelease; its command and retry failures bind to it and a later verified stop confirms it, instead of collecting failures and pushing resolveCleanup(). Removes one resolveCleanup() call; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(sqlite): let SQLite worker and root cleanup errors read their release (#10821)

Each retained SQLite snapshot cleanup records an AnalysisCleanupRelease for its worker and for its runtime root; the resource failures bind to them and a verified stop or root removal confirms them, instead of pushing resolveCleanup(). Composite failures keep reading those resource failures. Removes two resolveCleanup() calls; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(android): let JADX cleanup errors read their retained cleanup's release

Each retained JADX cleanup records an AnalysisCleanupRelease for the admission failure's descriptor owners and one for the whole retained cleanup. The admission failure and every error the cleanup reports bind to them, and a confirmed close confirms them, instead of pushing resolveCleanup() through WeakRefs to reported errors. Removes two resolveCleanup() calls; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(application): let session close failures read the client's later close

A retained session cleanup records an AnalysisCleanupRelease; unowned cleanup failures the client's close reported bind to it and the successful close confirms it, instead of the session collecting them and pushing resolveCleanup(). Failures that already follow their own owner keep reading it. Adds a regression for an unowned close failure. Removes one resolveCleanup() call; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(desktop): let build-computer and agentenv cleanup errors read their owner's release

Build-computer teardown, retained task readers, remote reader folders and agentenv solve sandboxes each record an AnalysisCleanupRelease that their bound failures read; a verified teardown or stop confirms it instead of pushing resolveCleanup() through WeakRef sets. Long-run job failures read whether every job they name has confirmed its stop, so a failure naming two jobs no longer reads complete when only one stops (regression added). WeakRef sets kept only where late facts (completion receipts, reader views) are still retained as diagnostics. Removes six resolveCleanup() calls; the counted baseline shrinks.

* refactor(kuna): let source-map and Kuna cache cleanup errors read their owner's release (#10856)

* refactor(browser): let late source-map fetch errors read their response's release

A pending source-map fetch and a response cancellation each record an AnalysisCleanupRelease that their cancellation or deadline failure reads; releasing the late response or the reader lock confirms it instead of pushing resolveCleanup(). Removes two resolveCleanup() calls; the counted baseline shrinks.

Each retained Kuna resource owner (process, staging, hash descriptor, retired file) records a release that the errors reporting it read; an error completes once every owner it reports confirms, and retirement that moves staging to a retained file forwards the staging owner's release to the file's. Replaces the WeakRef report list, its pruning and the resolveCleanup() push. Removes one resolveCleanup() call; the counted baseline shrinks.

Re-attributing a failure whose source cleanup already completed now binds a claim reading that source's release instead of pushing resolveCleanup() onto the new error; a pending source is still bound as a dependency. Resources stay as history, as before. Removes one resolveCleanup() call; the counted baseline shrinks.

ProviderProcessSupervisor records an AnalysisCleanupRelease that a stop proving the process ended confirms. Native command and LLDB resolver cleanup markers bind to their supervisor's release, so a verified stop by either owner completes them, instead of each owner pushing resolveCleanup() onto the markers it tracks. Removes the last two resolveCleanup() calls outside the error base; the counted baseline is empty.

commits.subject: refactor(sqlite): classify worker-reply read failures through the shared provider classifier (#10849)
commits.body:
refactor(sqlite): classify worker-reply read failures through the shared provider classifier (#10849)

* fix(pcap): report a refused tool launch as an unavailable tool

When a capture read's tool launch was refused with EPERM, pcap reported it
as unreadable tool output (AnalysisProtocolError) instead of an unavailable
tool. Pcap also never told "not executable" apart from "missing".

Add classifyLaunchFailure in src/process as the one owner of which spawn
errnos mean missing (ENOENT, ENOTDIR) and which mean present but not
executable (EACCES, EPERM, ENOEXEC, EISDIR). Pcap, apktool and gdb used three
different errno lists; all three now use it.

* refactor(process): classify owned command outcomes through one owner

Add ProviderOutcome, read once from the supervisor's facts, and classifyProviderOutcome, the one mapping from an outcome to a typed error. Migrate pcap and the shared artifact producer command failure (TShark, sigrok). * refactor(process): classify Java and adb launch refusals with the shared owner (#10598)

The Ghidra and JADX Java probes and adb's version probe now take
missing-versus-not-executable from classifyLaunchFailure instead of their
own errno checks. ELOOP and ENAMETOOLONG join the owner's missing set, so
adb keeps its existing classification and both Java probes now treat a
non-directory path component as a missing runtime.

* fix(pcap): preserve command launch attribution

* fix(apktool): report the decoder JVM's heap exhaustion as memory, not a target refusal

The supervisor now watches for a managed runtime's out-of-memory report while output streams (JVM java.lang.OutOfMemoryError, V8 'JavaScript heap out of memory'), so a retention budget cannot hide it. ProviderOutcome gains a runtime-exhausted kind and classifyProviderOutcome maps it once. executable-launch constraint, so pcap attributes those refusals to the
selected tool or limiter instead of an unknown stage.

* test(pcap): prove synchronous launch naming with ENOTDIR on every POSIX host

* fix(ghidra): read the supervisor's parsed OOM area instead of reparsing lines

* fix(sqlite,capture): read V8 heap exhaustion from streamed output, not retained stderr (#10724)

The SQLite worker and the Node capture decoders now declare runtime: "v8", so the supervisor observes V8's heap report as output streams. Both classifiers read the runtime-exhausted outcome instead of matching retained stderr, so a report beyond the retention budget, or one whose process then overflowed its output budget, is still reported as memory exhaustion.

* refactor(evm): classify EVMole worker outcomes through the shared provider classifier (#10716)

* refactor(evm): classify EVMole worker outcomes through the shared provider classifier

The EVMole worker's cancellation, deadline, output budget and CPU/file-size signals now go through classifyProviderOutcome; only the prlimit launch refusal and the reserved EFBIG exit remain in its dialect. The worker is opted into V8 exhaustion scanning so a heap report names its fixed 256 MiB heap. providerOutcomeOf now reads a launch refusal only from a spawn errno, so a private-storage or carrier read errno is no longer reported as a limiter launch failure.

* fix(evm): keep a stream failure's exit status and update Linux worker expectations

* refactor(process): read launch refusals through the launcher identity owner

* refactor(wasm): classify WABT command outcomes through the shared provider classifier (#10727)

* refactor(wasm): classify WABT command outcomes through the shared provider classifier

WABT's cancellation, command deadline, output budget, and inherited-limit signals now go through classifyProviderOutcome; its dialect keeps only the configuration-probe and launch-refusal unavailability and the unclassified-exit output error. A tool ended by SIGXCPU/SIGXFSZ or the memory limit is now a resource constraint instead of an output error, and a refused launch in the producer phase is reported as unavailable. The shared timeout context gains the analysis setting that selected the deadline, and the output-limit context may name its exceeded budget.

* fix(wasm): keep setup guidance when a WABT version probe's output cannot be collected

* refactor(providers): classify raw provider failures through one owner

* refactor(process): build classified cancellations with cancelledBy and the carried caller reason

* chore(lint): count runOwned's close-failure mapper from main in the classifier baseline

* fix(process): carry the runtime's exhaustion report on every memory error that claims it

SQLite and historical-capture memory errors recognised a streamed V8 heap report but dropped it, so a report outside retained output reached callers without its source line or omission flags. One projection, runtimeExhaustionReport, now owns that shape for the shared classifier and both consumers. Also lowers the EVMole and WABT cancellation-constructor baselines.

* fix(process): keep the provider's recovery for a native-thread exhaustion report

The shared classifier replaced the provider-supplied recovery with generic capacity advice whenever the JVM reported it could not create a native thread, dropping Apktool's launcher guidance and flipping retryable to true. The provider's recovery now wins; the capacity advice remains the fallback for providers that supply none.

* refactor(pwntools): classify pwntools failures through the shared provider classifier (#10782)

* refactor(pwntools): classify pwntools failures through the shared provider classifier

pwntools' per-site classifier is replaced by pwntoolsFailureDialect for classifyProviderFailure. Command outcomes go through classifyProviderOutcome, launch refusals through launcherRefusalOf instead of a 'spawn ' syscall prefix check, the input limit through the file dialect's fileSize, and the cleanup report through commandCleanup. The shared read cancellation now carries the reader's partial observation, and resource-signal reports accept provider detail.

* fix(pwntools): report a failed command's output once and expect resource_constraint for overflow

The shared outcome owner already attaches the command's output as capturedOutput, so the pwntools adapter fallback no longer copies the same text into diagnostics.stdout, diagnostics.stderr and diagnostics.captured_output; diagnostics keep the exit facts. Update the overflow expectations the dialect migration missed (layout provider cleanup and over-budget rows, pwntools cleanup) to resource_constraint.

* refactor(wasm): leave WABT cancellation to the shared owners

WabtFailures matched any Error named AbortError as a cancellation. No WABT path produces one: reads, path checks and owned commands report cancellation as ArtifactReaderFailure or OwnedCommandFailure, which classifyProviderFailure and classifyProviderOutcome already classify with the caller's reason. The provider's two signal checks now build the cancellation with cancelledBy. Lowers the AnalysisCancelledError constructor baseline for both WABT files to zero.

* fix(wasm): report a cancelled snapshot write as the caller's cancellation

The private snapshot write passed the caller's signal to Node's writeFile, whose abort envelope reached the dialect's unclassified output failure once the name-based AbortError guess was removed. The write now turns the envelope carrying its own signal's reason into cancelledBy at the producer.

* refactor(firmware): classify firmware failures through the shared provider classifier (#10810)

Firmware producers now report their own deadline expiry: the start check, the output inventory and launcher admission throw the phase timeout where they observe the abort, and a read the phase signal cancelled reports it through the dialect's interruption. The classifier no longer rereads a cancellation's reason as a timeout. A new readCleanup hook keeps firmware's cleanup report shape.

* refactor(captures): classify TShark, sigrok and pcap failures through the shared provider classifier

TsharkCaptureProvider and SigrokRecordingProvider replace #failure with a dialect, and PcapProvider replaces analysisFailure and the tool-identity classifier. ArtifactAnalysisResources exposes its command context and a readCleanupFailure composer so the readCleanup hook keeps each provider's cleanup report shape.

* refactor(jeb): classify JEB failures through the shared provider classifier

JEB's raw MCP failures go through classifyProviderFailure with a JEB dialect;
a typed attribution step reports a shared phase's failure under the REA
operation. Each MCP phase deadline now reports its own interruption when it
aborts, deciding a cancellation's owner from the caller's own signal instead
of comparing abort reasons. A refusal carrying the JVM's OutOfMemoryError
report becomes a resource constraint naming JEB's Java heap.

* fix(jeb): advise the JVM limit that governs the reported memory area

startup owner closed it, so Ghidra and Hopper no longer compare the abort
reason with the owner's sentinel, and Ghidra's startup no longer compares a

commits.subject: refactor(process): read Ghidra and Hopper replies through one bounded JSON-line reader (#10699)
commits.body:
refactor(process): read Ghidra and Hopper replies through one bounded JSON-line reader (#10699)

* refactor(process): read Ghidra and Hopper replies through one bounded JSON-line reader

Both clients now share JsonLineBridgeReader: UTF-8 framing with a mandatory
reply line ceiling (bridge.max_reply_bytes, REA_BRIDGE_MAX_REPLY_BYTES,
default 256 MiB), one fatal UTF-8 policy, request-id correlation including
rejections on the reserved id 0, and typed stream failures. An oversized
reply is refused as a transport resource constraint naming the setting and
its bytes are discarded. Hopper rejections on id 0 now reach the request on
the wire instead of being dropped.

Deletes GhidraResponseRouter and HopperResponseStream.

* fix(process): bound each bridge reply by the ceiling its own request admitted

* fix(process): admit the bridge reply ceiling before launching Hopper or Ghidra

* fix(ghidra): keep a refused setting's configuration error through the provider boundary

* fix(process): admit both bridge ceilings per request as a typed configuration refusal

A malformed REA_BRIDGE_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES or REA_BRIDGE_MAX_REPLY_BYTES seed covered by a runtime override at startup is refused by the runtime view once the override is reset. Hopper and Ghidra read those getters in the request path (and Hopper re-read the request ceiling when a queued request reached the wire, outside the caller's context), so the refusal was thrown instead of returned. Both clients now copy both ceilings once at admission through readRuntimeSetting, return the ConfigurationError (Ghidra as an admission failure), and write queued requests under the ceilings they were admitted with.

* refactor(config): read rizin, gdb, Kuna, Ghidra and regex settings through readRuntimeSetting (#10795)

Each site caught the ConfigurationError a setting view throws for a malformed launch seed by hand. They now read through readRuntimeSetting and return its Result. GDB reads both debugger limits once per console command and reuses those accepted values for its limitations, timeout and diagnostics instead of re-reading the views after the command ran. Kuna's single-function read returns the refusal after releasing admission instead of throwing it. A counted architecture guard keeps the remaining hand-caught sites from growing.

* refactor(hopper): return typed bridge replies from HopperClient.callTool (#10833)

* refactor(hopper): return typed bridge replies from HopperClient.callTool

The reply contract table existed, but the provider, caller reconciliation and
regex search each applied it after callTool returned JsonValue. callTool is now
typed by method: it validates the reply against that method's contract and
returns the typed reply, or a HopperReplyContractError that names the method
and keeps the raw reply. The caller scan keeps that raw reply as its unread
page or native result. The provider dispatches list_names, file offsets and
the three reconciled operations through their literal methods, and health has
its own contract. Transport tests inject a JSON-value table for the fake
bridge's own methods.

* fix(hopper): refuse value-changing reply contracts and uninstalled methods

parseHopperReply returns the raw reply, so a contract whose input and output types differ (a coercion, default or transform) would promise a type the reply does not hold. ValueKeepingContracts refuses such a schema at compile time, for the production table and any injected one. A client whose type argument names a table it was not given now returns AnalysisCapabilityUnavailableError for a method with no installed contract instead of throwing.

* refactor(hopper): read the startup handshake through the health reply contract (#10853)

parseHopperServerInfo hand-checked each health field that hopperReplySchemas.health already defines. It now parses through that contract, keeps the zod failure as the protocol error's cause, and binds run_id to the launch.

* refactor(kuna): read the project deadline through readRuntimeSetting at each request (#10837)

* refactor(kuna): read the project deadline through readRuntimeSetting at each request

The string, call-graph and xref scans read kuna.project_timeout_ms inside the background producer they start, and the project export read it inside the shared startup promise. A malformed launch seed without an override was thrown from there and reached the caller only through the generic failure mapper; a concurrent waiter that swallows the startup promise's rejection never saw it. Each site now reads the deadline with readRuntimeSetting before starting its work and returns the refusal as that request's value; the export start returns it to each caller that needs the project, and the next request reads it again.

* fix(kuna): return a call-graph deadline refusal from analyze_function

The dossier reported any relationship failure as unavailable call coverage. A call-graph deadline refusal is the request's own setting failure, so it now returns as that ConfigurationError, as cleanup and cancellation already did.

* refactor(kuna): require the accepted project deadline on every export request

Remove acceptedExportDeadline's fallback read of the throwing configuration view. KunaProjectRequest and KunaExportRequest now require the deadline the starting operation accepted; the session passes the one it admitted through readRuntimeSetting into #lookupOrBuild. Direct cache callers in tests take it from one shared helper, withKunaProjectDeadline.

* test(mcp): carry main's Evidence-format const count (#10995) beside the bridge reply setting's

* fix(process): clean Hopper and Ghidra sessions up under the ceilings their start admitted

Cleanup requests re-admitted bridge.max_request_bytes and bridge.max_reply_bytes from the current settings. Once an override covering a malformed launch seed was reset, Hopper's shutdown_document and Ghidra's closing checkpoint_program and shutdown were refused before writing, leaving Hopper's document and files or Ghidra's JVM behind. Each session now keeps the ceilings it admitted at start, and its cleanup requests use them.

* fix(hopper): reauthenticate for cleanup under the session's admitted ceilings

The cleanup reconnect's health handshake still re-admitted the ceilings from the current settings, so a seed refused after an override reset blocked reauthentication and the shutdown after it. It now uses the same session ceilings as the shutdown requests, through one #cleanupLimits accessor.

* refactor(process): report an NDJSON line above its ceiling as a limit parse failure

Utf8NdjsonOversizeError now extends ParseFailureError<"limit"> (format ndjson, limit ndjson-line-bytes) and keeps the observed bytes the transport error reports, so parseFailureFromCause recognizes it like every other byte-format budget.

fix(javascript): omit effects refused by host construction (#11122)

Filter child-process, fetch/WebSocket and TLS effects for literal calls
the host refuses to construct. Share copied child options across validation
and projection, preserving uncertainty from own and inherited getters.
Includes the original implementations from #10528, #10529 and #10530.

Validation: 394 domain/public CLI/MCP tests, then 54 request/public tests after the
review correction, static checks and discovery passed. Also verified 29
Node 24.22.1 probes and actual Chromium 156 header/Request constructors.
Full browser app/network behavior was not tested. Analysis does not execute
target source.

Fixes #10522
Fixes #10523
Fixes #10524
Related: #10528, #10529, #10530

commits.subject: refactor(sqlite): classify database failures through the shared provider classifier (#10870)
commits.body:
refactor(sqlite): classify database failures through the shared provider classifier (#10870)

* fix(pcap): report a refused tool launch as an unavailable tool

When a capture read's tool launch was refused with EPERM, pcap reported it
as unreadable tool output (AnalysisProtocolError) instead of an unavailable
tool. Pcap also never told "not executable" apart from "missing".

Add classifyLaunchFailure in src/process as the one owner of which spawn
errnos mean missing (ENOENT, ENOTDIR) and which mean present but not
executable (EACCES, EPERM, ENOEXEC, EISDIR). Pcap, apktool and gdb used three
different errno lists; all three now use it.

* refactor(process): classify owned command outcomes through one owner

Add ProviderOutcome, read once from the supervisor's facts, and classifyProviderOutcome, the one mapping from an outcome to a typed error. Migrate pcap and the shared artifact producer command failure (TShark, sigrok). Add the rea/provider-failure-classifier lint rule with a shrink-only baseline of per-site (cause: unknown) => AnalysisError functions.

* refactor(process): classify Java and adb launch refusals with the shared owner (#10598)

The Ghidra and JADX Java probes and adb's version probe now take
missing-versus-not-executable from classifyLaunchFailure instead of their
own errno checks. ELOOP and ENAMETOOLONG join the owner's missing set, so
adb keeps its existing classification and both Java probes now treat a
non-directory path component as a missing runtime.

* fix(pcap): preserve command launch attribution

* test(pcap): expect an unknown failing stage when a limited capture tool exits unsuccessfully

* refactor(process): classify owned command outcomes through one owner

Add ProviderOutcome, read once from the supervisor's facts, and classifyProviderOutcome, the one mapping from an outcome to a typed error. Migrate pcap and the shared artifact producer command failure (TShark, sigrok). Add the rea/provider-failure-classifier lint rule with a shrink-only baseline of per-site (cause: unknown) => AnalysisError functions.

* test(lint): cover baselined files in the provider-failure classifier rule

* fix(apktool): report the decoder JVM's heap exhaustion as memory, not a target refusal

The supervisor now watches for a managed runtime's out-of-memory report while output streams (JVM java.lang.OutOfMemoryError, V8 'JavaScript heap out of memory'), so a retention budget cannot hide it. ProviderOutcome gains a runtime-exhausted kind and classifyProviderOutcome maps it once. Apktool decode opts in and moves to the shared classifier; Ghidra's single-purpose output token becomes the JVM runtime option and its area matching reuses the shared table.

* fix(process): keep the runtime's out-of-memory report on the memory error it supports

* fix(pcap): attribute a limited capture's exit through the prlimit wrapper

* fix(process): keep a shortened out-of-memory line marked as shortened

* fix(process): identify the refused executable for every launcher shape

Name the executable on errnos Node throws synchronously from spawn
(ENOEXEC, ENOTDIR, ...) and read the Windows native launcher's
executable-launch constraint, so pcap attributes those refusals to the
selected tool or limiter instead of an unknown stage.

* test(pcap): prove synchronous launch naming with ENOTDIR on every POSIX host

* fix(apktool): advise the JVM limit that governs the reported memory area

* fix(ghidra): read the supervisor's parsed OOM area instead of reparsing lines

* fix(sqlite,capture): read V8 heap exhaustion from streamed output, not retained stderr (#10724)

The SQLite worker and the Node capture decoders now declare runtime: "v8", so the supervisor observes V8's heap report as output streams. Both classifiers read the runtime-exhausted outcome instead of matching retained stderr, so a report beyond the retention budget, or one whose process then overflowed its output budget, is still reported as memory exhaustion.

* refactor(evm): classify EVMole worker outcomes through the shared provider classifier (#10716)

* refactor(evm): classify EVMole worker outcomes through the shared provider classifier

The EVMole worker's cancellation, deadline, output budget and CPU/file-size signals now go through classifyProviderOutcome; only the prlimit launch refusal and the reserved EFBIG exit remain in its dialect. The worker is opted into V8 exhaustion scanning so a heap report names its fixed 256 MiB heap. providerOutcomeOf now reads a launch refusal only from a spawn errno, so a private-storage or carrier read errno is no longer reported as a limiter launch failure.

* fix(evm): keep a stream failure's exit status and update Linux worker expectations

* refactor(process): read launch refusals through the launcher identity owner

* refactor(wasm): classify WABT command outcomes through the shared provider classifier (#10727)

* refactor(wasm): classify WABT command outcomes through the shared provider classifier

WABT's cancellation, command deadline, output budget, and inherited-limit signals now go through classifyProviderOutcome; its dialect keeps only the configuration-probe and launch-refusal unavailability and the unclassified-exit output error. A tool ended by SIGXCPU/SIGXFSZ or the memory limit is now a resource constraint instead of an output error, and a refused launch in the producer phase is reported as unavailable. The shared timeout context gains the analysis setting that selected the deadline, and the output-limit context may name its exceeded budget.

* fix(wasm): keep setup guidance when a WABT version probe's output cannot be collected

* refactor(providers): classify raw provider failures through one owner

* refactor(process): build classified cancellations with cancelledBy and the carried caller reason

* chore(lint): count runOwned's close-failure mapper from main in the classifier baseline

* fix(process): carry the runtime's exhaustion report on every memory error that claims it

SQLite and historical-capture memory errors recognised a streamed V8 heap report but dropped it, so a report outside retained output reached callers without its source line or omission flags. One projection, runtimeExhaustionReport, now owns that shape for the shared classifier and both consumers. Also lowers the EVMole and WABT cancellation-constructor baselines.

* fix(process): keep the provider's recovery for a native-thread exhaustion report

The shared classifier replaced the provider-supplied recovery with generic capacity advice whenever the JVM reported it could not create a native thread, dropping Apktool's launcher guidance and flipping retryable to true. The provider's recovery now wins; the capacity advice remains the fallback for providers that supply none.

* refactor(pwntools): classify pwntools failures through the shared provider classifier (#10782)

* refactor(pwntools): classify pwntools failures through the shared provider classifier

pwntools' per-site classifier is replaced by pwntoolsFailureDialect for classifyProviderFailure. Command outcomes go through classifyProviderOutcome, launch refusals through launcherRefusalOf instead of a 'spawn ' syscall prefix check, the input limit through the file dialect's fileSize, and the cleanup report through commandCleanup. The shared read cancellation now carries the reader's partial observation, and resource-signal reports accept provider detail.

* fix(pwntools): report a failed command's output once and expect resource_constraint for overflow

The shared outcome owner already attaches the command's output as capturedOutput, so the pwntools adapter fallback no longer copies the same text into diagnostics.stdout, diagnostics.stderr and diagnostics.captured_output; diagnostics keep the exit facts. Update the overflow expectations the dialect migration missed (layout provider cleanup and over-budget rows, pwntools cleanup) to resource_constraint.

* refactor(wasm): leave WABT cancellation to the shared owners

WabtFailures matched any Error named AbortError as a cancellation. No WABT path produces one: reads, path checks and owned commands report cancellation as ArtifactReaderFailure or OwnedCommandFailure, which classifyProviderFailure and classifyProviderOutcome already classify with the caller's reason. The provider's two signal checks now build the cancellation with cancelledBy. Lowers the AnalysisCancelledError constructor baseline for both WABT files to zero.

* fix(wasm): report a cancelled snapshot write as the caller's cancellation

The private snapshot write passed the caller's signal to Node's writeFile, whose abort envelope reached the dialect's unclassified output failure once the name-based AbortError guess was removed. The write now turns the envelope carrying its own signal's reason into cancelledBy at the producer.

* refactor(firmware): classify firmware failures through the shared provider classifier (#10810)

Firmware producers now report their own deadline expiry: the start check, the output inventory and launcher admission throw the phase timeout where they observe the abort, and a read the phase signal cancelled reports it through the dialect's interruption. The classifier no longer rereads a cancellation's reason as a timeout. A new readCleanup hook keeps firmware's cleanup report shape.

* refactor(captures): classify TShark, sigrok and pcap failures through the shared provider classifier

TsharkCaptureProvider and SigrokRecordingProvider replace #failure with a dialect, and PcapProvider replaces analysisFailure and the tool-identity classifier. ArtifactAnalysisResources exposes its command context and a readCleanupFailure composer so the readCleanup hook keeps each provider's cleanup report shape.

* refactor(jeb): classify JEB failures through the shared provider classifier

JEB's raw MCP failures go through classifyProviderFailure with a JEB dialect;
a typed attribution step reports a shared phase's failure under the REA
operation. Each MCP phase deadline now reports its own interruption when it
aborts, deciding a cancellation's owner from the caller's own signal instead
of comparing abort reasons. A refusal carrying the JVM's OutOfMemoryError
report becomes a resource constraint naming JEB's Java heap.

* fix(jeb): advise the JVM limit that governs the reported memory area

* refactor(ghidra): classify Ghidra failures through the shared provider classifier

PSP extension inspection reports through classifyProviderFailure with a
Ghidra dialect. The startup deadline decides at abort time whether the shared
startup owner closed it, so Ghidra and Hopper no longer compare the abort
reason with the owner's sentinel, and Ghidra's startup no longer compares a
producer cancellation's reason with the deadline's. Three helpers that only
construct one error kind now name that kind instead of AnalysisError.

* refactor(hopper): classify original-source read failures through the shared provider classifier (#10838)

* test(ghidra): pin the aborted startup deadline over a producer cancellation

* refactor(kuna): classify Kuna failures through the shared provider classifier

Session operations, the workspace copy and the project export report raw
failures through classifyProviderFailure with Kuna dialects; the copy and
export keep their cleanup report shapes through the readCleanup hook.

* refactor(process): let artifact-resource consumers classify through the shared provider classifier (#10867)

commits.subject: refactor(cli): project core native commands with open_binary target options (#10736)
commits.body:
refactor(cli): project core native commands with open_binary target options (#10736)

* refactor(cli): project core native commands with open_binary target options

A session target's opening fields may now be caller paths, admitted
resolved and passed on as the caller spelled them, and a union of text
forms such as the provider selector renders as one argv token.

nativeTarget declares a native executable opened with open_binary's
format, architecture, entry point and provider fields, plus the snapshot
where a command loads one. runDirectOnTarget runs an operation on that
target through runDirectAnalysis, with Evidence delivery when declared.

Eleven core native commands are now derived from their contracts. Their
inputs are admitted by the service's contract parse, which replaces the
CLI's copies of the byte-pattern and data-type selector checks.
inspect-native-dispatch-metadata now exposes the contract's Objective-C
class import address fields.

* fix(cli): read core native contracts from their contract groups so startup stays lazy

* refactor(cli): project procedure-references and inspect-native-api with named selector options (#10738)

* refactor(cli): project procedure-references and inspect-native-api with named selector options

A contract projection may let the caller give a positional selector with
a named option instead, for values that begin with a dash. The positional
becomes optional; equal values agree (native addresses by identity), and
different values, or neither for a required field, are refused before the
target is opened. selectCliAnalysisSelector owns that rule and returns a
Result; resolveCliAnalysisSelector remains for the hand-written core
binary commands.

procedure-references and inspect-native-api are now derived from their
contracts on the native session target, which completes the core native
family.

fix(javascript): refuse member-mutation work beyond a fixed allowance (#11144)

* fix(javascript): refuse member-mutation work beyond a fixed allowance

Member-mutation indexing retained every scheduled alias state until its query finished, with no bound on the phase. Conditional self-selections before one member write (#8294) multiplied those states until the worker heap was exhausted.

Charge each scheduled alias state to a per-phase work meter. Past 524,288 states the phase is refused with a resource_constraint that names the fixed work allowance. The application and web bundle workers carry the reported limit to the parent, which rebuilds the refusal with that allowance instead of heap advice.

Refs #8294 #6127 #6344 #7170 #7510 #8298

* test(mcp): compile advertised patterns with the regex engines clients run

List the built package's tools over stdio in every input, output and
catalog profile and compile each distinct advertised regular expression
with V8 (plain, u, v), Go regexp (RE2), C++ RE2, Python re, and Rust regex
and fancy-regex through the Rust jsonschema crate. A refusal names the
engine, its error, and each tool, schema path and profile.

The Python engines are pinned, hash-checked wheels; Go is the host
toolchain with GOTOOLCHAIN=local. A missing engine is reported as not
verified, and REA_REQUIRE_SCHEMA_ENGINES=1 makes it a failure.

The pattern owner now also reports patternProperties keys, which clients
compile as well.

* test(mcp): load advertised schemas in the validators clients build (#10983)

with the Rust jsonschema crate's defaults, which check the declared draft's
meta-schema and formats and compile every subschema. --complete adds Python
jsonschema's check_schema, which jsonschema.validate runs in Python clients;
it takes several seconds, so it is opt-in.

Refusals are grouped by reason, so one shared pattern that breaks many
schemas is reported once with its sites.

Ajv strict mode and OpenAI strict mode are documented as not covered, with
the reasons.
