commits.body:
feat(mcp)!: retire the full schema profiles and declare schema facts as typed annotations (#10693)

* test(mcp): check advertised schemas against a portable dialect in every profile

* fix(mcp): re-emit advertised patterns in a portable regex grammar

* fix(mcp): present discover_tools input through the selected profile

The hot-cold catalog registered discover_tools directly with the SDK, so
the default compact input profile still advertised its canonical schema,
including page-size defaults clients apply on their own (#5322). Route
every listed input schema, transport discovery included, through one
server-owned presentation, and pass the selected presentation to the
deferred server, which serves recorded tool schemas but not discovery.

* fix(mcp): keep the Evidence union on described borrowed inputs

borrowEvidenceInput installed its advertised projection on one schema
instance. A call site's .describe() rebuilds the schema from its
definition, so match_native_functions advertised left and right as
unconstrained values in every input profile. Install the projection in
the borrowed parser's constructor so derived schemas keep it, for both
borrowed inputs and borrowed arrays.

* fix(mcp): validate advertised dialect by selected profile

* fix(mcp): preserve schema widening through references

* feat(mcp): project compact input schemas into the portable advertised dialect

One projection (advertisedDialectProjection.ts) owns the compact input
advertisement: one type per node, items on every array, string literals
as enums, oneOf widened to anyOf, allOf merged, tuples as element unions,
exclusive bounds made inclusive, and every keyword outside the dialect
dropped. Each rewrite is exact or widening; server validation is
unchanged. The root description and sentences for dropped cross-field
constraints move to the tool description, which Codex and Zed keep.

The compact baseline falls to nullable values only (29), which the
dialect cannot express without narrowing an input. The gateway shape
repairs (typeArrayItemUnions, hasGatewayIncompatibleShape), the second
dependentRequired-to-prose copy and the strict-gateway test denylist are
removed; the dialect checker gates the inline presentation instead.

* feat(mcp): omit output schemas from tools/list by default

No surveyed model API reads an output schema, MCP client validators
repeat REA's own result validation, and complete output schemas were
about 92% of the default tools/list. REA_MCP_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE now
resolves to off through one owner (resolveMcpOutputSchemaProfile);
compact and full remain selectable. structuredContent is still
delivered, and the deferred server serves both off and full from the
recorded catalog with the matching recorded identity.

Tests and artifact verifiers that validate results against complete
advertised output contracts select full explicitly.

* docs: describe omitted output schemas as the default in README translations

* fix(mcp): select schemas in verification workflows

* fix(mcp): refuse zero-padded repeat bounds and record host-specific path patterns

* fix(mcp): keep projected schemas permissive

* fix(mcp): keep references valid when presentation widens their targets

* fix(mcp): keep a single union branch's closure scoped to its properties

* fix(mcp): select complete output schemas in the Electron verifier

* fix(mcp): select complete output schemas in standalone verifier probes

* fix(mcp): keep an allOf member's tuple tail with its own positions

* fix(mcp): relax references into negations and conditionals presentation may remove

* refactor(contracts): declare root discriminators as typed schema annotations

* test(mcp): select the borrowed Evidence contract from its family

* fix(mcp): keep astral literals and dynamic references widening in every mode

* fix(mcp): omit astral literals and relax untracked references when presentation widens

* fix(mcp): select complete output schemas in every verifier transport

* fix(mcp): read reference pointers by schema position, not segment spelling

* fix(mcp): protect references into collapsing boolean unions and keep referencing branches out of the collapse

* fix(mcp): keep reduced schemas open when their root admits names by pattern

* test(mcp): keep the reduced-schema pattern case outside the size-limited block

* test(mcp): select full output schemas in packet and signal schema checks

* test(mcp): select full output schemas in HTTP session workflows

* fix(mcp): emit stack-safe classes with non-ASCII members and protect draft-07 reference siblings

* fix(mcp): protect references into literal siblings of relaxed draft-07 references

No surveyed model API reads an output schema, MCP client validators
repeat REA's own result validation, and complete output schemas were
about 92% of the default tools/list. REA_MCP_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE now
resolves to off through one owner (resolveMcpOutputSchemaProfile);
compact and full remain selectable. structuredContent is still
delivered, and the deferred server serves both off and full from the
recorded catalog with the matching recorded identity.

Tests and artifact verifiers that validate results against complete
advertised output contracts select full explicitly.

* fix(mcp): keep the Evidence union on described borrowed inputs

borrowEvidenceInput installed its advertised projection on one schema
instance. A call site's .describe() rebuilds the schema from its
definition, so match_native_functions advertised left and right as
unconstrained values in every input profile. Install the projection in
the borrowed parser's constructor so derived schemas keep it, for both
borrowed inputs and borrowed arrays.

* test(mcp): select the borrowed Evidence contract from its family

* docs(mcp): admit baseline growth only for restored contract declarations

* fix(mcp): state reduced multi-type properties as typed branches, not type lists

The reduced fallback derived a property's types and emitted them as a type
list, which Gemini, Moonshot and Ark reject. A property whose canonical
schema is anyOf string and number therefore traded a typed union for a
rejected construct when the inline projection fell back. Emit one type, or
anyOf typed branches, so [T, null] becomes the dialect's nullable union.

* feat(mcp)!: retire the full schema profiles and declare complete observations as a typed annotation (#10718)

* refactor(mcp): declare complete observations as a typed annotation applied only on the wire

* test(mcp): compare complete-observation declarations with their owning text

* refactor(schema): couple Zod checks with their JSON Schema constraint keywords (#10725)

* refactor(schema): couple Zod checks with their JSON Schema constraint keywords

* refactor(schema): declare pattern approximations and object output roots as typed annotations (#10754)

* refactor(schema): declare pattern approximations and object output roots as typed annotations

* fix(schema): refuse pattern declarations JSON Schema cannot state

* test(schema): select guided_workflows from its contract family

* feat(mcp)!: retire the full input and output schema profiles (#10841)

* feat(mcp)!: retire the full input and output schema profiles

The compact input presentation is now the only advertised input schema, and
output schemas are either omitted (`off`, the default) or bounded
(`compact`). Catalog identity, the build-recorded digests and the recorded
startup catalog collapse to those presentations: two digest profiles instead
of six, one recorded catalog instead of two, and no input dialect baseline.

Tests and verifiers that validated replies against listed full output
schemas now validate against the canonical output contract, which REA
already enforces server-side; tests that asserted canonical input
restrictions read the canonical input schema instead of a full listing.

BREAKING CHANGE: `REA_MCP_INPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE=full` and
`REA_MCP_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE=full` are refused at startup and by `rea setup`
with a configuration error naming the setting. Remove the setting from the
client registration (or rerun setup with `REA_MCP_INPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE=compact`
/ `REA_MCP_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE=compact`). `REA_MCP_INPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE`
still accepts `compact`. Server-side validation is unchanged.

* test(mcp): validate replies against canonical output contracts at every listed-schema reader

tools/list omits output schemas by default, so fixtures, verifiers and the
Android analysis runners that read a listed outputSchema now bind the
canonical contract instead. connectLocalToolsMcp and advertisedMcpToolSchemas
hand the SDK a definition carrying the canonical output schema, so the SDK
client and caller-supplied validators check every successful reply.

* test(mcp): resolve Android runners' output contracts from the selected repository

The Android efficiency runners imported the canonical output-schema helper from the harness checkout while --repository selects the revision under test. Import it from the selected repository, as the runners already do for the SDK and Ajv.

* test(mcp): let Android runners compare revisions before the canonical output helper

A selected revision without scripts/lib/canonical-output-schema.mjs could not start the Android runners. Choose the output contracts in one harness helper: the selected revision's canonical contracts when it has them, otherwise its listed schemas under the full output profile it still supports.

* fix(scripts): keep caller launch settings when the real Hopper verifier builds its server environment

The verifier deleted REA_VERIFY_SERVER_COMMAND and REA_VERIFY_SERVER_ARGS_JSON from process.env itself before reading them, so a caller selecting an installed REA command silently ran the checkout's dist/main.js. Copy the environment, as main does, so only the child's environment changes.

* test(mcp): validate whole replies against canonical output contracts wherever a listed definition is held

tools/list omits output schemas by default and the full output profile is gone, so tests that handed the SDK a listed definition no longer checked complete replies. Attach the canonical output schema with withCanonicalOutputSchema at every held REA tool definition. Environment-served tools (not REA contracts), and the deferred-runtime and doctor tests that exercise per-profile listings, keep their listed definitions.

* test(mcp): record the advertised catalog summary without the retired full profiles

Retiring the full input and output profiles leaves only the compact input and compact output listings, so the summary drops the full-profile digests and every pattern only the full listings carried. Regenerated with npm run verify:advertised-schemas -- --update-summary.

commits.subject: feat(javascript): make the member-mutation work allowance a runtime setting (#11181)
commits.body:
feat(javascript): make the member-mutation work allowance a runtime setting (#11181)

* feat(javascript): make the member-mutation work allowance a runtime setting

The member-mutation alias-state allowance from #11144 was a fixed constant, so a refused source could not be admitted without a code change.

Register javascript.member_mutation_alias_states (default 524288, 1 to 8388608 alias states) with the launch seed REA_JAVASCRIPT_MEMBER_MUTATION_ALIAS_STATES. The application, web bundle and reference-source boundaries resolve it from the accepted operation snapshot and launch environment, refuse a malformed seed before analysis, and send it to the workers with each source. A refusal names the setting, its effective value, source and range, and the recovery; worker parents rebuild it from the allowance they sent.

Refs #8294

* fix(javascript): keep the setting and recovery of a refused web script

A web bundle script refused by the member-mutation allowance kept only its reason and reported limits, so the public unknown lost the setting, value, source and recovery. Carry the refusal's structured limit and remediation on the per-script result and its javascript_analysis unknown, grouping scripts only when that recovery agrees. Assert structured limit facts and the owning formatter's recovery instead of fixed wording.

* fix(browser): keep only registered setting limits on a refused web script

* feat(javascript): keep syntax facts for a source whose member-mutation phase is refused (#11187)

* feat(javascript): keep syntax facts for a source whose member-mutation phase is refused

A source refused by the member-mutation work allowance during static analysis lost every fact, so the application graph counted it as skipped. Reference-source import failed outright on such a file.

Checkpoint the parser, comment and text facts the static owner can still state, with parse status partial, examination not-examined and refused_phase member-mutations, before reporting the refusal; the semantic phase is not started because it indexes the same mutations. Reference-source import keeps the file's declaration-level imports and records that its CommonJS require calls were not examined.

Refs #8294

* test(javascript): compare the reference-source refusal with its owning formatter

* feat(javascript): keep a refused web script's parse and text facts

A captured script whose member-mutation phase was refused lost every fact in analyze_web_bundle, so it was neither counted as parsed nor kept its vendor markers.

The analyzer now returns the script as unavailable with partial facts: refused phase, parse status and the inferences read from script text alone. Findings gathered before the refusal are dropped, because they may have read an incomplete mutation index. The worker parent states the refusal and its setting recovery from the allowance it sent, through the same helper the isolated analyzer uses for every unavailable script. The bundle counts the script as parsed, keeps its text inferences, and its javascript_analysis unknown carries refused_phase.

Refs #8294

* chore(mcp): record the member-mutation setting in the advertised summary

* fix(javascript): rebuild a parked source worker when the member-mutation allowance changes

A worker parked on a resource scope was reused when heap, timeout and precision matched, but its requests carry the allowance it was built with. After update_analysis_settings accepted a new allowance, the next analysis on that scope kept the old one.

The reuse check now compares the allowance's value and source, so a changed setting gets a worker built with it. The web bundle worker already takes the allowance per script.

commits.body:
fix(native)!: report a target-selected plist against the target, not the unsent path input (#10798)

* fix(native): report a target-selected plist against the target, not the unsent path input

inspect_plist resolved a plist that the open target itself selects with the same origin as a caller's path input, so an unreadable target plist was reported as an input issue on path even when the caller never sent path. The selection now records a target origin, and unreadablePlist reports it as a BinaryTargetError for the target. The inspect-plist CLI command is projected from its contract, so its --relative-path issues are named by the CLI key.

* refactor(cli)!: route analyze to the contract its target selects (#10808)

* refactor(cli): route analyze to the contract its target selects

analyze hand-declared both lanes: native open options for binary_overview and the JavaScript integrity policy and source selection for analyze_javascript_application, with its own routing and refusals. registerTargetRoutedCommand now projects each route from its contract, takes the union of their options, runs the first route that owns every given option and takes the target, and refuses options the chosen route does not own by their CLI key. Omitted union fields, including a root discriminator, no longer need an argv projection.

* fix(cli): give a routed command's chosen route its CLI-only option defaults

Routing strips option defaults so an omitted option routes no target. Contract fields regain theirs on admission, but CLI-only options have no later parse, so a defaulted one reached the handler as undefined. The chosen route's omitted CLI-only options now receive their defaults before the handler runs.

* refactor(cli): deliver decompile and inspect-macho Evidence by the contract's detail (#10813)

* refactor(cli): deliver decompile and inspect-macho Evidence by the contract's detail

decompile and inspect-macho omitted the contract's detail field and always printed complete Evidence. Both now declare evidenceDelivery, adding --detail and --evidence_output from the contract. Publishing a result never used the provider id it required, so publication takes no provider and runOnSessionTarget no longer needs one to deliver.

* refactor(cli): project managed artifact and native-boundary inspectors from their contracts (#10816)

inspect-managed-artifact and inspect-managed-native-boundaries re-declared the managed budget fields by hand. Both now register from their contracts on a session target, and inspect-managed-artifact gains --detail and --evidence_output from its detail field.

* fix(cli): name every contract command's input issues by their CLI key

Commands applied their CLI field binding only where a session-target or
direct handler returned an undelivered result. With evidenceDelivery,
decompile publishes through the shared delivery, which returned a
provider failure unprojected, so an issue about the procedure would be
reported at ["procedure"] instead of the advertised positional
"address". Handlers that run a service or publish themselves never
applied it: inspect-il2cpp-metadata reported ["generic_instances"],
inspect-go-binary ["max_string_literals"] and inspect-apple-ips
["join_path"] rather than the CLI keys other commands report.

The contract command now projects whatever its handler returns through
the binding it owns, for plain and target-routed commands alike, and
the handler context no longer carries the binding.

* fix(analysis-view): summarize pseudocode that selected an independent fresh decompile

The pseudocode view parsed its parent's parameters with a selection
schema that admitted only procedure and document. A procedure_pseudo_code
observation made with analysis independent_fresh records that field, so
its summary view refused the parent. Through the CLI's new summary
delivery, `decompile --analysis independent_fresh --detail summary
--evidence_output <file>` would fail after a successful decompile and
never save the bundle; an inline inspect_analysis_view of such Evidence
failed the same way.

The selection schema now admits the analysis the contract offers, and
the contract reads that enum from the same owner.

* test(cli): restore the worker's exit status after synthetic contract command runs

logCliCommand sets process.exitCode on a refused or failed command. The
synthetic routed and input-field harnesses ran in the cli-boundary
project's shared workers (isolate: false) and left that status for later
tests. Each invocation now restores the previous status.

* refactor(cli)!: deliver inspect-managed-members Evidence through the shared --evidence_output (#10845)

inspect-managed-members was the last command with its own Evidence
delivery: a hand-written registration passed --detail and
--evidence-bundle to runProviderAnalysis, whose members-only delivery
variant re-checked heap headroom and published through
deliverAnalysisEvidence. Every other producer writes its bundle with
--evidence_output through publishCliAnalysisEvidence, and elsewhere on
the CLI --evidence-bundle names an input bundle to read.

The command now registers from the inspect_managed_members contract on
a session target with evidenceDelivery, like inspect-managed-artifact;
--type is the contract's type_names. runProviderAnalysis loses its
delivery parameter and its two refusals, and deliverAnalysisEvidence,
now unused, is deleted. Its lifecycle tests drive publishEvidenceDelivery
directly or the CLI delivery; the managed-only headroom pre-check tests
are removed, since the shared delivery deliberately does not
re-authenticate immutable Evidence and keeps the writer's check for
mutable sources.

BREAKING CHANGE: `rea inspect-managed-members --evidence-bundle <path>`
is now `--evidence_output <path>`; the old flag is refused as an unknown
flag. With `--detail summary`, stdout is now
`{"summary": <summary Evidence>, "evidence_bundle": {"path", "bytes"}}`
instead of the summary Evidence alone, and a publication failure is the
shared delivery's error projection without the `error` label or
`input_path`. A summary without a destination names `evidence_output`
in its issue path. Migrate by renaming the flag and reading
`.summary`. Compatibility is not kept: one spelling cannot mean "read
this bundle" on view and workflow commands and "write this bundle" on
one producer.

* refactor(cli): project analyze-javascript-application and analyze's JavaScript route from one contract projection

analyze-javascript-application declared its options by hand, mapped
about twelve option names to contract fields itself, parsed its delivery
separately and resolved its own caller path. analyze's JavaScript route,
projected from the same contract, omitted every field but the path,
source selection and integrity policy, so the two commands for one
contract offered different options.

Both now use javaScriptApplicationCliProjection and
runJavaScriptApplicationCommand: the path positional, --artifact-format,
--source-path, and the two options that accept a JSON file
(--source-paths-json, --semantic-precision), with contract delivery.
analyze therefore takes the JavaScript budgets, --artifact-format,
--semantic-precision and --detail/--evidence_output/--view for
JavaScript targets, and refuses them by CLI key for native targets.
javascriptApplicationOptions is deleted.

The command's missing-target refusal now names its CLI key, "path",
as every contract command does.

runner, as inspect-managed-members does, and compares the records as MCP
compare_managed_members does. A failing candidate names its argument and

Select snapshot faults by file identity, guard real permission denial to

contract inputs to service requests for both adapters.

* refactor(cli): finalize the Evidence-target composition through runOwned

runOnEvidenceTargets turned a completed comparison into a cancellation by reading the abort signal by hand, which main's architecture guard now refuses outside runOwned. The composition now finalizes through runOwned: its close drains queued interrupts (it owns no resource), and a cancellation observed as it settles keeps the completed Evidence as the partial observation, as before.

The command now registers through registerContractCommand with `path` as a
caller path, so the builder's absoluteCallerPath owns relative-path

* test(cli): derive contract-built commands from the builder registries instead of a hand list

Every command named after a public tool contract must register through a contract builder unless it is in a shrinking list of hand registrations, and the renamed contract commands are listed exactly, so an earlier migration that reverts fails instead of dropping out of the parity cases. The JSON-document command hand list is covered by the same check and removed.

* refactor(cli): project compare-web-screenshots and analyze-web-bundle from their contracts with builder JSON inputs (#11012)

* refactor(cli): project compare-web-screenshots from its contract with builder JSON inputs read from inline text or a file

The contract command builder gains jsonInputs: structured fields taken as inline JSON or a JSON file path (- reads stdin), read when the command runs and admitted with the contract input before any target is opened. Inline text that is not JSON is refused under its CLI key; a file that cannot be read keeps its own failure. compare-web-screenshots takes both artifacts this way, replacing its hand-written JSON argument parsing.

* refactor(cli): project analyze-web-bundle from its contract

analyze-web-bundle now registers through registerContractCommand with Evidence and view delivery, semantic_precision as a builder JSON input, and source_map_limits flattened onto the existing --source-map-* flags. Page-inspection extras stay omitted, and script sources stay on as the contract default. The superseded javascriptRouteDelivery options, passive browser scope options, observation duration helper and fetched source-map option set are removed.

analyze-javascript-application and the analyze route read --semantic-precision through the contract builder's jsonInputs instead of a CLI-only option decoded in the handler, so the decoded budgets are admitted with the contract input before analysis.

* fix(cli): keep branch-only defaults to their branch and name admission issues by CLI key

A branch-only field no longer carries its default into the shared options, so another branch never receives it; the selected branch applies the default on parse. Contract admission failures are projected to CLI keys like handler failures. CLI defaults are typed only on top-level fields, the one place that applies them.

* refactor(cli): project compare-process-captures from its contract, checking each capture before reading the next (#11114)

* refactor(cli): project compare-process-captures from its contract, checking each capture before reading the next

The contract builder gains jsonInputChecks: each check runs on a decoded JSON input as soon as it is read, in argv order, so a refused input stops the command before the next is read; the handler receives what each check admitted. compare-process-captures authenticates the left capture before reading the right and the right before the trace specification, then compares the authenticated facts. It now also takes inline JSON, stdin and --max-capture-age-ms like MCP. Empty JSON input text is refused at argv. A JSON input whose final file close fails is reported as cleanup_incomplete naming the file instead of an unclassified failure. compareProcessEvidenceFiles and its trace-spec parser are removed.

* fix(cli): retry a refused JSON input close and keep the read's refusal beside incomplete cleanup

parseCliJsonInput gives the file's owner a resource scope, so a transient close refusal is retried before the command fails. A close that still fails reports cleanup_incomplete composed with the read's own refusal. Routed commands refuse routes that check a shared JSON input differently, since it is checked before the route is chosen.

* refactor(cli): project inspect-web-network-capture from its contract with nested protobuf options

The contract builder flattens a nested optional object member in turn (protobuf.schema), resolves a flattened caller-path member and reports it as spelled under its dotted path in callerInputs, keeps a flattened member's contract default out of argv so an omitted member stays omitted, and takes an array of numbers as repeated decimal tokens within its bounds. inspect-web-network-capture registers from its contract with the same option names; Evidence keeps the capture and descriptor paths as the caller spelled them. CLI input issues name the capturePath argument.

* fix(cli): name a selector field by its own option in admission issues

A selector parameter's positional may share another key (decompile's procedure positional is address), so mapping the field to its positional key renamed selection issues that already name the option, such as a missing or conflicting --procedure. Map a selector field to its option.

* fix(cli): retain a JSON input file whose close fails and keep why its read stopped

parseCliJsonInput dropped its per-read scope after the owner's close retry failed, so the handle lost its owner, and a read or cancellation failure recorded before the close was replaced by the cleanup failure. The read's scope now stays with the CLI process until final CLI cleanup retries it, and the recorded outcome is translated once into the primary failure with the cleanup attached. The module moves into src/cli so it can register with the CLI process owner without a layer cycle.

* refactor(cli): project inspect-with-objdump and inspect-api-contract from their contracts (#11142)

* refactor(cli): project inspect-with-objdump, list-objdump-architectures and inspect-api-contract from their contracts

The contract builder selects input branches by a field that is a literal in
one branch and an enum in another, takes the default of the one branch that
admits omission, and lets a command take a subset of a union's branches by
their discriminating values, fixing the field when one value is selected.

* refactor(cli): project trace-web-source-location from its contract with flattened positional objects (#11167)

* refactor(cli): project trace-web-source-location from its contract with flattened positional objects

The contract builder flattens required objects as well as optional ones; a
flattened field listed in positionals takes its members as positionals in
member order. The hand-written source-map limit options and the separate CLI
delivery schema are removed.

* fix(cli): refuse to flatten a required object without a required member

* fix(cli): refuse a malformed Evidence-input document before reading the selected bundle

runEvidenceInputCommand admits the document with its transport frame before
it reads --evidence-bundle, so every Evidence-input command refuses a
malformed document first, as compare-static-and-observed-endpoints already
did by hand.

* test(cli): expect a selector field to be named by its option in input issues

* fix(cli): report a refused view before the delivery rule it would trip

Refusing delivery options before JSON inputs are read checked --evidence_output before the view's own schema, so a summary view naming an unknown field reported only the missing bundle. Admit the view with the contract's view field first, as full admission does.

* refactor(cli): project inspect-android-jni-bindings from its contract with a grouped --query option (#11196)

* refactor(cli): project inspect-android-jni-bindings from its contract with a grouped --query option

A projection's fieldGroups take several optional top-level contract fields as the members of one JSON object option. The text is decoded when the command runs, refused with the group's message when it is not a JSON object, a member that is not one of the group's fields is refused by its path, and the contract admits each member as its field. inspect-android-jni-bindings keeps its --query selection through a group and now registers through the contract builder, so the hand-registered contract command list is empty; the superseded parseCliAnalysisEvidenceDelivery and androidJniDeliverySchema are removed.

* fix(cli): refuse an object rule that names a grouped field

A grouped field is a JSON member, not an option, so a contract rule such as dependentRequired naming it would be advertised over an option that does not exist. Registration now refuses that combination.

* fix(cli): describe the --view and --maxCaptureAgeMs options of projected commands

A projected view field kept no help because the contract's own description was skipped and none replaced it, and compare-process-captures exposed max_capture_age_ms without help. The canonical CLI catalog test refused both. The view option now takes the same help in both builders.

* refactor(cli): derive the CLI command inventory from the contract registry (#11248)

A contract now declares `cli: true` when the CLI exposes it as the command
named by its kebab-case name. The primary CLI inventory (CLI_COMMAND_NAMES,
now owned by catalogIdentity.ts) is derived from those declarations plus the
commands no contract names, and a contract projection omits `command`: the
builder names the command from the contract and refuses a contract that does
not declare one. CLI_COMMANDS keeps only the 32 commands no contract names;
the 164 contract-named entries and the copied MCP-only list in
cliToolCoverage.test.ts are removed.

* fix(managed): keep decoded members when only their loaded literals exceed capacity

A capacity failure while decoding #US literals discarded the member facts already decoded, because the shared representation budget threw through the whole inspection. Literals carry their own coverage, so the inspection is retried without them and reports user_strings as partial with the capacity issue. compare-managed-members, which now runs full inspections, keeps comparing members it used to read with literals disabled.

* test(cli): expect builder-admitted issues by CLI key and option help with its default

Builder admission of compare-web-captures, compare-web-screenshots and analyze-web-bundle names input issues by the CLI key (beforeJson, afterJson, normalizationJson, endpoint), and --integrity-policy help states its default. Four test files still expected the contract field names and the old help, so they failed on the stack.

* test(cli): read each refused browser input's CLI path directly now that every case names one

Every invalid browser input now carries its CLI key, so the fallback branch narrowed to never and failed the TypeScript compiler's typecheck.

* chore(verify): carry the moved cliJsonInput baseline entry into its per-guard file

Rebased on main after #11316 split the guard baselines and #11181 threaded the launch environment into the web bundle command; the contract-built analyze-web-bundle command now passes that environment to the browser provider.

* refactor(cli): hand whole-input contract handlers the admitted parse instead of parsing again (#11301)

* refactor(cli): hand whole-input contract handlers the admitted parse instead of parsing again

* refactor(cli): parse an argv whole input only when the handler reads it

Admission parsed every argv whole-input command eagerly, so handlers that
hand the raw input to a service (inspectWithService) parsed it twice.
parseWholeInput now parses on the first admittedContractInput call and
reuses the result; run-time JSON and view delivery still parse at
admission. The test counts whole-schema evaluations.

* refactor(cli): hand JSON-document handlers the admitted parse of their document (#11332)

observe-native-calls, capture-electron-scenario and match-native-functions
parsed their resolved document against the contract schema in the handler.
registerContractDocumentCommand now gives each document handler
parseWholeInput, a memoized parse of the resolved document as the whole
contract input whose refusal names the caller's spelling, so
admittedContractInput serves argv and document commands alike. A handler
whose document is not the whole input never calls it, so it adds no parse.

* fix(cli): admit checked JSON inputs through their checks only

compare-process-captures walked and copied both capture records again in
the whole-input parse after their checks had admitted them. Admission now
parses the remaining fields with the contract and hands the handler the
checked documents uncopied. The managed summary example names
--evidence_output.

ensureTerminated proved target exit with kill(pid, 0), which succeeds for a
zombie. A target that SIGKILL ended but debugserver had not reaped yet was
reported as "verified target did not exit after SIGKILL" and the run as

The host acknowledged an unreadable target identity as "unavailable" and
dropped the observation's reason, so a target-identity-unavailable failure
said only that the identity could not be verified. The reason (the
identity reader's own reason, a thrown inspection failure, or that the PID
had already exited) is now diagnostics.identity_observation.

  ManagedMemberRows always writes a boolean. Now required; the comparison
  owner's `undefined` branch and the "historical omission" test are gone.
- Evidence `caller_input_path`: written only when a request selects a
  direct path, so it stays optional; the wording now says that.
- Ghidra `containing_instruction`: optional because other instruction
  statuses have no container; wording corrected.

BREAKING CHANGE: inspect_firmware_regions and extract_firmware results
require `analysis_timeout_ms`, and inspect_managed_members call edges and
field accesses require `target_row_resolved`. Evidence or analysis-view
input without them is refused. Every producer in this release writes them;
recreate observations made by a build that omitted them.

commits.subject: fix(process): settle an observed exit in progress before reporting a process present (#10620)
commits.body:
fix(process): settle an observed exit in progress before reporting a process present (#10620)

* fix(process): settle an observed exit in progress before reporting a process present

An exiting process closes its sockets before it becomes a zombie. A
caller that reacts to the closed transport could read the captured
identity in that window and report it as present, so Hopper cleanup
retained the document and private runtime although the application had
exited.

Wait, within the existing cleanup verification grace, only while the
same identity is positively observed exiting.

Refs #10556

* refactor(process): reuse exit settlement when observing a bridge exit

Review follow-up for observeProcessStartIdentityExit.

The exit check added its own waiting loop beside
settleExitingProcessIdentities, with the same deadline, polling interval
and same-identity exiting check, so future exit-race fixes would need
two changes. The check now hands its first observation to the shared
settlement and keeps only the final result choice. The settlement and
its identity reader accept PID-only rows, the shape the host identity
reader already takes. One liveProcessIdentity helper maps absent and
exited identities for both observeProcessStartIdentity and the settled
result.

Behavior is unchanged: an exiting identity is re-read until it leaves
exit in progress or the cleanup grace ends; a replacement, absent or
zombie identity is exited, an unreadable one unverified, and one still
exiting at the deadline present.

Tests: src/process (850), the Hopper cleanup and session tests (15) and
20 Hopper boundary test files (114) pass. check:fast passes.

commits.subject: ci: trace script modules and built-server consumers in PR test selection, and balance selected shards (#11516)
commits.body:
ci: trace script modules and built-server consumers in PR test selection, and balance selected shards (#11516)

* ci: trace shared script modules to the tests that import them

A pull request that changed any scripts/lib module ran the complete
suite. Shared script modules now pass a change through to the tests,
verifiers and other shared modules that import them, like test helpers.
Another consumer (a build or test-runner script, root configuration,
package metadata, a hook or a workflow) that imports the module or names
it by file name still selects the complete suite.

The tracing core is exported as traceAffectedTests so a bounded local
gate can reuse it.

Fixes #11381

* ci: follow verifier source loads and named verifiers when tracing script modules

- Module URLs (new URL("./x.mts", import.meta.url), as loaded by
  importVerifierSource) are import edges.
- A test that names a verifier or shared module the change reaches is
  selected, not only one that names a changed path.
- A changed shared module that no test reaches runs the complete suite
  even when other changes select tests.

* ci: select tests that start the built server beside a changed presentation owner (#11519)

* ci: select tests that start the built server beside a changed presentation owner

A test that starts the built CLI or MCP server reaches server, contract,
entrypoint and CLI modules through the build, not an import, so a change
there selected none of them (#11146 failed on main this way). Such a
test is now selected when it, or a helper it imports, starts
scripts/rea.mjs or dist/, and it imports a module from the changed
owner's directory.

Fixes #11366

* ci: recognise only the repository's built entry points as runtime launchers

A package subpath such as ajv/dist/2020.js matched the dist/ pattern, so
in-process tests importing Ajv counted as built-runtime launchers.

* ci: balance selected test shards by recorded duration (#11522)

A selected PR run split its files across groups round-robin, so a few
slow files could land together. The plan now records the selected files
and a shard count (version 3), and each job runs one --shard of the
selection through the exact-test runner with the timing history main
already publishes, so the CI sequencer balances shards by per-file
duration (the median for files without a timing). Without history,
Vitest's own deterministic sharding applies.

commits.subject: refactor(native)!: report native initializer coverage as partial or unknown instead of incomplete (#11483)
commits.body:
refactor(native)!: report native initializer coverage as partial or unknown instead of incomplete (#11483)

* refactor(native)!: report native initializer coverage as partial or unknown instead of incomplete

inspect_native_initializers coverage.status was `incomplete` for both a known gap
(slot budget, unreadable arrays, withheld names) and undetermined coverage
(relocation, fixup, symbol or mapping coverage, duplicate or unterminated dynamic
tags). The scans now record which one each observation causes and the report
uses the shared coverage status: `partial` for a known gap, `unknown` when
completeness cannot be determined, unknown winning when both occur. The
top-level `status` keeps `parsed` / `incomplete`.

BREAKING CHANGE: inspect_native_initializers `coverage.status` reports `partial`
or `unknown` instead of `incomplete`. Treat both as not complete; `partial`
means declared slots or names were left unreported, `unknown` means the
report could not establish completeness.

* fix(native): report a withheld object-file relocation symbol name as partial coverage

nameAt labelled every name over the budget as unknown coverage. In an MH_OBJECT
the relocation symbol it reads is the reported entry's own import or defined
name, so withholding it is a known gap. The caller now states the effect: the
object-file relocation symbol is partial (and is read only when the entry
reports it), the LC_SYMTAB address index stays unknown (#11500).

commits.subject: feat(evidence)!: name the Evidence subject by its target identity (format revision 2) (#11416)
commits.body:
feat(evidence)!: name the Evidence subject by its target identity (format revision 2) (#11416)

* feat(evidence)!: name the Evidence subject by its target identity (format revision 2)

The Evidence subject carries subject.identity (kind, sha256, format,
architecture, selection) and the Evidence ID commits to it, so raw/DOL
entry points and ESP flash offsets of the same bytes are different
subjects. Every record declares evidence_format: 2; revision 1 bundles,
standalone records and snapshots are refused with the recreate guidance.
binaryTargetIdentity is the one projection of an open target, used by
Evidence and snapshot comparison.

BREAKING CHANGE: Evidence format revision 2. Evidence IDs commit to the
subject's target identity (subject.identity, including the raw/DOL entry
point or ESP flash offsets), and every record declares evidence_format: 2.
Evidence bundles, records and analysis snapshots from earlier releases are
refused; recreate the observations with this release.

* refactor(analysis-view): read parent subjects through the Evidence identity accessors (#11423)

Analysis views compare their parent's file identity (evidenceFileTarget)
and take path and digest from evidenceSubjectTarget instead of reading
the subject's digest, format and architecture members, which duplicate
subject.identity until they are removed. A counted guard
(evidence-subject-declaration-read) keeps new direct reads out and
records the 20 remaining files.

* fix(evidence): carry format refusals through Evidence readers and bind target selections

- safeParseEvidence/safeParseImmutableEvidence return the format refusal as
  an expected failure; every consumer maps it to the one integrity refusal
  with the recreate guidance. An unmarked object is an earlier record only
  when it has every member records have always carried.
- ArtifactProvider inventory roots and provider subjects that name the
  target's own bytes carry the target's selection (ESP flash offsets).
- Snapshot rows bind only Evidence whose identity, selection included,
  matches the snapshot target.
- Entry-point selections use the raw-binary entry point form.

* fix(evidence): refuse unauthenticated or earlier-format records instead of reading them as absent

- recognizeEvidence (evidenceValidation) replaces tryParseEvidence: input
  without an evidence_id is not Evidence (ok(undefined)); a record that names
  one but fails authentication or is from another format revision is an
  EvidenceIntegrityError carrying the recreate guidance, never undefined.
- Direct analysis retains that refusal as a secondary failure instead of
  silently skipping source capture; cleanup projection, source-closure
  annotation and the flutter, debugger and release-exposure recoveries use
  the same owner (the last three previously read the unauthenticated schema).
- A desktop capture.json from an earlier format is refused with the recreate
  guidance instead of "not desktop application capture Evidence".

* fix(evidence): advertise revision 2 ledger examples and rank delivery omissions by serialized size

- The obligation ledger and reconstruction coverage examples named
  evidence_format 1, which revision 2 refuses; they now use
  EVIDENCE_FORMAT_REVISION.
- MCP delivery chose which unretained recovery to omit by a parsed-storage
  lower bound clipped at the response budget. Once revision 2 subjects made
  the source record's estimate cross the budget, both candidates tied at the
  clip and the smaller source was omitted ahead of the larger completed
  observation. Candidates are now ranked by serialized size, which is what
  the budget counts.

* refactor(native): compare function snapshots by their Evidence target identity (#11450)

Function snapshots carry the subject's file target identity instead of the
duplicated subject declaration. Call paths and function comparisons compare
targets through sameTargetIdentity, so the same bytes opened at a different
raw entry point or ESP flash offset no longer count as one coordinate space:
build_call_path refuses the mix, and compare_functions no longer matches
entries by address across selections. Structural candidates and native
function matching read the architecture and digest through
evidenceFileTarget.

Refs #11417

* refactor(artifacts): compare artifact and WASM summaries by their Evidence target identity (#11461)

Artifact comparison authenticates a summary against its retained inventory
through sameTargetIdentity and rebinds the alias with the whole target,
selection included, so a flash-selected inventory summary taken under an
alias path is no longer refused. WASM comparison, the analysis view
artifact projection and the inventory root check read the digest, format
and display path through the Evidence identity accessors.

Refs #11417

* refactor(evidence): read record subjects through the identity accessors in JS, managed, ledger and bundle readers (#11470)

JavaScript application graphs, runtime reconciliation, managed inspection
and native verification sources, the record summary filter, the ledger's
residual-unknown target and bundle scope selection read the subject digest,
format and display path through evidenceFileTarget and
evidenceSubjectDisplay. No comparison changes: each reader matches one
record's facts against its own payload or a caller filter.

Refs #11417

* refactor(evidence)!: name the Evidence subject only by its target identity (#11497)

* refactor(evidence)!: name the Evidence subject only by its target identity

The subject keeps `identity` and the display facts `name` and `local_path`.
The duplicated `digest`, `format` and `architecture` members are removed; the
format-owned declaration now validates the identity itself. Readers the type
checker found move to the owner accessors; untyped reads in verify scripts,
the efficiency harness and test matchers move to `subject.identity`. The
`evidence-subject-declaration-read` text guard and its baseline are deleted.

Fixes #11473
Refs #11417

BREAKING CHANGE: the Evidence subject no longer has `digest`, `format` or
`architecture`; read `subject.identity.sha256`, `subject.identity.format` and
`subject.identity.architecture`. A record that still carries them is refused.

* test(evidence): give the Flutter verifier fixture the identity subject and check the DOL declaration without the ID

* test(evidence): drop the removed subject members from the declaration matrix and tamper fixtures

* feat(evidence)!: give every Evidence record an explicit subject identity (#11536)

* feat(evidence)!: give every Evidence record an explicit subject identity

A producer that cannot name a file passes an `unknown` target identity
with a closed reason (derived-from-linked-evidence, not-observed,
unsupported-subject) instead of no subject. The subject is non-null;
unknown subjects have no display facts. The generic missing-subject
limitation and `subjectUnavailableReason` are removed; producer-specific
explanations are ordinary limitations. Comparison identity requires the
derived unknown, and null-subject consumers ask the owner accessors.

Refs #11417

BREAKING CHANGE: every Evidence record has a subject. A record without a
file target names `subject.identity` `{ "kind": "unknown", "reason": … }`
with `name` and `local_path` null, instead of `subject: null` and the
limitation "Artifact identity is unavailable for this observation.".
Their Evidence IDs change.

* fix(evidence): name explicit unknown subjects in JavaScript callers and keep a managed graph's file subject

The verification scripts are not type-checked, so five createEvidence
callers still passed undefined (or a missing first target) after the subject
became required. They now pass unknownTarget("not-observed").

A managed application graph chose the first present input subject. Every
subject is now present, so an unknown artifact subject hid a file subject on
the member or boundary Evidence. The graph now takes the first input subject
that names a file.

* test(evidence): assert the subject kind instead of a presence the type now guarantees

Every Evidence record has a subject after this change, so test guards and
assertions that checked it for null always passed. Each now checks that the
fixture subject names a file, or is removed where a later fileIdentity,
fileSubjectTarget or fileSubjectDisplay call already requires that. Non-null
assertions on Evidence subjects are removed; analysis-view inputs, whose
subject is optional, keep an undefined check.

* test(evidence): expect the Evidence subject format under its identity

Two boundary tests still matched subject.format, which slice 2e moved into
subject.identity. toMatchObject is not type-checked against the Evidence
shape, so they failed only when run (the signature test on macOS).

commits.subject: fix(javascript): move reader effect reads into the effect log and order require and process rebinding by activation (#11356)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): move reader effect reads into the effect log and order require and process rebinding by activation (#11356)

* refactor(javascript): move the last reader effect reads into the effect log

* refactor(javascript): skip escapes when a reader asks only about member writes

* fix(javascript): order require and process rebinding by activation timing (#11479)

* refactor(javascript): ask one ordering whether require was rebound before a call

* refactor(javascript): order process replacement by activation, like require

* fix(javascript): keep instance field values out of literal-loop source ordering

* fix(javascript): stop effect ordering at instance field values inside the effect

semanticEffectFollowsReference proved that an assignment follows a read
written inside its own right-hand side, even when the read sits in an
instance field value, which runs on construction after the assignment.
process = class { value = process.env.MODE; }; new process() therefore kept
the original process identity, and require = class { fs = require('fs') }
kept a Node module origin. The first walk now stops at instance field
values like it stops at function bodies.

* fix(javascript): attribute process effects that may reach the original object (#11521)

* fix(javascript): attribute process effects that may reach the original object

A write or escape through the global process object was attributed to
node:process only when no replacement of process may precede it. Effects
need the opposite question: they reach the original unless a replacement
with a fresh object is proven to run before them. The effect log gains
ambientReplacementPrecedes (the must counterpart of the may-observe
queries), RequireOrigin owns the effect question, and member mutation
asks it for direct, qualified and ambient process effects.

Refs #11488

* fix(javascript): prove a process replacement with the global path reader

ambientReplacementPrecedes accepted any earlier fresh assignment of the
process path, even when a later write might restore the original or when
the assignment went through a possible alias of the global object. The
global path reader already owns definite replacement at a site (it checks
the written namespace and every competing write), so the effect question
asks it and keeps only the freshness check. ambientReplacementPrecedes is
removed.

* refactor(mcp): bind artifact and bundle comparison through an acquiring derived binding that owns their artifact resource scope

compare_artifacts and compare_bundles registered bespoke handlers that read caller-named files under the server's artifact resource scope and then repeated the session-derived delivery. The derived binding kind now takes an optional acquisition with the resource scope it reads under; the table passes the scope, the readers open and release handles in it (failed releases stay owned for retry), and acquisition failures are delivered unchanged. The artifact unknown and the bundle Evidence moved to application owners.

commits.subject: feat(snapshots)!: persist the target identity as the snapshot target (#11551)
commits.body:
feat(snapshots)!: persist the target identity as the snapshot target (#11551)

* feat(snapshots)!: persist the target identity as the snapshot target

The snapshot target is now `{ kind, identity }`, where `identity` is the
FileTargetIdentity that `binaryTargetIdentity` produces and `kind` is the
binary kind query IDs commit to. The per-format target projection and
`snapshotTargetIdentity` are deleted; the schema checks the format's
selection, architecture and kind instead of keeping one union arm per format.

Entry execution subjects use the Evidence subject shape (file or explicit
unknown), so a snapshot entry commits to the same identity, including the
selection, as its Evidence record. Workflow entries take the subject of the
workflow's own Evidence. Replay no longer re-derives the selection from the
open target.

`FileTargetSelection` gains `universal-slice` (`offset`, `size`, and the FAT
`cpu_type`/`cpu_subtype` when target admission supplied the FAT table, else
null). `binaryTargetIdentity` produces it for `mach-o-universal` targets, so
Evidence and snapshots for different slices of one container no longer share
an identity.

Refs #11417

BREAKING CHANGE: analysis snapshot files change shape: `target` is
`{ kind, identity: { kind: "file", sha256, format, architecture, selection } }`
and entry `execution.subject` is the Evidence subject

commits.subject: fix(javascript): count escapes of Function.prototype before trusting call and apply (#11501)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): count escapes of Function.prototype before trusting call and apply (#11501)

* fix(javascript): count escapes of Function.prototype before trusting call and apply

* fix(javascript): key cached returned references on ambient escapes too

* fix(javascript): track arguments of directly invoked functions through their parameters (#11538)

* fix(javascript): track arguments of directly invoked functions through their parameters

Passing a value to a function expression invoked where it is defined, such
as a UMD header (function(root, factory){...})(this, ...), recorded an
escape of the argument to unevaluated code although the callee's body is
source code whose effects are indexed. javascriptSemanticDirectInvocations
owns which arguments reach such a callee only through a plain parameter;
the ambient path resolver and member mutation indexing follow that
parameter back to its argument, and neither records an escape for it.
Spread and rest lists, pattern or default parameters, arguments and direct
eval keep the escape, as do unknown callees.

Refs #11499

* fix(javascript): escape values thrown out of a function and scan arguments once

A value thrown out of a function or class body reaches handlers the
throw-to-catch index does not link to it. Arguments of a directly invoked
function used to hide this behind the call escape; they no longer do, and
captured values had the same gap. The binding pass records such throws,
and ambient and member effect indexing escape their values at the throw.

Which functions name 'arguments' is now found in one program walk instead
of one subtree scan per directly invoked function.

* perf(javascript): find shadowed direct-invocation parameters in one pass

* fix(javascript): settle Object and Reflect static call receivers in one owner (#11543)

* fix(javascript): settle Object and Reflect static call receivers in one owner

Ambient write indexing skipped the receiver escape of any resolved Object
or Reflect static call, even when source code had replaced the method,
while member mutation indexing escaped the constructor for every such
call. The second escape (global.Object contents) made each later
Function.prototype.call/apply check uncertain in bundles that call
Object.defineProperty or Object.freeze. Ambient indexing now settles these
receivers once all ambient writes are known: the constructor escapes only
when a write or escape may replace the method before the call, and member
mutation reuses that decision through retainedGlobalCallReceivers.

Refs #11535

* fix(javascript): retain the receiver only for native Object and Reflect statics

A resolved Object member that is not one of the language's own static
methods (for example one Object inherits from Function.prototype, or an
unknown name) may be user code that receives the constructor, so its call
keeps the receiver escape.

* fix(javascript): look up intrinsic and builtin method tables by own key only

NATIVE_STATIC_METHODS and BUILTIN_RECEIVER_METHODS were plain objects, so
an owner such as globalThis.constructor or a module named 'constructor' or
'toString' found an inherited Object.prototype function and analysis threw
a TypeError on '.has'. Both are Maps now.

* fix(javascript): escape values thrown uncaught at the top level (#11556)

A value thrown uncaught at the top level reaches the host's uncaught-exception handlers (process.on('uncaughtException'), window.onerror), which may change it before a timer or callback reads it. The binding pass recorded escaping throws only when the walk reached a function or class body; a throw that reaches the program without a handler now escapes the same way.

* fix(javascript): follow direct-invocation arguments through returned references and function arguments properties

A callable argument of a directly invoked function no longer escapes at the call, but the shared returned-reference owner could not follow the parameter to it, so patch(get()) inside the callee lost the escape of the value get returns. The returned-reference walk now follows the parameter to its argument like the write and escape walkers.

A sloppy function's arguments property (f["arguments"], g.caller.arguments from a function it calls) exposes its activation's arguments. A non-strict callee is no longer tracked through its parameters when the program reads an arguments or caller property by a static key. The strictness reader moves beside javaScriptProgramStrictness so both modules share it.

commits.subject: fix(native): keep unreported value-flow and archive coverage unknown, and exempt generation caps by reason marker (#11288)
commits.body:
fix(native): keep unreported value-flow and archive coverage unknown, and exempt generation caps by reason marker (#11288)

* fix(native): keep unreported value-flow truncation and archive decode coverage unknown

* test(verify): count multiline optional-fact defaults and pin the guard's exclusions

* fix(domain): keep unknown counts and costs unknown in comparison and coverage summaries (#11325)

* fix(domain): keep unknown counts and costs unknown in comparison and coverage summaries

* refactor(verify): exempt legitimate optional-fact defaults with a reasoned marker (#11355)

* refactor(verify): exempt legitimate optional-fact defaults with a reasoned marker

The optional-fact-default guard counted request defaults and absence that
is modelled elsewhere as hidden unknowns. A comment
`// optional-fact-default: <reason>` on the default's line or the line
before now exempts it; the guard reads unstripped source for the marker and
ignores matches inside comment lines.

Marked: the two evidence paging offsets and four Swift literal reads whose
absence swiftLiteralCoverage reports. Removed instead of marked: jsdiff 9
types Change.count as required, so its two `?? 0` defaults were dead; the
evidence link traversal now carries retained records, so it no longer
re-looks them up behind `?? []`. Baseline 31 -> 22.

* fix(verify): blank comment spans instead of skipping comment-led lines in the optional-fact guard

Skipping a match whose line starts like a comment hid live code after a
leading block comment and counted defaults inside a block comment without
leading stars. The counter now blanks comment text (keeping offsets and line
breaks, skipping string literals) and matches the blanked code, while
exemption markers are still read from the original lines.

* refactor(domain): mark optional-fact defaults whose absence is not an observation (#11389)

* refactor(domain): mark optional-fact defaults whose absence is not an observation

Per-site review of the remaining optional-fact-default entries. Each marked
default is a caller option (trace ignore_fields, environment rules), a list
whose producer omits the empty case (unknown_size_frames, the schema's
min-1 representation_node_ids), caveat text whose completeness another field
carries (call diagnostics, unresolved calls, semantic resource limits), or
absence that already turns the result unknown (Wasm interface inventory,
WebMCP discovery, managed ExportedType rows, legacy integrity mismatch IDs).

Left counted: webCaptureDiff redirects (2; the CDP producer always records
them, so absence is a legacy record that should compare as unknown, not
as no redirects) and HopperCallerReconciliation (2; index-miss semantics not
yet verified). Baseline 22 -> 4.

* fix(browser): compare redirects as unknown when a capture predates redirect recording (#11402)

* fix(browser): compare redirects as unknown when a capture predates redirect recording

The CDP producer records every request's redirect chain, empty when there was none; a record without one predates redirect recording (#986). Comparing it against a current capture reported the network dimension as unchanged, treating the missing chain as "no redirects". Redirects are now compared only when both captures recorded them, and the network dimension is otherwise unknown with a reason; proven membership changes are still reported.

* refactor(hopper): interpret a caller-index miss once at the lookup (#11403)

The forward index holds observations from the examined procedures only, and relationship coverage stays unknown with the scan facts as its reason. A miss therefore adds no callers without showing there are none; the lookup now says so once instead of four optional reads defaulting at each site. The optional-fact-default baseline is now empty.

* docs(javascript): state why an omitted representation list adds no nodes

* fix(verify): count optional-fact defaults from parsed TypeScript, not comment-blanked text

The guard blanked comments with a hand-written scanner and matched a regular expression on the rest, so a default quoted in a string counted and a regular expression holding /* hid the code after it. It now walks the TypeScript syntax tree for property reads defaulted with ?? 0, ?? [] or ?? false, and reads exemption markers only from comment trivia.

* fix(verify): tokenize optional-fact defaults without a compiler and count chained defaults

* fix(verify): match whole optional-fact default expressions across calls and operators

* fix(verify): count optional-fact defaults in template substitutions and after postfix updates, and tie markers to their own expression

* refactor(verify): exempt generation and sample caps from the constant-maximum-slice guard by reason marker (#11454)

* refactor(verify): exempt generation and sample caps from the constant-maximum-slice guard by reason marker

* fix(verify): read reason markers only from real line comments

* fix(verify): read reason markers from the shared source tokenizer

* fix(verify): read a regular expression after a control head as a statement start

The shared tokenizer treated every closing parenthesis as the end of an operand,
so in `if (ready) /[/*]/.test(v)` it read `/[` as division and `/*` inside the
regex as a block comment, hiding the rest of the file from the marker-aware
guards. Parentheses are now tracked: the `)` closing an if/while/for/with head
allows a regular expression, while a call's `)` still means division.

* fix(verify): keep a keyword-named member call out of control-head detection

`policy.if(ready) / (…)` was read as an if-statement head, so the division was
taken for a regular expression and the denominator's optional-fact default was
not counted. A control keyword after `.` or `?.` is a member call.

* refactor(verify): exempt budget-arithmetic cursors and tallies by a not-an-allowance marker (#11493)

* refactor(verify): exempt budget-arithmetic cursors and tallies by a not-an-allowance marker

The budget-arithmetic guard cannot tell a scan cursor, an observed total, a
string being assembled or a tail buffer's retained length from an allowance
when each is compared with a limit. A field declaration marked
`// not-an-allowance: <reason>` (read through the shared reason-marker scan)
is no longer counted. The four remaining sites carry a marker, so the
baseline is empty and removed.

* refactor(verify): exempt detail levels, lifecycle states and domain vocabularies from the completeness-enum guard by reason marker (#11510)

A zod enum containing "complete" is counted as a local coverage vocabulary. Eleven
are not coverage: a caller-chosen detail level, how far a command or session
ran, and format states (GPU decode depth, WASM name section, SQLite column
details). They now carry `// detail-level:`, `// lifecycle-state:` or
`// domain-vocabulary:` with a reason, read through the shared reason-marker
scan (which gains an optional predicate for the matches a guard counts).
local-completeness-enum: 22 -> 11 on this branch.

* fix(verify): bind a not-an-allowance marker to its own class field

Exemptions were a file-wide set of names, so a marked tally in one class hid an
unmarked allowance with the same name in another, and a marked object property
could exempt a class field. Markers now exempt only a member declaration (at
class member depth) of the top-level class that contains it, and the named-
allowance count is taken per class so the same scoping applies to it.

* fix(artifacts): keep main's resources import in the Deno standalone reader after merging main

* fix(verify): start an expression after a template substitution and a non-member keyword, and accept any marker reason

The shared tokenizer read the `/` after `${` as division, so a regular
expression holding `/*` in a substitution hid the rest of the file from
every tokenizer-based guard, and it treated property names such as
`row.return` as keywords. Tokens now record whether template text opens a
substitution and whether a name is an expression keyword (not after `.` or
`?.`), and the regular-expression rule and the optional-fact-default operand
rule read those facts. The optional-fact-default guard reads markers through
reason-marker's isReasonMarker, so any non-empty reason exempts, as for the
other reason markers.

* fix(verify): blank comments with the shared tokenizer before matching architecture guards (#11573)

* fix(verify): blank comments with the shared tokenizer before matching architecture guards

The guards stripped comments with a regular expression that took a `/*`
inside a string, template or regular expression for a comment opener and
deleted code up to the next `*/`. src/flutter/FlutterBuildProvider.ts's
"lib/*/libapp.so" text hid four --pool-policy remediation strings from
cli-option-text-outside-cli. blankComments in source-tokens.mjs now owns
comment removal for the architecture guards and the reason-marker scan: it
blanks comment tokens in place (newlines kept) and keeps strings, templates
and regular expressions. The scan behind it retains only the last tokens it
reads, and whitespace runs are skipped at once.

The cli-option-text-outside-cli baseline records FlutterBuildProvider.ts at
its true count of 4; no other baseline changed.

Fixes #11477

* fix(verify): read a regular expression after a statement block and keep comment offsets for wide characters

The tokenizer now records whether each `{` opens a statement block or an
object literal (from the token before it) and marks the `}` that closes a
block, after which a statement, and so a regular expression, can start; an
object literal's `}` still ends an operand. blankComments replaces each run
of comment text with one space per UTF-16 unit, so a surrogate pair no longer
shifts later offsets.

* chore(verify): drop the Flutter CLI-text baseline entry now that main names no option there

feat(cutter): name the response limit on an unknown-completion command failure (#11598)

When a Cutter response exceeded the framed transport limit after the command
was sent, the client kept the structured limit error only as message prose:
the command result's `message` named the bytes and the launch seed, and the
returned failure (completion unknown) carried no limit. The client result now

so it projects as `details.limit` (`bridge.max_request_bytes` with its
effective value and source). The test asserts the fact instead of the prose.

commits.subject: fix(evidence)!: require ESP flash_dump and PE unsigned attribute OIDs (#11595)
commits.body:
fix(evidence)!: require ESP flash_dump and PE unsigned attribute OIDs (#11595)

* fix(evidence)!: require ESP flash_dump and PE unsigned attribute OIDs

Both fields were optional only for Evidence recorded before REA reported
them (6.8.0 and earlier). Every producer writes them: the ESP image reader
and facts builder write `flash_dump` (null unless the file is a flash dump
read from a later address), and the PE certificate parser writes
`unsigned_attribute_oids` (null when the signer has none). They are now
required and nullable, and the inspection hint no longer branches on an
absent `flash_dump`. The ESP acceptance test that read pre-6.9 inventory
Evidence now checks that such Evidence is refused.

A call-path comment called Evidence without relationship coverage "legacy";
providers that report no coverage still produce it, so the comment now says
so.

BREAKING CHANGE: inline inventory Evidence for an ESP image root without
`format_metadata.flash_dump`, and PE certificate Evidence whose signers lack
`unsigned_attribute_oids`, are refused as invalid input. Recreate the

commits.subject: perf(reference): overlap reference-source identity lookups in traversal order (#11585)
commits.body:
perf(reference): overlap reference-source identity lookups in traversal order (#11585)

The reference-source reader made about nine serial filesystem calls per
directory. It now runs its read-only identity lookups ahead of their turn,
bounded to four running at once (libuv's default filesystem concurrency):
opening admissions of the next pending directories, metadata of the next
listed names, and closing admissions of directories already enumerated.
Results are applied in traversal order: policy and exclusion callbacks keep
their order, the first error in traversal order is returned, a failure a
started lookup observed is retained, and every started lookup settles before
the read returns. Running opening admissions are counted, so older siblings
buried by deeper levels cannot raise concurrency with tree depth.

Measured on macOS, Node 24.22.1: the 130,000-directory regression's
reference-source read 27.5 s -> 17.2 s; a 20,000-directory flat tree
2.1-2.3 s -> 1.2 s; an 8,641-file source tree 1.41 s -> 1.31 s.

commits.subject: fix(rust): report compiler-path byte trimming only when it removes a path (#11582)
commits.body:
fix(rust): report compiler-path byte trimming only when it removes a path (#11582)

* fix(rust): report compiler-path byte trimming only when it removes a path

When the reader's compiler guidance did not fit the complete-report
allowance, trimming replaced the reader's coverage (max_rustc_hashes) and its
guidance with the shorter byte-trimming record. In a narrow allowance range
that swap alone made every hash fit, so the report kept all paths but claimed
they were omitted by the byte budget and lost the count-limit control.

Now, when every path fits, the reader's record and control stay and only its
guidance text (which restates rustc_commit.coverage) is left out; if even
that does not fit, one path is dropped so the recorded byte coverage is true.

* fix(rust): keep the complete compiler record whenever it fits without guidance

Check the reader's record without its guidance before building the trimming record, so trimming always removes a path and the unreachable fallback is gone. The boundary test now requires a tight budget that keeps every path with the reader's coverage record.
