commits.subject: fix(native): size link-time relocation kinds in x86-64 and AArch64 objects (#12235)
commits.body:
fix(native): size link-time relocation kinds in x86-64 and AArch64 objects (#12235)

* fix(native): keep an assumed relocation width from reporting a section overrun

inspect_native_initializers assumed that a relocation of a type it does not
size writes a whole word. For a 4-byte field that ends its section, such as
R_X86_64_PLT32 or R_AARCH64_CALL26 on a tail call that ends .text, the assumed
word ran past the section, so the object was reported incomplete with
"A section relocation extends beyond its target mapping".

An assumed width is now narrowed to the bytes its mapping holds. A relocation
of known width that runs past its section is still reported.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(native): use the tail-call relocation clang emits for AArch64

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(native): size link-time relocation kinds instead of narrowing an assumed width

Review found that narrowing an assumed word to its mapping hid a real overrun
of an unlisted kind and, in a linked image, a slot behind zero-fill bytes.
The mapping remainder does not establish what a relocation writes.

The section walk is restored to its previous logic. The width table now sizes
the link-time kinds clang emits into x86-64 and AArch64 objects, as the i386
row already does, so a call that ends .text is a known 4-byte field. A kind
the table does not hold keeps its assumed word and its overrun note.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(plist): keep literal carriage returns in XML plist keys and strings (#12236)

The XML plist reader replaced every literal CR and CRLF with LF before
parsing. CoreFoundation keeps them, so REA reported a different string than
plutil for the same file, and two keys that differ only in their line ending
collapsed into one repeated key.

The document is now parsed as written. Source spans for integer, real, date
and data literals already count CR, CRLF and LF as one line break each.

commits.subject: refactor(errors): compose multi-part provider cleanup failures through one owner (#12002)
commits.body:
refactor(errors): compose multi-part provider cleanup failures through one owner (#12002)

* refactor(errors): compose multi-part provider cleanup failures through one owner

CdpBrowserProvider, CdpElectronProvider, FridaInstrumentationManager and
PlaywrightBrowserScenarioProvider each built the same composite by hand: a
ProviderCleanupError listing the parts' resources, an AggregateError cause,
and bindCleanupDependencies over the parts. providerCleanupErrorFromFailures
in src/domain/analysisErrorCleanup.ts now owns that composition. `causes`
keeps non-AnalysisError failures in the aggregate cause without making them
own completion, as the CDP providers did; `message` keeps the aggregate
messages Frida and Playwright used.

Tests: helper unit tests, new close-composition tests for both CDP providers,
and a Playwright test with two failed cleanup retries. They pass on the base
revision and on this change, and fail when the helper drops the dependency
binding, the extra causes or the message.

Lowers the cleanup-dependency-binding baseline to 43 files / 73 sites.

Refs #11859

explanatory reason or aggregate message. A harmless wording change passes;

commits.subject: fix(environment): map id-list elements when a scalar set also changed (#7161)
commits.body:
fix(environment): map id-list elements when a scalar set also changed (#7161)

* fix(environment): map id-list elements when a scalar set also changed

When comparing an answer's scalar id list, the id mapping ran only on the
sameItems fast path. Once one element genuinely changed, or the lengths
differed, array fell to pairwise comparison that compared each element
without its id-list field, so scalar skipped the mapping: comparing live
[101,102] with env [1,9] under 101->1, 102->2 reported /ids/0 (101 vs 1) as
a change as well as the real /ids/1 (102 vs 9).

Thread an idList flag from array to scalar, set by the same per-element rule
sameItems uses, so a mapped element matches and is counted as a normalised
id while a genuine change is reported with its original value. Non-id arrays
are unchanged.

* fix(environment): pair id-list survivors by translated identity

The first fix mapped each id-list element but still paired scalar arrays by
position, so a survivor that shifted position paired with the wrong item:
[101,102] versus [2] under 101->1, 102->2 still emitted a false /ids/0 value
difference even though 102->2 is the survivor and only the removal changed.

Pair id-list survivors by the environment identity they map to, then any
remaining live and environment items by position. The translation is one owner
shared with sameItems, and the paired comparison still maps the original live
id and reports its original value on a genuine change. Non-id arrays keep
positional pairing.

* fix(environment): keep id-list order checks to matched survivors

#idListPairs appended a positional fallback pair for a replaced id, and the
order check read every pair, so a single surviving identity that shifted
emitted a spurious order difference: [101,102] versus [2,9] under 101->1,
102->2 reported order as well as the real /ids/0 value change.

Return the identity-matched survivor pairs separately and compute order from
them alone; the positional fallbacks are value replacements, not the same
item in a new position. Two or more reordered survivors still report order.

* perf(environment): limit ID recovery to conflicting components

* fix(environment): prove response list order across maximum matches

* fix(environment): detect complete duplicate ID list reorders

commits.subject: fix(zstd): share exact-frame Zstandard decoding across ELF and OTA (#12416)
commits.body:
fix(zstd): share exact-frame Zstandard decoding across ELF and OTA (#12416)

* fix(zstd): share exact-frame Zstandard decoding across ELF and OTA

Walk RFC 8878 frames once so ELF sections, Android OTA REPLACE_ZSTD, and GPU payloads reject truncated headers, blocks, checksums, and trailing bytes on every supported Node runtime. Bound that walk with the runtime zstd.max_frames setting.

* fix(zstd): keep frame output tight and report GPU frame-cap refusals

Copy each Node 22 frame off its decoder chunk before the next frame is decoded. Map a GPU zstd.max_frames refusal through the resource-limit contract instead of a provider failure.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(zstd): keep frame-cap refusals and bad seeds out of malformed results

Project zstd.max_frames through one resource-limit helper for ELF notes, DWARF, GPU, and artifact reads. An invalid REA_ZSTD_MAX_FRAMES seed stays a configuration failure, and frame-header tests cover content size, window, dictionary id, and RLE blocks.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(zstd): yield GPU frame decoding so cancellation can land

The frame-by-frame fallback awaits a caller pause before each data frame. GPU yields and checks the read signal there, so a many-frame payload does not finish before a disconnect is observed.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(zstd): advertise the frame cap and keep strict GPU decode cancellable

List every operation that enforces zstd.max_frames, including GPU, DWARF, and ELF notes. The strict sequence uses the async decoder and checks the caller signal again after it returns, and a single output buffer is not copied a second time.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(zstd): refresh analysis-setting schemas and GPU frame-cap projection

Regenerate the advertised input summaries for inspect_analysis_settings and update_analysis_settings. GPU inventory now throws the projected zstd.max_frames resource limit from payload decode and #retainFailure, so the adjustable setting survives the public failure.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* style(gpu): format the frame-cap projection throw

oxfmt keeps the zstd.max_frames throw in #retainFailure on one line so CI format:check matches the local formatter.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(zstd): yield after the last frame-by-frame GPU decode

The fallback returned success in the same turn as the final synchronous frame, so a queued abort was still invisible to the caller's signal check. Pause once more before that success, matching the strict sequence.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(zstd): yield ELF, OTA, and DWARF frame decoding on the caller signal

The synchronous frame loop ignored abort signals owned by inspect_elf_notes, inspect_dwarf_units, and Android OTA partition reads. Those callers now use the cooperative decoder and yield before Zstandard work, and 32-frame cancellations cover each path.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(zstd): observe cancellation during structural parsing

* fix(zstd): project section-name frame caps at the ELF directory boundary

readElfDirectoryFromBuffer now requires the caller's operation and throws the adjustable zstd.max_frames resource limit. Hardening, unwind, and the other directory consumers keep that typed refusal instead of an adapter or I/O error.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(zstd): preserve optional ELF evidence when frames are capped

* fix(zip): validate Zstandard members through frame completion (#12461)

fix(zip): require complete Zstandard member frames

* fix(elf): yield hardening section name decoding

* fix(elf): yield section names for unwind and export reads

* fix(zstd): yield ELF directory reads that already own a cancellation signal

Hardening, unwind, initializers, exports, kernel modules, debug link, and Android JNI now read section names through the cooperative directory when their caller has a signal. Readers with no signal stay synchronous.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(elf): share one initializer directory and retain its snapshot

* fix(android): reuse the admitted JNI ELF directory

* fix(elf): retain optional debug candidate evidence through cooperative decoding

* fix(zstd): yield ELF section names for Go, Rust, and IL2CPP

These inspections already own an abort signal. Their ELF directory read now uses the cooperative container decoder so a queued cancellation can land during a many-frame section-name table.

Co-authored-by: morluto <morluto@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(elf): recognize compressed kernel modules before ELF decoding

The cooperative module reader decoded the bytes as ELF before the container check, so gzip, xz, and zstd modules became malformed images. The compression check now returns the unsupported-container report first.

commits.subject: feat(artifacts): inspect NES 2.0 container headers and regions (#10674)
commits.body:
feat(artifacts): inspect NES 2.0 container headers and regions (#10674)

* feat(artifacts): inspect NES 2.0 container headers and regions

Problem: the iNES lane refused every header whose byte 7 bits 2-3 select
NES 2.0, so NES 2.0 cartridges could not be inventoried, extracted or
reconstructed even though their file layout extends classic iNES.

Fix: the single iNES-family header parser now reads NES 2.0 alongside
classic iNES. It reports the 12-bit mapper, submapper, 12-bit and
exponent-multiplier PRG/CHR sizes, declared PRG/CHR RAM and NVRAM sizes,
CPU/PPU timing, console type with Vs. System and extended console codes,
miscellaneous ROM count and default expansion device in a "nes-2.0"
header variant; classic headers keep their exact serialization. Regions
add one prg.bin/chr.bin for exponent sizes and misc-rom.bin for the bytes
after CHR-ROM when miscellaneous ROMs are declared. Oversized
declarations (with exact totals, including exponent sizes beyond safe
integers), nonzero unused header bits, empty PRG-ROM and declared but
absent miscellaneous ROM bytes are refused through the existing format
error. Nested byte classification now admits NES 2.0 through the same
parser. The reader limitation, tool description, guide and skill
reference now state that UNIF remains unsupported and that RAM, timing
and console values are declarations.

Validation: new synthetic NES 2.0 unit cases fail on the base (15 of 24)
and pass after the change; focused boundary and acceptance iNES suites
(75 tests) pass, including NES 2.0 inventory, extraction, reconstruction
and compiled CLI inspection; npm run check:fast passes.

Refs morluto/rea#2072

* test(artifacts): extract an exponent-sized NES 2.0 ROM area

Review follow-up for NES 2.0 headers.

The exponent-multiplier case stopped at parseInesLayout, and the
extraction test used counted ROM units, so prg.bin and chr.bin from
an exponent-sized area never went through the reader or extraction.
A boundary case now builds a NES 2.0 file with a 2^10 * 3 byte PRG-ROM
area beside one counted 8 KiB CHR-ROM unit. It checks the header omits
the PRG unit count, the source offsets of prg.bin and chr/000.bin,
the verified reconstruction order, and that the extracted regions
match the original bytes exactly.

Tests: tests/boundary/filesystem/inesArtifact.test.ts passes (38).

* refactor(artifacts): read NES header bytes through one helper

The NES 2.0 declaration added a sixth raw Buffer read to
inesContainer.ts. On current main the architecture guard allows five
there, so the merged tree failed Static checks. iNES and NES 2.0
declarations and the format probe now read header bytes through one
headerByte helper. The file has one raw read, and its counted baseline
drops from 5 to 1 through --shrink-baselines.

Tests: inesContainer domain tests (24) and the NES boundary and
acceptance tests (76) pass. architecture-guards, format:check and
check:ci:fast pass on the branch merged with main.

* refactor(artifacts): report iNES header failures through ParseFailure

Review follow-up: the NES 2.0 declaration added plain-string failures.
The iNES-family parser now returns Result<_, ParseFailure> with its
kind and where it was found:
- malformed: a missing signature, a dirty legacy header, an empty
  PRG-ROM area, reserved NES 2.0 bits or an invalid file extent;
- truncated: a short header, a short payload, or declared
  miscellaneous ROM with no bytes;
- unsupported: UNIF or another header variant, with undecoded content.
The detail text is unchanged.

The format registry refuses with the detail, and the iNES reader and
root classifier translate the failure at their boundary into the
existing format ArtifactReaderFailure, with the ParseFailureError as
its cause.

Tests: the refusal table now asserts each failure's kind and format
as well as its detail. iNES domain and recognition tests, NES boundary
and acceptance tests (76), architecture-guards, format:check and
check:ci:fast pass on the branch merged with main.

commits.subject: feat(uefi): add pure-TypeScript UEFI firmware analysis tools (#12342)
commits.body:
feat(uefi): add pure-TypeScript UEFI firmware analysis tools (#12342)

* feat(uefi): add pure-TS UEFI firmware volume/FFS parser with inspect/extract tools

Add a dependency-free rea-uefi provider that maps AMI/Aptio flash images:
- inspect_uefi_firmware: aligned _FVH discovery, volume-relative FFS walking,
  guided section/compression classification, conservative PSP-directory probing,
  embedded-volume rescan and leftover-region classification; incremental SHA-256
  and explicit integrity notes.
- extract_uefi_firmware: whole-image/volume/FFS-file/section extraction with
  LZMA-custom/LZMAF86 and AMD-zlib decoding, SafeOutputTree staging, derivations
  and extraction_gaps.
- UefiArtifactReader + 'uefi' format wiring across inventory/domain/contracts
  so parsed volumes and extracted PE32/TE files hand off to deep-provider
  analysis (open_binary -> Ghidra).

* feat(uefi): add inspect_uefi_nvram for AMI NVRAM variable stores

Add a pure-TypeScript tool that maps the vendor AMI NVRAM variable stores
(factory-default "StdDefaults" and peers) inside a flash image:
- scan the raw image for NVAR entry chains ("NVAR" + u16 total size +
  u32 attribute 0x8[23]FFFFFF + state + NUL-terminated name + data),
- recurse into a container entry whose data is itself an NVAR chain, so the
  StdDefaults setup variables surface as depth/parent_offset rows,
- report attributes, state, data range, SHA-256 and trailing padding per entry.

Verified against B550 AORUS Elite V2 FId: one StdDefaults store at 0x37090 with
the 11 expected nested variables (Setup, PlatformLang, AMITSESetup, XhciDID,
GcSensorVarName, PCI_COMMON, SioSetupData, UsbSupport, NetworkStackVar,
SecureBootSetup, Setup). Exposed as MCP tool and inspect-uefi-nvram CLI command.

* fix(uefi): address review on checksums, compression, guided sections, NVRAM bounds

- FFS file checksum: verify the two's-complement invariant (payload sum +
  stored byte == 0 mod 256) instead of comparing sums, and encode the correct
  complement in the fixture builder.
- Compression sections (type 0x01): use the 9-byte header and classify EFI
  standard compression instead of 'none', so extraction reports a gap rather
  than publishing compressed bytes as a raw section.
- GUID-defined sections: derive GUID/data-offset/attributes from the parsed
  common header size (compact or extended) and reject out-of-range payload
  offsets.
- AMI NVRAM: bound recursive chains to the enclosing container's data end and
  report partial coverage when a valid nested chain is cut by max_depth.

* fix(uefi): bound decode memory, serialize operations, enforce deadline, mark truncation

- LZMA worker: enforce max_output_bytes while decoding through a bounded output
  sink, so an oversized stream is rejected during expansion instead of after a
  full decompression plus a second Buffer copy.
- Provider: serialize admitted operations (the promised single decode-worker
  lane must not become one worker per overlapping call) and apply one
  whole-request deadline that covers every decode stage, not a fresh per-stream
  timer. close() drains the queue and the resource scope.
- Scan: track truncated sections of known type and report coverage partial
  instead of complete when a section declares more bytes than are present.

* fix(uefi): cancellable queue, timeout surfacing, availability and reader omissions

- Queue: check the caller signal before enqueue and when a job reaches the head,
  and race the queued promise against abort so a cancelled wait returns
  immediately instead of blocking behind the active request.
- Deadline: track the internal deadline and return AnalysisTimeoutError instead
  of the AnalysisCancelledError that runOwnedCommand reports for any external
  abort, preserving the real failure reason for CLI/MCP callers.
- CapabilityInventory: treat inspect_uefi_nvram like the other bundled rea-uefi
  tools so discovery does not demand Unblob for it.
- UefiArtifactReader: report image truncation through onOmission so inventory
  coverage reflects the unread suffix even when no volume was found.

* fix(uefi): limit early cancellation to unstarted jobs and preserve timeout cleanup

- #raceWithAbort only returns early for jobs that have not started; once a
  request is running, await it so worker cleanup and completed output are
  preserved instead of being discarded by a bare cancellation.
- Reclassify a deadline-induced cancellation as AnalysisTimeoutError while
  keeping its cause and cleanup observations, and never override a different
  primary failure.

* docs(licenses): record UEFI decoder dependency notices

* fix(uefi): preserve stream provenance and bound firmware analysis

* feat(uefi): decode LZMAF86 guided sections

* fix(uefi): validate publication before commit and order decoder cleanup

* fix(uefi): preserve unsupported volumes and extraction gaps

commits.subject: feat(ghidra): admit ELFv2 PPC64 executables through a Power ISA 3.0 lane (#12517)
commits.body:
feat(ghidra): admit ELFv2 PPC64 executables through a Power ISA 3.0 lane (#12517)

* feat(ghidra): admit ELFv2 PPC64 executables through a Power ISA 3.0 lane

An EM_PPC64 ELF has been classified in the powerpc family since #12089, but
the Ghidra lane still refused every ELF64 file. It now admits ELF64 ET_EXEC
files that declare the ELFv2 ABI, little or big endian, and imports them with
PowerPC:LE:64:A2ALT or PowerPC:BE:64:A2ALT by byte order.

Ghidra's 64-bit "default" languages decode the G2-era instruction set and
stop at the first VSX instruction in POWER8 or POWER9 code; the A2ALT
languages are Power ISA 3.0 and decode it. The ELF loader selects A2ALT
today, and the lane passes it explicitly and records it as provider-pinned.

ELFv1 (.opd function descriptors), an undeclared ABI, other e_flags bits,
ET_DYN and ET_REL are refused with their own reasons. The 32-bit lane is
unchanged.

npm run verify:ghidra:ppc64 builds a source-owned ELFv2 fixture in both byte
orders and checks it against GNU readelf and real Ghidra through MCP and the
CLI: the bound language, fixed instruction bytes including a VSX xxlor, the
global-entry thunk to each function's local entry, direct calls, snapshot
identity, and a shared object refused before Ghidra starts.

Refs #12085

* fix(ghidra): supervise PPC64 verifier compiler and CLI processes

Timeouts on bare execFile stop only the direct child, so a linker can
outlive Clang and disappear from the parent-tree cleanup check. Launch
those commands through the shared command owner, pass that runner into
the PPC64 fixture builder, and close the owner before the lineage check.
A failed close stays registered for retry and the diagnostic workspace
is retained.

* docs(ghidra): record the PPC64 ELFv2 Power ISA 3.0 lane

Add the feature specification, plan, and tasks for the lane, and index
them with the other feature records.

* fix(ghidra): finish shared PowerPC verifier command ownership

commits.subject: fix(elf): decode a 32-bit prpsinfo whose ABI gives pr_uid 32 bits (#10189)
commits.body:
fix(elf): decode a 32-bit prpsinfo whose ABI gives pr_uid 32 bits (#10189)

* fix(elf): decode a 32-bit prpsinfo whose ABI gives pr_uid 32 bits

`decodeCorePrpsinfo` assumed every ELFCLASS32 core carries the i386/ARM `struct elf_prpsinfo`:
16-bit `pr_uid`/`pr_gid` and a 124-byte descriptor.

`pr_uid` is `__kernel_uid_t`, and its width is an ABI property, not an ELF-class one. Only
`arch/x86/include/uapi/asm/posix_types_32.h` and its ARM/m68k/sparc counterparts narrow it to
`unsigned short`; everything else takes `asm-generic/posix_types.h`'s `unsigned int`, so MIPS o32,
PowerPC-32, s390 and `compat_elf_prpsinfo` (`include/asm-generic/compat.h`:
`typedef u32 __compat_uid_t`) write a 128-byte struct with every member after `pr_flag` four bytes
later.

Reading a 128-byte descriptor with the 124-byte offsets published wrong values rather than null.
Measured through `parseElfNotes`, with `uid 70000, gid 80000, pid 4242, fname mips-proc`:

    before: {"pid":80000,"ppid":4242,"pgrp":1,"sid":4242,"uid":4464,"gid":1,
             "filename":"\u{10}","psargs":""}
    after:  {"pid":4242,"ppid":1,"pgrp":4242,"sid":4242,"uid":70000,"gid":80000,
             "filename":"mips-proc","psargs":"./mips-proc --serve"}

`pid` came out of the middle of `gid` and the two text fields came from the wrong offsets
entirely.

The kernel writes `sizeof(*psinfo)` as the descriptor — `fs/binfmt_elf.c`:
`fill_note(&info->psinfo, PRPSINFO, sizeof(*psinfo), psinfo)` — so the declared length already
carries the distinction and no machine table is needed. The 32-bit id width is now
`descriptor.length >= 128 ? 4 : 2`, and `pr_pid`/`pr_fname`/`pr_psargs` are derived from it. The
124-byte and 136-byte decodes are unchanged; the second new case pins that.

`src/native/elf` and `src/domain/native` — 535 passing. Forcing the 16-bit layout fails the new case.

* test(elf): produce the 32-bit prpsinfo layout from the shared note builder

Review finding: the regression hand-encoded a second NT_PRPSINFO layout while `corePrpsinfoNote` is
the repository's producer for this format, so nothing else could represent the MIPS/PowerPC/s390
ABI and the two encodings could drift.

`corePrpsinfoNote` takes `idWidth: 2 | 4` now. It allocates 124 or 128 bytes from it, writes
`pr_uid`/`pr_gid` at that width, and derives `pr_pid` through `pr_psargs` from `8 + idWidth * 2`
instead of the fixed 12/28/44 offsets. The option is ignored for a 64-bit image, whose layout is
fixed at 136.

Both new cases build their descriptor through the producer, so the test no longer carries offsets
the fixture does not know about.

* test(elf): drop the duplicate 124-byte prpsinfo case

The previous commit's rewrite left the original hand-built 124-byte block in place, so the same
regression ran twice — once through `corePrpsinfoNote`, once with the offsets written out again.
Keeping both is exactly the drift the shared producer was supposed to end.

* fix(elf): preserve SuperH PRPSINFO decoding

commits.subject: fix(v8): read the code cache header size from the container (#10279)
commits.body:
fix(v8): read the code cache header size from the container (#10279)

* fix(v8): read the code cache header size from the container

V8 sizes the header with `kHeaderSize = POINTER_SIZE_ALIGN(kUnalignedHeaderSize)` and
`kUnalignedHeaderSize` is 28, so the header is padded *after* its words: a 64-bit producer writes
32 header bytes and a 32-bit one writes 28. The reader pinned 32 and required the declared payload
to equal `bytes.length - 32`, so every container from a 32-bit producer failed as "truncated or
corrupt".

Measured here on Node 24.22.1 (V8 in x64): take a real cache and drop the four alignment bytes at
offset 28. V8 loads it unchanged — `cachedDataRejected === false` — while the reader refused it:

    before: Header declares a 392-byte payload but 388 bytes follow the 32-byte header
    after:  ACCEPT header_bytes=28 words=7 payload.offset=28

The payload-length word sits at byte 20 in both layouts, so the declared length already states how
much trailing padding the container carries. The header size is derived from it now: `28` and `32`
are admitted, the reported word table covers exactly the header the container holds (7 or 8 words),
and the schema requires that table to agree with `header_bytes`.

Nothing is loosened. A header that is neither 28 nor 32 bytes is still `malformed`, and the
16 existing cases pass unchanged — dropping only the derivation back to the constant fails exactly
the new narrow-header case.

`src/v8` — 26 passing. `npm run lint` and `tsc --noEmit` clean.

* fix(v8): refuse a wide cache that is only four bytes short

A review finding on the previous commit, and a real one: deriving the header size from the declared
payload length makes a 32-byte-header container truncated by four bytes resolve to 28, because
`bytes.length - declaredPayload` loses exactly those four bytes. The reader then accepted a
truncated cache and read its payload one word long.

The wide header's last word is `POINTER_SIZE_ALIGN` padding that V8 leaves zero, and a narrow
container has payload where that word sits. Measured on Node 24.22.1 across six different sources:
the padding word is always `0x00000000` and the first payload word is always non-zero. So the zero
word is the only evidence that separates the two, and it is now required to be non-zero for the
28-byte layout:

| container | before this commit | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| real 32-byte header | accept | accept, `header_bytes=32` |
| real 28-byte header | accept | accept, `header_bytes=28` |
| 32-byte header truncated by 4 | **accept** | refused as `malformed` |

The guide also described one pinned 32-byte header; it now describes both layouts, how the size is
resolved, and why an ambiguous container is refused.

`src/v8` — 27 passing. Removing the guard accepts the truncated container again.

* fix(v8): read the padding word through the header accessor

A Static checks finding: `verify/architecture-guards.mjs` counts raw Buffer reads in parser folders
and allows only a shrinking baseline, and the previous commit added one:

```
raw Buffer or DataView numeric read (use BinaryReader ...); new copies are not allowed:
  src/v8/V8CodeCacheParser.ts: 2 (baseline 1)
```

The read is the narrow-header discriminator — the alignment word a 64-bit producer leaves zero at
offset 28. It now goes through the file's existing `field(index)` accessor instead of calling
`bytes.readUInt32LE` directly, so the count returns to the baseline while the check itself is
unchanged: `field(7)` is byte 28, and `V8_CODE_CACHE_NARROW_HEADER_BYTES / 4` spells that index.

`node scripts/verify/architecture-guards.mjs` — passed across 2 843 source files.
`src/v8` + `tests/boundary/rust` — 68 passing. `tsc --noEmit` 0 errors.
Setting the condition to `false` fails "refuses a wide container that is only four bytes short",
so the check is still load-bearing.

* fix(v8): ground the narrow-header rule in the producer, and test the word table

Two review findings.

**The rule was stated as measurement, not as format.** The previous comment justified the zero-word
discriminator with "measured on Node 24.22.1 every real payload begins with a non-zero word", which
makes support for other producers depend on one host. The producer zeroes that padding rather than
copying payload over it: `SerializedData::AllocateWithPayload` in `src/snapshot/snapshot-data.cc`
runs `std::fill_n(data_, header_size, 0)` before writing any header word, and
`kHeaderSize = POINTER_SIZE_ALIGN(kUnalignedHeaderSize)` in `src/snapshot/code-serializer.h` puts the
four padding bytes inside `header_size`. So a zero word at byte 28 is a fact about the producer, not
about one Node build.

The refusal is now worded as the reservation it is: a narrow container whose payload happened to
begin with four zero bytes would match the same test, and no reading of the header alone separates
the two cases. The message says both readings instead of asserting corruption.

**The word-table rule had no test that could fail.** `header.fields.length * 4 === header.header_bytes`
cannot disagree on a parsed container — the parser derives both from `payloadOffset` — so it is only
reachable through the schema, which is what a stored or projected report also goes through. The new
case builds four reports directly: seven words with 32 bytes and eight words with 28 are refused on
`header.fields`, while the two consistent pairs are accepted. Setting the rule to `false` fails it
with `7 words / 32 bytes: expected true to be false`.

`node scripts/verify/architecture-guards.mjs` — passed across 2 843 source files.
`src/v8` + `tests/boundary/rust` — 69 passing. `tsc --noEmit` 0 errors, `npm run lint` 0 errors.

* refactor(v8): share decoded code cache header words

* fix(v8): validate narrow header evidence without assuming runtime compatibility

commits.subject: perf(javascript): allocate nested evaluation contexts with fixed shapes (#9007)
commits.body:
perf(javascript): allocate nested evaluation contexts with fixed shapes (#9007)

nestedContext builds one EvaluationContext per recursive expression step. A conditional object spread forces V8 through the generic property-copy path even when the spread adds no fields, and prevents a stable shape. It was the top self-time frame (25.4%) in a profile of semantic indexing.

Use two explicit object literals selected by capturePoint, keeping the same field set, order, values and optionality. Completed analyses are byte-identical across 12 representative sources (36 IR/facts/coverage digests), and member-mutation indexing is 1.47-1.65x faster on the profiled alias-chain workload.

Co-authored-by: Zhenyang Han <mshzy@users.noreply.github.com>
